title.narrative: Protection, Assistance and Solutions for Forcibly Displaced Populations in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative: This action aims to contribute to alleviating protracted forced displacement in Sub-Saharan Africa by:1.To improve the access of forcibly displaced populations, in particular women, persons with disabilities and children, and host/resident communities to effective basic services, accessible housing and economic inclusion2.To enhance the provision of urban and rural green and climate resilient durable solutions (voluntary return, local integration, resettlement) by host/resident communities and countries to forcibly displaced populations, in particular women, persons with disabilities and children3.To promote national and regional policy dialogue and commitments in favour of displaced population, in particular women, persons with disabilities and children, by strengthening policy, legal and regulatory frameworks and via the IGAD Support PlatformThis action tackle the following forced displacement situations: i) Sudanese crisis: Chad and South Sudan; ii) Central Sahel: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger; iii) protracted situations: IGAD Support Platform, Sudan and South Sudan Solutions Initiative, CAR refugees in Cameroon and CAR refugee returnees, and refugees in Uganda; iv) Emergency Transit Mechanism (ETM) in Rwanda; and v) IDPs in Somalia.

title.narrative: PROGIRESS : Projet de Gestion intégrée des Ressources en Eau de Surface et Souterraines dans les bassins du fleuve Sénégal et de l¿aquifère Sénégalo-Mauritanien

description.narrative: L¿action vise à renforcer la résilience aux changements climatiques des systèmes des eaux de surface (Bassin du Fleuve Sénégal ou BFS) et des eaux souterraines (Bassin Aquifère Sénégalo-Mauritanien ou BASM) à travers l¿amélioration de la gestion durable des ressources en eau et des écosystèmes dans les deux bassins. Elle répond à l¿attention grandissante des populations par rapport aux problématiques de dégradation environnementale (salinisation des terres, érosion des sols, perte de couvert végétal, plantes invasives) et de réduction de la qualité et de la disponibilité de la ressource en eau, problématiques qui contribuent à renforcer le processus de désertification, affectent la production agricole et énergétique et nuisent au développement socio-économique durable des zones ciblées.L¿action s¿inscrit dans le cadre de l¿Initiative Equipe Europe pour la gestion des eaux transfrontalières en Afrique portée par les institutions européennes et huit Etats membres afin de soutenir le développement et l¿intégration régionale à travers le continent. Elle renforce le rôle de leader de l¿Equipe Europe sur la gestion des eaux transfrontalières et de leurs bassins versants en Afrique et en particulier dans la région ciblée.L¿action s¿inscrit dans la stratégie de la Commission européenne « Global Gateway », en investissant sur des activités d¿adaptation et de résilience face au changement climatique, en promouvant la consolidation de la paix et de la bonne gouvernance et en soutenant la connaissance et le montage de projets pour permettre la réalisation d¿investissements transfrontaliers d¿envergure au service du bien commun.Les résultats indiqués et les activités qui sont prévues constituent des priorités déjà identifiées par les organismes de bassin responsables de la gestion des ressources en eau dans les deux bassins, à savoir l¿Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS) et l¿Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Gambie (OMVG). Au niveau des pays des bassins ciblés par l¿action (Gambie, Guinée, Guinée Bissau, Mali, Mauritanie et Sénégal), l¿action est également alignée avec les politiques sectorielles nationales et complémentaires des projets et programmes actuellement mis en ¿uvre. Sur le plan régional, l¿action est en particulier complémentaire de l¿Initiative Blue Peace Bonds (FEDD+) au bénéfice de l¿OMVG et du projet NaturAfrica mené dans le Parc national du Niokolo-Koba, affluent du fleuve Gambie.L¿action contribue à l¿atteinte des ODD 6 (eau potable et assainissement), 5 (égalité entre les sexes), 8 (travail décent et croissance économique), 10 (réduire les inégalités), 12 (consommation et production responsable), 13 (lutte contre les changements climatiques) et 15 (vie terrestre). L¿objectif général de cette action est l¿amélioration de la résilience aux changements climatiques des systèmes des eaux de surface dans le bassin du fleuve Sénégal (BFS) et des eaux souterraines dans le bassin aquifère Sénégalo-Mauritanien (BASM). Les objectifs spécifiques de cette action sont : 1.La gestion durable des ressources en eau de surface et souterraines est renforcée2.L¿état des ressources naturelles et de la biodiversité est amélioré3.La coopération dans le domaine de la gestion de l¿eau est renforcée

title.narrative: La réintégration des ex-combattants et l¿autonomisation des femmes : remparts communautaires à l'extrémisme violent en Afrique (REMPARTS)

description.narrative: Le programme a l¿objectif général de contribuer de manière inclusive à la lutte contre le terrorisme et l¿extrémisme violent en Afrique Centrale et de l¿Ouest, avec une attention particulière sur le rôle des femmes. Cet objectif général commun est basé sur l¿importance de se focaliser sur les causes profondes de l'extrémisme violent et autonomiser les groupes vulnérables, qui comprennent les femmes mais aussi les individus stigmatisés tels que les anciens associés des groupes terroristes. L¿Action s'aligne sur le domaine prioritaire 2 (Gouvernance démocratique, paix et sécurité, et culture), Objectif spécifique 2 (Paix et sécurité) du Programme indicatif pluriannuel pour l'Afrique subsaharienne 2021-2027. Les marqueurs CAD/internes (objectifs politiques) pertinents pour cette action sont la promotion de la « Gouvernance démocratique et inclusive (GDI) » et de l¿ « Égalité des genres ». Cette action contribuera directement aux ODD 16 - Paix, justice et institutions efficaces, 5 - Égalité des sexes, 8 - Travail décent et croissance économique et 10 Inégalités réduites.Dans la fenêtre du bassin du lac Tchad, que couvre les zones transfrontalières et limitrophes entre le Cameroun, le Nigeria, le Niger et le Tchad, l¿Action soutien la réintégration des ex-associes et ex-combattants de Boko Haram, tout en améliorant les conditions socio-économiques des communautés hôtes et renforçant la contribution des femmes, de la société civile et des autorités locales et traditionnelles à la lutte contre l¿extrémisme violent et aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG). L¿Action ciblant la fenêtre Afrique de l¿Ouest se focalise sur l¿analyse des vulnérabilités spécifiques des femmes face aux groupes extrémistes et sur le renforcement de leur rôle comme facilitatrices dans les processus de paix et de lutte contre l¿extrémisme violent dans la zone transfrontalière entre le Burkina Faso, le Ghana et la Côte d¿Ivoire. En particulier, l¿action vise à : renforcer la compréhension du rôle des femmes dans les groupes extrémistes ainsi que les obstacles à leur participation à la prévention de l¿extrémisme violent ; renforcer le rôle des groupes de femmes et des communautés locales dans la lutte contre l¿extrémisme violent ; et renforcer les capacités des autorités locales, administratives, religieuses et coutumières pour stimuler la participation des femmes aux processus décisionnels locaux.

title.narrative: Countering Illicit Trafficking and Transnational Organized Crime in Africa (CITOC)

description.narrative: The Action aims to strengthen Africa's resilience to transnational security threats by enhancing the capacities of African countries to prevent, protect against, and combat illicit trafficking and transnational organised crime (TOC). It is structured around a main component focused on combating illicit trafficking along major trade and transport land corridors, supported by two additional components that specifically address the trafficking in substandard and falsified medical products and cybercrime respectively. Primarily focused on West African countries, the Action¿s scope extends to several countries in Central, East and Southern Africa. By concentrating on critical socio-economic sectors ¿ transport, health, and digital-related ¿ that show particular vulnerability to organised crime, it contributes to the 360-degree approach of the EU Global Gateway Strategy and advances EU-Africa partnership¿s goals of peace, security, and prosperity.The Specific Objectives [components] of this Action are to:1.Contribute to the reduction of illicit trade and other forms of organised crime and trafficking along major trade and transport land corridors in West Africa costal countries and Cameroon.2. Strengthen the capacity to prevent, detect and respond to the trafficking of medical products across West, East and Southern Africa countries, with a focus on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products (SFMP).3.Enhance the capacity to effectively tackle online fraud and cybercrime in West and Central Africa.Component 1: Trafficking corridors. Major trade and transport corridors often intersect with trafficking routes and hubs. New investments improving connectedness of markets and territories are likely to exacerbate opportunities for criminal exploitation. These risks are especially acute in environments where governance and regulatory capacities are weak. In West Africa, road networks also play a critical role in the operations of armed groups, serving as both a revenue source and a means to exert control over local populations. To address these challenges, the Action will strengthen the capabilities of frontline actors in countering illicit trafficking along the established Global Gateway Trade and Transport Corridors through a mix of local and cross-border activities across coastal West African countries and Cameroon. It will enhance law enforcement capabilities through innovative, locally-designed pilot initiatives; encourage harmonised regional control measures and cross-border cooperation through joint operations and intelligence sharing. The focus will be on land corridors, which are often under-prioritized compared to air and maritime routes, despite accounting for 80% of goods transport and 90% of people movement on the continent.Component 2: Trafficking in Substandard and Falsified Medical Products (SFMP). In Sub-Saharan Africa, SFMP account for 30% of medical products in circulation, and up to 55% in West Africa, leading to thousands of deaths annually. The illicit trafficking of pharmaceuticals is not only deadly and lucrative (estimated 10 to 25 times more profitable than drug trafficking) but also serves as a privileged avenue for laundering illicit proceeds and funding illegal activities. Joining EU efforts to combat the trafficking of pharmaceutical and medical products will contribute to both public health and security outcomes, while supporting the EU Global Gateway Health Strategy and complementing the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines, and health technologies in Africa (MAV+) efforts. title.narrative: Zones frontalières pacifiques et résilientes IV

description.narrative: Les zones frontalières d¿Afrique subsaharienne sont fréquemment caractérisées par des mouvements de population, de bétail, de marchandises, et de ressources naturelles. Ces zones, lorsqu'elles sont associées à l'insécurité, aux conflits, aux impacts du changement climatique, à la pauvreté ou à un abandon par rapport à l'État central, peuvent progressivement se muer en foyers d'instabilité. Ceci est notamment le cas des territoires riverains de la frontière entre le Mali et la Mauritanie, où l¿escalade des violences perpétrées par les groupes armés non étatiques au Mali a causé un nouvel afflux d¿arrivants maliens et de retournés mauritaniens. Dans la sous-région des Grands lacs, les tensions dans les zones frontalières sont souvent exacerbées par le développement des groupes armés, les difficultés d¿accès aux services sociaux de base, l¿absence de dialogue politique et le faible progrès économique et développement global de la population. La guerre civile au Soudan et l¿afflux de personnes déplacées au Sud Soudan ont contribué à aggraver les tensions dans la zone frontalière déjà en proie de récurrents conflits inter et intra-ethniques violents, potentiel pôle de déstabilisation pour les deux pays.Cette action vise à prévenir et atténuer l¿impact des conflits locaux en améliorant la résilience et la cohésion sociale des communautés transfrontalières. Pour ce faire, une approche intégrée à la sécurité sera appliquée, en promouvant la coopération transfrontalière en tant que levier de paix. description.narrative: Study and Research in Africa aims to increase the attractiveness of African higher education offer for all types of mobile learners within Africa and to Africa. It seeks to strengthen regional integration, knowledge networks, cooperation, branding of EU-funded programmes in African Higher Education and in particular support the effective creation of the African Higher Education and Research Space (AHERS). The programme will also support the capacity building of universities/ and their affiliated research centres (RCs)[1] to interact with the wider eco-system (i.e., public and private organizations and institutions, development finance institutions, civil society organizations, etc.) in Global Gateway (GG) investment priority areas such as digital, climate, energy, transport, health, and applied research so that they play a stronger role in the skills development and innovation of value chains and build up a more relevant training offer. It will build scale, connect initiatives, and increase the relevance of projects funded through EU, as well as MS programmes and will offer an enabling facility to build up multilayer partnerships at the country level, increasing the chances of countries to access EFSD+. In the medium term, the Action will support the attractiveness of African Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) by creating a platform to disseminate information, advancing the wider ecosystem of HEIs in Africa and by supporting HEIs access to EU funds.Contributing towards the external dimension of the European Education Area¿s European Universities Strategy, the action will be structured around three components covering Opportunities, Partnerships and Targeted Support, all contributing to a transformational impact of Team Europe efforts in Africa in the field of higher education.The action is part of the Youth Mobility for Africa GG flagship initiative, which brings together several EU programmes in higher education and youth, such as Erasmus+, the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme and the Africa-EU Youth Academy under one umbrella. Supporting continental integration, providing learning opportunities both within Africa, and between Africa and Europe and reinforcing cooperation to leverage investment in knowledge and innovation to support strategic autonomy and sustainable value chains, build scale and enhance African higher education¿s relevance and responsiveness to labour market needs in partner countries, while also creating green growth, are core elements of the GG Africa-Europe Investment Package and are the aims of the Youth Mobility for Africa GG Flagship Initiative.Concretely, the Action will focus on three specific objectives/components:1.Opportunities: Support African HEIs to be more visible and accessible, strengthen their profile, branding and disseminate targeted information, attract mobile learners, researchers and staff and sharing of data and information.HEIs will be supported in positioning themselves in fields in which they excel, and which can also highlight the linkages with EU investments at country or regional level. This positioning will help mobile learners, researchers and staff make informed decisions about their choice of studies, work and location and build up the internationalisation and marketing of countries offer. description.narrative: The Action aims to enable agribusinesses, MSMEs, farmer groups, and farmers to maintain and improve access to domestic, regional and EU market, benefitting from the AfCFTA commitments, EPAs and other preferential trade arrangements with the EU (main focus on fruit and vegetables, but open to other agri-food value chains). The Action will increase the resilience, fairness (inclusiveness), competitiveness and sustainability of a selected number of agricultural value chains, through the development and adoption of safe and sustainable practices, skills and technologies, as well as boosting equal access to finance and investments, which in turn are expected to contribute to decent job creation and the sustainable and inclusive transformation of the agri-food sector in the target countries. Skilled and resilient agri-food operators from both private and public sectors are key in order to promote inclusive, sustainable, low carbon and (climate) resilient agricultural value chains. In this context, the action will focus on two mutually reinforcing components: 1) Continental facility; 2) Country facility.Component 1 (continental facility ¿ Sustainable horticulture in SSA) Important challenges and bottlenecks are impairing the competitiveness of the horticultural sector in Africa. The enabling environment struggles to effectively support the private sector by providing adequate and cost-effective services such as extension, regulation, certification, logistics and in general enabling a predictable and stable business environment.This component seeks to strengthen national horticultural production and distribution systems across SSA countries. This means supporting agri-food MSMEs (including farmer groups and cooperatives), local services providers in the horticultural sector and the national competent authorities, to strengthen their capabilities and support a strong African horticultural sector. By improving access to domestic, regional and international markets for fruit and vegetable value chains, as well as access to finance and investment, this component will create an operational and enabling platform that contributes to the overall transformation of food systems in SSA within a sustainable framework. Component 1 will also seek the development of partnerships with African educational institutions to develop massive open vocational capacity building. Component 2 (Selected country-agrifood value chain facility)The European Union continues to be a highly appealing market for African agricultural goods, while intra-continental exchanges are also gaining importance. Agri-food exports from SSA economies to the EU are of pivotal importance in terms of generating income and employment, and key contributors towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Nonetheless, meeting evolving EU Regulations and Standards remains a major and challenging determinant for market access, as well as competitiveness. The EU has built a strategic approach in support of intra-African and EU-Africa investment and trade by anchoring its support on key priority areas (i.e. trade in goods, services, trade facilitation, competition, digital trade) of free trade and investment agreements at continental, regional and national levels (AfCFTA, RECs, EU Bilateral and Regional - EPAs), as well as key value chains, and trade corridors.To complement this support, this Action will focus on four additional key enablers of EU-Africa and intra-Africa sustainable trade and investment that will be concretely implemented through four different projects, some of which are a continuation of existing support, namely:1. Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) protection and enforcement are key for investment and innovation facilitation and protection. Support will contribute to the harmonisation, creation, registration, management, utilisation and administration, protection, and enforcement of IPRs in Africa. To this end, the Action will focus on continental, regional and national: (i) African IP legal and policy frameworks (i.e. AfCFTA IP Protocol, the Continental Strategy for Geographical Indications (GIs) of the African Union, Regional and national IP regulations, etc.); (ii) African IP administration capacities; (iii) African and EU productive sector support, with a particular focus on SMEs (i.e. the Africa IP SME Helpdesk); and (iv) Support to the elaboration and implementation of the post 2023 Continental Strategy for GIs of the African Union.2. EU-Africa Trade and Investment Agreements, with the main objective to boost sustainable EU ¿ Africa trade and investment flows and strengthen the trade and investment capacities of African partners through the design of a flexible on-demand facility that can offer ad-hoc support to countries with whom the EU has concluded trade and investment agreements (EPAs, SIFAs, etc.). This facility will also provide complementary technical support needed for alignment with EU regulations and directives having an impact on EU-Africa trade and investment, such as the relevant policies adopted in the framework of the European Green Deal and the EU Circular Economy Action Plan or the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D).3. Customs Cooperation, a main enabler at the basis of all trade. The Action proposes a follow up to the existing successful programmes `Harmonizing the classification of goods based on WCO standards to enhance African trade¿ (EU-WCO Harmonised System (HS) Programme, 2018-2024) and `Implementation and application of Rules of Origin (RoO)¿ (EU-WCO RoO Programme, 2021-2025). The scope of the new programme is to enhance African trade by further developing and implementing key customs pillars of the AfCFTA and of other regional agreements through dedicated technical capacity support to (i) Harmonised System (HS), (ii) Rules of Origin (RoO), and (iii) Valuation. 4. Investment Facilitation, a crucial soft enabler to accompany Global Gateway hard investments, ensuring that they are conducive to sustainable and inclusive development. title.narrative: Support to the African Governance, Peace & Security Architectures

description.narrative: This Action seeks to contribute to the above joint principles as well as the African Union¿s (AU) Agenda 2063 and the ¿Silencing the Guns¿ flagship initiative (2020-2030). The latter¿s objective is to end all wars, civil conflicts, gender-based violence and violent conflicts, and prevent genocide by supporting: i) the APSA as the main framework for promoting peace, security and stability in Africa, and ii) the AGA in responding to the AU vision to promote and protect human and people¿s rights, consolidate democratic institutions, good governance and the rule of law on the continent. In addition, the Action further contributes to SDG 5: Gender Equality; SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions; and SDG 17: Partnership for the Goals. Specifically, this Action will support the African Governance Architecture (AGA) and African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA) to help prevent conflict and enhance participatory democratic governance across the African continent. This will be done by engaging with the AU Commission (AUC) and its continental organs, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and AU Member States (AUMS) at political, policy and operational levels. It represents a more focused support to the AU Governance, Peace and Security (GPS) Architectures, while continuing the EU¿s political commitment to the continent in the spirit of shared African-European priorities.Indeed, this Action proposes to gather formerly separate support programmes to APSA (peace and security) and AGA (governance)[1] under one conceptual roof by building on lesson learnt and wider consultations with the AU at various levels. With a planned budget of EUR 40 million over four years managed by the EUD to the AU, it will address key thematic issues of mutual interest and reinforce the GPS nexus. The Action responds to ongoing major AU reforms, notably i) the effective transformation of the Political Affairs, Peace, and Security Department (AU-PAPS) towards more integrated approaches to conflicts and their political root causes by addressing the Governance, Peace and Security (GPS) nexus; ii) the operationalisation of the AU Peace Fund; and iii) the rationalisation of the AU treaty-based human rights organs. Engagement with Pan-African civil society networks (CSOs), think tanks and academia is mainstreamed to build on positive results of previous programmes. To ensure the sustainability of GPS efforts, the need to engage with youth and women is widely recognised as instrumental to maximising the demographic dividend.

description.narrative: The Social Protection Systems Strengthening Action in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is aimed at building inclusive, resilient, and sustainable social protection (SP) systems. This action supports the EU¿s Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for SSA under Priority Area 1: Human Development, focusing on reducing poverty, promoting gender equality, ensuring decent work, and advancing social inclusion. The action aligns with key African Union (AU) frameworks, including Agenda 2063, which underscores social protection as a critical component of economic stability and integration. It also supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1, No Poverty, Target 1.3.SSA¿s social protection systems face numerous structural challenges. With fewer than 20% of people in the region covered by any form of social protection, factors such as high levels of informality, limited fiscal resources, administrative capacity, inadequate benefit levels and fragmented policies contribute to substantial coverage gaps. These limitations, combined with pressures from recurring crises¿including the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change impacts, migration, economic instability and fragility contexts¿necessitate social protection systems that are adaptable, responsive, and accessible to vulnerable populations. Inadequate SP coverage leaves marginalized groups without necessary support systems, deepening poverty and widening social inequalities.A regional approach to SP across SSA offers substantial added value, fostering alignment of policy standards, enabling cross-border crisis-responsive measures, promoting portability of rights while facilitating exchange of experiences across countries. A regional approach can reduce disparities that lead to migration pressures and economic inequality while enhancing countries¿ abilities to respond cohesively to regional crises. The coordinated framework facilitates the exchange of best practices and collaborative learning among SSA countries. Collaboration at the regional level is also integral to achieving the ambitions of Agenda 2063, which emphasizes social protection as fundamental for economic integration, social cohesion, and sustainable development.This action has a clear results chain aimed at achieving the overall impact through specific objectives and outputs.The overall objective is to support and strengthen national social protection systems in SSA by leveraging a region-to-region approach. The ultimate aim is to enhance resilience, reduce poverty, and promote equitable economic growth aligned with the sustainable development agenda.The specific objectives are:Support Social Protection System Strengthening: This objective focuses on building SSA countries¿ capacity to design and implement robust, inclusive SP systems. Capacity building and regional knowledge-sharing initiatives will improve social protection governance, sustainable financing, and integrated policy frameworks for inclusive and shock-responsive social protection systems in participating countries.<span style="color: rgb(13, 13

title.narrative: Supporting Clean Cooking Solutions in Central and East Africa

description.narrative: The clean cooking sector is gaining traction in some countries of East and Central Africa, but it remains fragmented and underfunded. The dominating use of low-efficiency biomass cooking solutions comes with major negative environmental, socio-economic, health and gender impacts. Significant additional financing and policy efforts in the region are required to reach universal access to clean cooking by 2030.The Action intends to contribute to increasing and accelerating the access to affordable, clean and sustainable cooking solutions (high-tier cooking solutions) in East and Central Africa. The Action will foster clean cooking business development with coaching, financial partnership brokering (finance catalyst) and innovative financial solutions for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) including manufacturers, distributors and importers of clean cooking solutions. More particularly, it will offer results-based-finance and thematic grants to support and accelerate market development and innovation. It will also expand the portfolio of finance institutions to clean cooking through training, sector-specific tools and de-risking mechanisms, like guarantees and credit lines where blending will be possible. It will strengthen the regulatory and market framework by supporting regional dialogue and coordination of policies and plans through platforms, networks of task forces, and by promoting regional performance standards and reduced tariffs barriers, contributing to stronger clean cooking strategies and facilitated international trade of clean cooking solutions. The Action is fully aligned with regional and national policies and strategies. It will build on on-going activities, more particularly, Europe (EU) and EU Member States¿ funded programmes in the region. It is intended to improve, adapt and replicate successful approaches, to selected countries for a possible future extension at full regional scale. This Action will contribute to the regional priority area 3 of the MIP ¿Green Transition¿ and to its specific objective 2 ¿Support the development of an efficient, sustainable and resilient African energy sector¿. The action will also actively contribute to the pledge of the Clean Cooking Declaration of Paris (2024) to make clean cooking a priority and enhance the efforts toward achieving universal access for all.The action will contribute to affordable and clean energy access for cooking (SDG7), climate mitigation (SDG13), forest conservation (SDG15), gender equality, including in entrepreneurship (SDG5), health, more particularly of women and girls (SDG3), and sustainable cities (SDG11).

description.narrative: This action aligns with the Multi-Annual Financing Framework 2021-2027 and will continue crucial EU support for the UHC-Partnership with the World Health Organization (WHO) starting in 2025. Launched in 2011, the programme is currently active in more than 120 countries across Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, Asia, and Europe, with participation from EU Member States such as Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, and Luxembourg, as well as the United Kingdom, Canada, and Japan. The action aims to support the implementation of WHO¿s 14th General Programme of Work (2025-2028) in partner countries, enhancing efforts to build resilient health systems and achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Youth Engagment Hub (YEH)

description.narrative: The Youth Engagement Hub (YEH) aims at facilitating the integration of youth perspective in policy development and implementation and youth-led initiatives at country level, leveraging young people¿s insights, innovation capacity, and building trustful relationships. Complementing already ongoing initiatives such as the Women and Youth in Democratic Engagement, the Youth Empowerment Fund and national level actions by EU Delegations, the action will support the implementation of the Youth Action Plan in EU external action for 2022-2027 in the roll out of the Global Gateway strategy. It will also contribute to the commitments in the European Commission President¿s Political Guidelines 2024-2029 by ensuring intergenerational fairness and making ¿sure that young people can use their voice ¿ their own voice ¿ to help shape our future¿.The action responds to the demands of young people to be engaged in policy-making and contribute to the EU priorities and provides support to EU Delegation to strengthen their institutional youth engagement by implementing initiatives developed with the advice of their Youth Sounding Boards. The action also responds to the needs of the EU, including the European Commission and EU Delegations, to further embed youth engagment in the EU policy processes and the Global Gateway priorities. The YEH will connect young people¿s needs and interests with Global Gateway priorities at country level. With the objective to strengthen the partnership between the EU and young people through enhanced youth engagement with a focus on policy development, the action will aim at:Increasing institutional youth engagement in policy development and implementation, in particular to advance the roll out of the Global Gateway strategy in line with the Youth Action Plan and EUDs priorities.Supporting youth-led initiatives, inlcuding those developed with the advice of Youth Sounding Boards.Building on the principle of partnership, the action will allow for strong(er) cooperation between EU Delegations, Youth Sounding Boards and young people as well as promoting broader inclusion of young people and the participation of EU MSs, the private sector, partner countries and other interested stakeholders. The action will strengthen capacity-building around youth participation and empowerment of all involved actors and strengthen the youth relevance of EU actions across Global Gateway priorities.The action supports the contribution of young generations as key agents for the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals, to promoting stronger, peaceful, democratic and inclusive societies for sustainable development and building effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels (SDG 16 ¿Peace, justice and strong institutions¿). It contributes to the EU commitments to support the broad implementation of the United Nations SDGs (4 ¿Quality Education¿, 5 ¿Gender Equality¿, 8 ¿Decent Work and Economic Growth¿, 10 ¿Reduce inequalities¿, 11 ¿Sustainable cities and Communities¿, 13 ¿Climate Action¿, 17 ¿Partnerships¿ etc.) and the UN Youth, Peace and Security Agenda.

title.narrative: Evidence for migration and forced displacement management

description.narrative: Forced displacement is dramatically increasing every year, from some 40 million in 2012 to 120 million reported in June 2024. While new crises create new displacements, many displacement crises remain, further exacerbated by environmental and climate impacts, and most refugee contexts have become protracted. In parallel, the increasing mixed movements of forcibly displaced, stateless people, and migrants pose significant, multifaceted challenges for governments, the people themselves and communities in countries of origin, asylum, transit, and destination. To address these challenges, the collection of data is key to understand the needs of the displaced and the migrants in vulnerable situations, as well as the needs of the host communities. Without investment in these areas and ensuring timely and accurate data about the actual situation, protection challenges and opportunities faced by refugees, stateless persons, migrants in vulnerable situations, and host communities, the responses by States and other actors risk being dictated and shaped by immediate political imperatives and are more likely to be manipulated and misinformed, thus reducing the capacity to uphold rights and better protection of people on the move, provide alternatives to dangerous journeys, or effective management of asylum and migration systems. Lack of reliable evidence on the actual situation of migrants and refugees may also facilitate the growth of misperceptions in the public opinion of the host countries leading their authorities to promote restrictive migration and asylum policies and practices. It can also fuel anti-migrant and anti-refugee rhetorics in some contexts.To establish this more effective data and evidence system, it is necessary to improve coordination and interoperability of the diverse data systems. Stakeholders will work together in view of eliminating discrepancies and inconsistencies in data production, data sharing and analysis, with the aim to gain efficiencies in the understanding of the situation of migration and forced displacement. The increased knowledge of the persons to be targeted, deriving from the better collection and combination of the information delivered by the different stakeholders, would also allow a better and more timely targeting and prioritization of the assistance. Against this background, the Action will specifically contribute to improving data quality on the needs of forcibly displaced, stateless populations, migrants in vulnerable situations and their host communities, through two components. The first component will focus on enhancing the production, analysis and availability of the data and statistics related to forcibly displaced people, stateless populations and host communities, and facilitating their use for decision making, while ensuring the right to privacy and data protection. The second component will aim to strengthen the partnership and collaboration between UN organisations and key states of origin, transit and destination to set up an interoperable system on data collection and analysis of mixed movements of refugees and migrants, notably on the Central Mediterranean and Western Mediterranean/Atlantic routes, in the context of the delivery of their route-based approach. Both components will be implemented in indirect management with entrusted pillar-assessed entities. The action will contribute to the MIP Global Challenges Partnerships Pillar, and its specific objective 1 ¿enhanced global and multilateral partnerships¿. By further strengthening our partnership with the multilateral fora, and investing in our knowledge base in both qualitative and quantitative data, while also strengthening coordination and interoperability, the action will contribute to the expected results 1, 2 and 4. title.narrative: Activity under preparation Strengthened Local Authorities and their associations

description.narrative: Local Authorities (LAs) are important partners of the EU in the context of its development policy. NDICI-Global Europe has recognized them as key actors in advancing territorial approaches to local development and fostering local democracy. The action aims at the recognition of LAs as development actors per se and the establishment of an enabling environment for LAs that will allow them to deliver on their mandate and, in fine, improve the living conditions of their constituencies.The main activity of this action consists in the continuation of our engagement with i) global Associations of Local Authorities (ALAs) which have signed a framework partnership agreement with the EU in 2022, and ii) EU delegations to enhance their work with LAs. Direct support to sub-national authorities may also be considered in specific contexts.ALAs will thus continue their work to improve LAs¿ capacities for dialogue at local, national, regional and global levels and EU delegations will be in a better position to enter into a constructive dialogue and support LAs and their associations in their respective countries. In addition, ALAs and EU delegations will reinforce LAs in sustainably delivering resilient services to their constituencies and facilitate their access to development finance. Grants will be awarded to global and regional ALAs and, potentially, to sub-national authorities to achieve the objectives above. The action may delegate funds to EU delegations in order for them to give grant to sub-national authorities. A service contract will be contracted to pursue the Territorial Approach to Local Development (TALD) facility¿s support to EU delegations to strengthen their work with LAs and their associations.

description.narrative: In line with the external dimension of the EU Green Deal, the EU Energy & Climate Diplomacy, the transport sector in its railway and maritime sub-sectors is at a critical juncture with the potential to play a significant role in global decarbonisation efforts. The EU external action on transport has become more strategic and geopolitical, and the relation with and support to EU companies has become a key priority. EU values and its regulatory framework contribution towards rail and maritime global sectors sustainability is key to also to find entry points supporting EU industry competitivity. This action will complement EU¿s support to international organisations such as the International Maritime Organization (IMO) activities involving several countries sharing EU values also looking for further support to EU¿s efforts on the regulatory front. In a similar manner, it will promote through entities such as the European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) the EU¿s rail regulatory framework in the African context.  This action aims at completing INTPA¿s toolbox in preparation to scale up the Global Gateway in the next MFF, and includes two main specific objectives: (i) to support partner countries in improving the investment climate and regulatory frameworks to contribute to unlocking investment, (ii) to promote and transpose to partner countries EU values, standards, knowledge, and best practices on sustainable transport, including just and better working conditions for women building the necessary human resources capacity. Three outcomes are expected: (a) specific support to the rail sector in sub-Saharan Africa, (b) on the maritime sector, cooperation with international organisations such as IMO for port governance and green and digital investments preparation (including single window), specifically in sub-Saharan Africa, and (c) support globally on maritime transport-related gender issues.  The African maritime and port governance components, as well as the project on African rail, are key to the continent's efforts in maritime and rail decarbonisation and promoting greener, safer, and more socially responsible transportation. The actions include capacity building aiming to develop advanced training capacity for a new generation of seafarers proficient in decarbonised and digital shipping operations. Additionally, this action will contribute to combating violence and harassment in the maritime industry, with the goal of fostering a culture of zero tolerance and strengthening regulatory frameworks, in line with EU commitments to promote decent, safe, and fair employment, and improve workplace safety and culture at sea. the EU's perspective, supporting these actions is crucial as it aligns with the EU's own goals of reducing emissions, promoting sustainable transportation, and ensuring safe and fair working conditions, and demonstrates the EU's commitment to cooperation and partnership with African countries in achieving these shared objectives, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable and equitable global maritime industry. The proposed maritime and railway components contribute to the NDICI-Global Europe `Global Challenges¿ Priority area on Prosperity, directly addressing climate change mitigation through GHG emission reduction in international maritime shipping, maritime and port governance, the green transition and promoting zero tolerance

title.narrative: Activity under preparation The Green Coupon Subsidy Facility

description.narrative: The Global Green Bond Initiative (GGBI) sets out a comprehensive, three-pillar approach to accelerate the flow of green finance to low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), with the goal of unlocking EU investor¿s capital participation in sustainable development projects. By addressing barriers on both the supply and demand sides of the green bond market, the initiative seeks to foster a thriving ecosystem for green capital in regions where it is most urgently needed.More than just a financing mechanism, the GCSF embodies the Team Europe approach to sustainable development. It will play a pivotal role in advancing the Global Gateway¿s objectives by mobilising private sector capital for transformative infrastructure and green investment in priority sectors. The primary goal of the GCSF is to reduce the cost of debt by providing direct support in the form of grants, through grant agreements, directly to issuers of green and sustainable bonds to lower their cost of borrowing. The facility is particularly focused on supporting first-time issuers with use-of proceeds of the bonds (underpinned green investments) aligned with the EU¿s Global Gateway and with the green eligibility criteria of the GGBI fund. By offering targeted, non-distortionary subsidies, the GCSF fills a crucial gap in the green finance ecosystem¿unlocking private capital that might otherwise remain out of reach. It enables LMICs to access international markets on more favourable terms, thus supporting long-term investment in climate-aligned infrastructure and environmental projects. By supporting LMICs in accessing international capital markets, the GCSF aims to bridge the gap between limited concessional finance and broader market finance, facilitating critical investments in sustainable infrastructure.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Reinforce Pharma, Health Products and Technologies value chains

description.narrative: The overall objective is to strengthen the African health security architecture, pharmaceutical systems and public health capacity, contributing to stronger, more resilient health systems and improved health outcomes. This objective pursues SDG 3.8 and promotes ultimately universal health coverage (UHC).The Action has two specific objectives:1.Specific Objective 1 (50 M): aims to reinforce health sector resilience and African strategic autonomy by focusing on underserved segments of the pharmaceutical value chain. This action is the fourth EU funded regional programme formulated in the framework of the regional MAV+ initiative. It encompasses a regional level and country level interventions through two workstreams.·Country level: through a Global Gateway 360° approach, it will focus on building stronger public and private ecosystems, with special attention to supporting innovative financial solutions (indicative countries: Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Ethiopia, Guinea Bissau and Guinea Conakry).·Regional level: will focus on 1) supporting regulatory strengthening and harmonisation, in line the African Medicines Agency mandate, 2) support establishment of regional pooled procurement mechanisms 3) support the fight against illicit drugs and 4) strengthen R&D/laboratories (indicative countries: Ethiopia, Guinea Bissau, Guinea Conakry, Burundi, DRC and Angola).2.Specific Objective 2 (5M): create a structure to support the EU-AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative. Following lessons learnt from the MAV+ Team Europe Support Structure (TESS), the support structure will have as main goal to ensure a coherent and coordinated approach of all interventions done under each of 5 hubs under the EU-AU Health Partnership TEI, namely MAV+, SRHR, Health Security using a One Health approach (HSOH), Public Health Institutes (PHI) and Digital Health (DH) and support the teams behind these hubs to ensure an effective implementation.This Action contributes to the Global Gateway Health Package presented at the 6th EU-AU Summit in 2022 and the EU-AU Health Partnership Team Europe Inititiave[1], which includes the Manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+) hub. [1] The EU AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative (TEI) includes five TEI Hubs: theHub on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+), the Hub on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, the Hub on Health Security using a One Health approach, the Hub on Digital Health and the Hub on Support to Public Health Insititutes in SSA

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Enhancing maritime security and safety of navigation in the Southern Red Sea, Horn of Africa and Gulf of Aden region (Red Sea-HoA Programme II)

description.narrative: The Red Sea and Gulf of Aden form a key maritime route for international trade, where a single disruptive event, such as conflict or a shipping accident, can significantly impact trade and transport. Historically, the region has been plagued by piracy and remains a corridor for illicit trafficking, including arms, people smuggling, and potential terrorist movements between the African and Arabian Peninsula coasts. The strategic landscape shifted dramatically following the numerous Houthi attacks targeting shipping vessels and tanks, further highlighting the region's vulnerabilities. Due to these attacks, shipping through the Red Sea has fallen by 70% since the beginning of 2024 Many vessels now detour around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 3,500 nautical miles, 16 to 32 days, and nearly EUR 900K in costs per journey. European shipping companies rerouted the vast majority of Asia¿Europe loops during peak months, implying an effective 60¿75% reduction in container services using the Red Sea in 2024, with avoidance persisting well into 2025The Action intends to build on the results of the first phase of the programme (11th EDF - Regional Programme for Maritime Security in the Red Sea Area, ending in November 2026), adapting the intervention logic and the activities to the new security and geo-political scenario, with the overall objective of enhancing maritime security and safety of navigation in the Southern Red Sea and Gulf of Aden region, with a specific focus on Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Sudan and Yemen. This subject was identified in Priority Area 2 (Democratic Governance, Peace and Security, Culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The Action is in line with SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions and DAC Markers on maritime security and trafficking, legal and judicial development, advanced technical and managerial training, and governance.Contributing to the implementation of the EU¿s policy and priorities under its maritime security strategies, the Strategic Compass, and the Global Gateway, the Action will contribute to: (i) strengthening national maritime law enforcement agencies to efficiently prevent, repress and respond to maritime threats and related hybrid menaces; (ii) enhancing capacities and capabilities of maritime affairs and port authorities in terms of port security and safety of navigation standards; (iii) strengthening intra and inter-regional maritime domain awareness (MDA); and (iv) reinforcing national judicial capacities to establish or improve the legal finish mechanism.To achieve the overall objective, an integrated approach will be applied, covering capacity building and mentoring, and promoting communication and coordination among national, international and regional partners, including the private sector. The Action will be carried out in complementarity with both EU and non-EU funded actions at national and regional level, and in cooperation with relevant Regional Economic Communities and other regional stakeholders.

description.narrative: The Action will mainly support the continuation and consolidation of NaturAfrica, the EU¿s Global Gateway flagship regional programme for biodiversity conservation in sub-Saharan Africa launched in 2022, with a second contribution. The overall objective remains to combat biodiversity loss while sustainably improving the livelihoods of local communities living around protected areas, building on the recommendations of the European Commission¿s publication ¿Larger than Elephants¿ for a strategic approach to wildlife conservation in Africa. To achieve this, NaturAfrica phase II will build and consolidate on actions launched during phase I since 2023, in 26 priority transboundary Key Landscapes for Conservation and Development (KLCD), located in six regions, representatives of main African habitats: the West African Sudano-Sahelian savannahs, the West African forests, the Congo basin rainforest, the Transhumance landscapes of Central Africa, the Eastern Rift Savannahs and Watersheds, the Trans-frontier Conservation Areas of Southern Africa. These landscapes cover the continent¿s main ecosystems, which preserve exceptional biodiversity and also provide a basis for sustainable livelihoods for more than 77.7 million people.NaturAfrica phase 2 pursues two closely linked specific objectives: (i) at local/landscape level, to improve ecosystem conservation and the governance of land and natural resources, and promote a green and sustainable economy benefitting local populations, including women and vulnerable groups; (ii) at continental and regional level, to strengthen inclusive governance of transboundary landscapes through cross-border and cross regional cooperation, information sharing, and harmonisation of policies between neighbouring countries. By financing the conservation and restoration of natural habitats and ecosystems, as well as supporting sustainable landscape development, the EU seeks to enhance ecosystem services ¿including carbon sequestration, soil fertility, water regulation, and disaster risk reduction¿while generating tangible benefits for local communities. By the end of Phase 2, NaturAfrica will strengthen the conservation status of at least 26 biodiversity-rich landscapes across 3.4 million km² through improved management and reduced pressures such as deforestation, poaching, and habitat loss. Thousands of households are expected to gain improved access to income-generating opportunities linked to sustainable value chains such as ecotourism, agroforestry, non-timber forest products, and renewable energy. Efforts will also focus on strenghtening inclusive governance, promoting cross-border cooperation, and enhancing participation of women and youth, and local communities in natural resource management, while applying human rights principles in practice. Regional and continental organisations will be supported to play stronger coordination and policy roles, contributing to the continuity and scaling-up of NaturAfrica results beyond the EU funding horizon.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Partnership for Accountability, Civic Engagement and Democratic Governance (PACED)

description.narrative: Upholding democratic governance goes far beyond single electoral events and requires informed citizen engagement through credible, transparent and inclusive decision-making processes that enhance the effectiveness, responsiveness and legitimacy of public policies. This action will reaffirm the EU¿s position as a reliable partner in supporting African ownership in the implementation of the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP) ; provide comprehensive electoral support at national, regional and continental levels; and enhance accountability mechanisms integrating a human rights-based approach (HRBA) perspective, including oversight by independent media, open governance reforms, and the fight against tax evasion, fraud, and illicit financial flows to reinforce credible inclusive democratic institutions, sustain resilient and accountable democracies, and increase tax transparency and domestic resource mobilisation. In a context of an evolving autocratic wave[1] and increasing political instability affecting in particular Sub-Saharan Africa, the action aligns with EU and AU strategies and interests, including that of promoting a rules-based order, enhancing the respect for human rights and gender equality and ultimately fulfilling African citizens¿ aspirations for a democracy that delivers positive outcomes.[2] The proposed action adopts a multi-level, multi-stakeholder approach, recognising that sustainable solutions require coordination across continental, regional, and national levels. It aims to strengthen African institutions, enhance electoral integrity, promote independent media and accountable governance, ultimately contributing to a more stable and prosperous continent.Transitional Justice (TJ) is considered at the highest political level by the African Union (AU) as a tool for conflict prevention and resolution, essential for addressing the root causes of conflict and building the foundation for lasting peace and sustainable development. Operationalising ¿African solutions to African problems¿, AU Member States (MS) have demanded increased support from the AU to implement the AUTJP and its roadmap. Hence, building on a predecessor project[3] under AAP 2022, greater emphasis will be placed on capacitating AU MS and regional bodies such as ECOWAS, SADC, IGAD and ECCAS.To enhance electoral processes, SO2 (Electoral Support) will extend beyond traditional technical and logistical support to election management bodies and State institutions, incorporating support for civil society, voter education, and independent media to ensure fair democratic coverage. The EU will promote a coherent approach by supporting the implementation of EU Election Observation Missions¿ (EU EOMs) recommendations and harmonising pan-African electoral capacities. To counter shrinking civic space, the action will strengthen regional CSO networks for election observation and foster structured collaboration between the AU, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and corresponding CSO platforms.The action will also promote accountability by strengthening independent media, advancing open governance reforms, and reinforcing the fight against tax fraud, evasion, and illicit financial flows. Support to media will focus on strengthening the resilience and financial sustainability of independent media and investigative journalism. title.narrative: EU support to the Eradication of PPR (Peste des petits ruminants) from Africa ¿ Phase 2

description.narrative: This action constitutes the second phase of the European Union¿s support to the eradication of Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) from Africa. PPR is a highly contagious infectious disease of sheep and goats that undermines food security, rural livelihoods, and trade across Africa. Its eradication would contribute to the improvement of sheep and goats productions, would protect the incomes of millions of smallholders, boost nutrition, and unlock new market opportunities. The overall objective of the action is to ensure the contribution of small ruminants (including wildlife) to resilient agri¿food systems and livelihoods by eradicating PPR and fighting other transboundary animal diseases while the specific objectives are to: -Enhanced governance, legal framework and access to finance for effective management of transboundary animal diseases-Strengthened capacity of Veterinary Services to prevent and control transboundary animal diseases, and -PPR Eradication efforts streamlined in alignment with WOAH standards. The action targets smallholder farmers, pastoralists, traders, women, and youth, who depend on sheep and goats for food security, incomes and resilience

title.narrative: Activity under preparation EMoRA - Eau du Mono et Résilience Alimentaire

description.narrative: En complémentarité des programmes régionaux IREE-MONO et PG-EAU, financés respectivement par le FEM et la BAD pour appuyer l¿ABM, l¿action EMoRA ambitionne d¿accompagner les deux États à coopérer pour une valorisation rationnelle et durable des ressources en eau du fleuve Mono, conformément à la Convention du bassin signée en 2014. Elle vise à créer les conditions techniques, organisationnelles et institutionnelles permettant d¿engager, à moyen terme, des aménagements structurants à l¿échelle du bassin (adduction en eau potable, préservation des écosystèmes, production énergétique, développement hydro-agricole, etc.).Dans cette perspective, l¿action appuiera l¿ABM dans le renforcement de ses fonctions de coordination, de planification et de suivi, à travers la mise en ¿uvre opérationnelle de son Plan stratégique (P.1.1) et le développement d¿une plateforme digitale regroupant et diffusant les connaissances, informations et initiatives disponibles (P.1.2). Cette plateforme sera alimentée par deux dispositifs de suivi intégrés : un suivi hydro-climatique (P.2.1) et un suivi environnemental (P.2.2), réunissant les services techniques et les universités des deux pays afin d¿améliorer la connaissance de l¿état des ressources et des usages. Les modèles d¿aide à la décision développés (P.2.3) permettront d¿estimer les effets du changement climatique et de fournir des informations essentielles à la planification et à la gestion des infrastructures actuelles et futures, mais aussi aux populations locales, à travers la diffusion d¿informations climatiques et hydrologiques accessibles pour les systèmes d¿alerte précoce et l¿appui à la planification agricole.

description.narrative: Border regions across Sub-Saharan Africa are characterised by complex, overlapping dynamics of fragility, where weak governance, insecurity, displacement and migratory movements, and limited economic opportunities intersect with environmental degradation and demographic pressures. These cross-border settings often experience the spillover of conflict, violent extremism, and illicit trade, while remaining vital corridors for mobility, trade, and cooperation. Addressing these challenges requires integrated, conflict-sensitive approaches that combine security, governance, and socio-economic resilience.The Action takes an integrated approach connecting peace, security, governance, and sustainable development to address fragility stemming from governance deficits, resource pressures, demographic trends, and climate change across the targeted regions. It also tackles displacement and migratory challenges, contributing to the EU¿s migration agenda through stability, inclusion, and sustainable solutions in priority areas.The overall objective of this Action is to prevent and mitigate instability and the impact of local conflicts in border areas. This subject was identified in Priority Area 2 (Democratic Governance, Peace and Security, Culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The Action is in line with SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, as well as No poverty (SDG 1); Zero hunger (SDG 2); Reduce inequality (SDG 10), Gender equality (SDG 5), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8) and Climate action (SDG 13).The action will target four different geographical windows: (i) border areas between Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, and Guinea (West Africa window) which face structural weaknesses worsened by climate change and natural resources degradation trafficking, and violent extremism. In this region, the Action will aim to enhance stability and resilience in border areas through inclusive economic growth, sustainable resource management, and coordinated action against cross-border trafficking; (ii) border areas between Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) - Uganda (Great Lakes window), where armed groups, natural resource exploitation, and weak law enforcement shape regional dynamics. In this area, the Action will enhance stability and resilience by addressing the drivers of violent extremism and fostering inclusive socio-economic development; (iii) border areas between Kenya, Somalia, Ethiopia and South Sudan (Horn of Africa window), where climate change jeopardises the main economic activities thus worsening inter-communal and cross-border conflict. In this region, the Action will aim to enhance peace, resilience, and sustainable growth in cross-border communities (including those affected by displacement) through strengthened conflict management, sustainable natural resource use, and inclusive, climate-smart economic development; (iv) border areas between Malawi and Mozambique (Southern Africa window) impacted by radicalisation within vulnerable communities and the spill over of terrorism and organised crime. Here, the Action will enhance institutional cooperation and community resilience to prevent conflict and radicalisation, fostering inclusive and secure border environments.The Action will be carried out in complementarity and coordination with both EU and non-EU funded actions at national and regional level, including relevant Regional Economic Communities and other regional stakeholders. This would include relevant TEIs, nexus actions, green deal sector related actions, as well as actions addressing terrorism spillover.

title.narrative: Tackling Trafficking and Crime along Corridors of Eastern and Southern Africa (TraCES Africa)

description.narrative: As Global Gateway investments gradually strengthen road, rail and port connectivity across the African continent, new opportunities for trade and regional integration are being created ¿ but so too are heightened risks of exploitation of these routes by organised crime and illicit trafficking networks. The development of strategic land corridors linking ports such as Mombasa, Durban and Lobito to the interior has made them both potential economic lifelines as well as vectors for organised crime. Across Eastern, Southern and Central Africa in particular, organised criminal networks exploit weak border governance, porous frontiers, corruption and uneven enforcement capacities, for trafficking in minerals, wildlife, fuel, firearms, illict drugs, human beings and migrant smuggling. These illicit flows move fluidly between legal and illegal economies, undermining state revenues, distorting markets and fuelling instability in fragile areas, also reaching EU Member States and affecting the EU¿s internal security. These trends call for a holistic, intelligence-led and corridor-based approach with an integral human dimension, rather than narrow, commodity-specific interventions.This Action responds to the growing security and governance challenges emerging along Africa¿s expanding trade and transport corridors, with the overall aim to reduce illicit trafficking and enhance security along key Global Gateway corridors through three interlinked outcomes:1.Enhanced intelligence through the establishment of National Intelligence Focal Points (NIFPs) and a Regional Intelligence Cell (RIC) to analyse, consolidate and disseminate corridor-specific risk profiles;2.Strengthened capacities for border posts, mobile enforcement teams and joint road-control operations, integrating an inclusive, gender-responsive and human rights-based (HRBA) approach;3.Regional cooperation and policy coherence: promotion and replication of good practices at regional level, supported by peer review and policy exchange.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Climate Mobility and Resilience in the Horn of Africa (CLIMHoA)

description.narrative: The overall objective of the Action is to reduce the impact of climate change, hazards, environmental degradation, and correlated stressors on forcibly displaced persons, migrants and host communities in the Greater Horn of Africa. This Action will support forcibly displaced populations (refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons (IDPs)) as well as migrants (i.e. persons who move away from their place of usual residence, whether within their country or across an international border, temporarily or permanently), with a specific focus on those moving at intra-regional level. It will also support host communities. The concept of «mobility» in the context of climate change and environmental degradation will also be used to encompass the full spectrum of movements.The Action¿s approach is to design area-based interventions targeting forcibly displaced persons and migrants as a whole ¿ although diverse - group of beneficiaries, specifically people who live in areas already affected by and at risk of climate mobility. The programme will focus its interventions on: - addressing the root causes of forced displacement and irregular migration in the context of climate change and environmental degradation by supporting sustainable initiatives and strategies that promote anticipatory action, disaster risk reduction and climate resilience and adaptation; - providing assistance and promoting inclusion of forcibly displaced, migrants and host communities, seeking resilience with durable solutions against climate impacts; and promoting research, data collection and analysis as well as knowledge-sharing. Three specific objectives have been formulated: Anticipatory action, disaster risk management and reliable data-driven early warning systems are strengthened at regional and national levels and in areas affected by climate risks and mobility. The planning and implementation of conflict-sensitive natural resources management in areas impacted by climate mobility is improved. Protection, resilience, and self-reliance mechanisms for the forcibly displaced, migrants and their host communities towards climate impacts are strengthened. Based on a tailored and area-based approach, the Action addresses different crisis scenarios, ranging from environmentally fragile environments affected by or at risk of human mobility due to climate change, environmental degradation or natural hazards to building longer term resilience at the regional, national, local, and community level. The Action is implemented with a regional approach, covering the Horn of Africa, and implemented in up to four countries, as countries share correlated pressures due to the complex interplay of climate change, environmental degradation, conflict, forced displacement and intra-regional migration.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation EU Investment for Nutrition (EU-I4N)

description.narrative: In the framework of Team Europe nutrition commitments, the EU Investment for Nutrition (EU-I4N) Action aims to improve nutritional outcomes by supporting the development of a pipeline of bankable nutrition-positive investment opportunities in agri-food value chains, with a particular focus on Sub-Saharan Africa, under a Global Gateway approach.The Action will seek to improve the availability, affordability, and competitiveness of nutritious foods through three mutually reinforcing pillars:Originate: investment pipeline development.Strengthen: operational technical assistance.Enable: support to the enabling legal, regulatory and policy environment.The Action will use EU funding catalytically to identify and structure investment opportunities, support selected projects and firms in becoming investment-ready and implementation-ready, and strengthen the enabling environment for responsible nutrition-sensitive investment. It will thereby help crowd in larger volumes of public and private capital while contributing to healthier diets, stronger local value addition and more resilient food systems.EU private sector actors will be involved, where relevant, as investors, technical partners, technology providers, processors, off-takers and business networks. Priority value chains may include formulated complementary foods and other specific nutritional foods, fortified foods, dairy, fresh fruits and vegetables, legumes and pulses, fish and aquaculture, eggs, aviculture, roots and tubers, biofortified crops and other nutrient-dense food segments, as well as selected enabling non-food segments directly linked to their performance and nutrition impact, such as storage, cold chain, packaging, transport, distribution, wholesale market functions, quality systems and traceability services.The action will not directly fund investments. Rather, it will facilitate matchmaking with third-party sources of finance, including EFSD+ guarantees, EU blending operations, EDFIs, DFIs, PDBs, impact funds and other private financial actors, including via the INTPA Investment Hub where relevant. Potential geographical areas of intervention include West Africa (Nigeria, Cote d¿Ivoire, Benin, Senegal) and East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Rwanda), given favourable business environment, positive dynamics for investment in nutrition-sensitive value chains and strong synergies with other EU programmes (i.e. ATCMA, MbA).

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Sustainable Value Chains in Food Systems

description.narrative: Current food systems ¿ encompassing agricultural, aquatic, and livestock production ¿ are environmentally unsustainable, contributing significantly to biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation and desertification, climate change, pollution, and deforestation. They are also structurally fragile and, therefore, cannot be relied upon to feed the world over the long term especially in a context where food security has become increasingly geopolitical. Moreover, they drive global trends toward poor diets and diet-related diseases, while failing to provide adequate opportunities for decent livelihoods, particularly for young people, women, and persons with disabilities.The proposed Action seeks to foster the transformation of agrifood systems into ones that are economically viable, socially equitable, environmentally sustainable and climate resilient. This will be achieved through the development of efficient value chains embedded in robust governance structures and mechanisms at national and territorial levels, across three complementary components. Component 1 (EUR 11.00 million) supports investments in sustainable, resilient, inclusive, and efficient agricultural and food value chains, in full alignment with the Global Gateway strategy. This will be pursued through two sub-components:Sub-component 1.1 (second phase of the AGRINFO Project) monitors, analyses, and translates new or increasingly stringent EU sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) regulations into accessible, timely, and actionable guidance for producers, exporters, competent authorities, and policymakers in partner countries seeking to maintain or improve access to the EU market.Sub-component 1.2 (second phase of the SATAF Project) strengthens linkages between local agricultural producers and international market actors, especially European buyers, financial institutions, and research organisations, in selected value chains based on agroecology and agroforestry, for both export and domestic markets.Component 2 (EUR 5.45 million) strengthens multistakeholder governance and land tenure legal frameworks to enable responsible, inclusive investment in agrifood systems, through two sub-components:Sub-component 2.1 supports the Committee on World Food Security (CFS) Secretariat and its civil society and private sector mechanisms to function effectively as a space for active multilateralism and open dialogue toward sustainable agrifood systems transformation.Sub-component 2.2 enhances the sustainability, technical soundness, and social legitimacy of agrifood investments through a coherent, on-demand support mechanism covering land governance, community engagement, and capacity-building for policy implementation.Component 3 (EUR 11.00 million) aims to catalyse the impact of research on agricultural innovation and its scaling across agrifood systems, through continued support to CGIAR Centres as part of the EU pledge of EUR 140 million (September 2021).

title.narrative: Improving access to commercial networks for aquaculture- related businesses in East Africa

description.narrative: This contract aims to stimulate a more competitive regional aquaculture industry, particularly in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, supporting the development of stronger business links between regional and with international commercial aquaculture related businesses, strengthening trade and investment support services as well as facilitating investment and business scale-up. The following are the results to be achieved by the contractor: 1) Support the Lake Victoria Fisheries Organisation (LVFO) and regional aquaculture associations in the emergence of an East African Aquaculture Exhibition and Conference; 2) Facilitate flow of increased investment through connecting regional aquaculture companies to individual and institutional investors and funding sources; 3) Support regional aquaculture associations to develop and execute effective Business to Business and study tour programmes.

title.narrative: Am¿lioration de l'acc¿s aux services pastoraux et des structures agro-pastorales de gestion des ressources naturelles dans les zones transfrontali¿res du Sud du Tchad, Nord de la RCA, Nord du Cameroun

description.narrative: Objectif : Dans la zone dintervention, la transhumance transfrontalière et la mobilité pastorale sont sécurisées dans un cadre de développement régulé, spécifique, respectueux de lenvironnement, des droits humains et de légalité de genre, et contribuant à la résilience des communautés pastorales face aux aléas climatiques. Le présent projet (volets 2.2. et 2.3. du PAIRIAC) y contribuera ensemble avec le projet dédié au volet 2.1. du PAIRIAC. Impact : Dans la zone dintervention, les ressources naturelles liées au pastoralisme sont gérées durablement. OBJECTIFS SPECIFIQUES, RESULTATS ATTENDUS ET PRINCIPALES ACTIVITES : Le cadre logique BC Chari et du présent projet PAIRIAC-2.2/3 sera unique. Pour rappel, les objectifs spécifiques sont les suivants : OS1. « Aménagement territorial intégré et gestion concertée dans le Paysage BC Chari » OS2. « Appui à la régulation, à la gestion et au contrôle transfrontalier pour contrer les menaces vis-à-vis des AP, de la faune et de la flore dans le Paysage BC Chari » OS3. « Bonne gouvernance locale de la transhumance transfrontalière et accès aux services pastoraux dans le Paysage BC Chari et la zone Sud-Ouest Tchad/Nord Cameroun » OS4. « Bonne gouvernance locale et actions innovantes du secteur productif des sédentaires dans le Paysage BC Chari » OS5. « Consolidation de lapproche paysage durable paysage BC Chari et la zone Sud-Ouest Tchad/Nord Cameroun »
