title.narrative: Projet de soutien à la stabilité et à la lutte contre l’extrémisme violent, le terrorisme et la criminalité transnationale organisée dans les zones frontalières du Bénin, Niger et Nigéria (LAKALI KANE)

description.narrative: Contract related to: Projet de soutien à la stabilité et à la lutte contre l’extrémisme violent, le terrorisme et la criminalité transnationale organisée dans les zones frontalières du Bénin, Niger et Nigéria (LAKALI KANE) - The security landscapes in West and Central Africa encompass a complex web of challenges, among which terrorism, civil conflicts fuelled by ethnic and political tensions, transnational organised crime and illicit trafficking, increasing violent extremism, widespread corruption and resource-related disputes. These multidimensional security challenges contribute to instability and hinder socio-economic development in the two regions that, as of today, approach security threats with different levels of engagement, both at national and at regional/international level. The national and international lack of awareness (and response) on the extremely complicated security situation has been having tremendous impact on the local populations in Central Africa, where the space for dialogue with state authorities on security and governance aspects is shrinking to the benefit of other geopolitical players. On the other hand, the critical and unstable situation in the Sahel in the last five years has forced countries in the region and international partners to actively engage in response mechanisms to avoid the spill-over of jihadist threats to neighbouring countries, and particularly in the coastal countries of West Africa. Notwithstanding the extremely different landscapes, the consequences of the strong interconnections between transnational organised crime, terrorism and violent extremism are far reaching and common to the two regions.The overall objective of the Action is to support stability efforts and contribute to the fight against violent extremism, terrorism, and transnational organised crime in Africa. The Action will have a multidimensional approach to the plethora of different but interconnected challenges that allow violent and armed groups, terrorists and criminal organisations to flourish in West and Central Africa. It will be implemented at the national, regional and inter-regional level and build on a comprehensive multi-stakeholder engagement strategy to maximise and sustain the results across both regions. It aligns with the Priority Area 2 (Democratic governance, peace and security, and culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The DAC/internal markers (policy objectives) relevant to this Action are the promotion of ¿Democratic and Inclusive Governance (DIG)¿ and ¿Gender equality¿. The Action will directly contribute to the SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions. The Specific Objective targeting Central Africa focuses on enhancing knowledge and capacity to produce data on transnational organised crime and illicit markets, including their connection to conflict and violent extremism to support evidence-based policy and appropriate criminal justice responses. A specific attention will be given to the trafficking in medical and pharmaceutical products in the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC) area. In West Africa, the Action focuses on five additional Specific Objectives: strengthening integrated border management practices in Cote d¿Ivoire, Ghana, Togo and Benin; reinforcing the criminal justice chain related to terrorism and terrorism financing in Cote d¿Ivoire, Ghana, Togo and Benin; increasing resilience and capacities of populations in the triborder area Benin-Niger-Nigeria, to prevent conflict and violent extremism; and, improving ECOWAS Member-States capacities to apply national and regional referral mechanisms in cross-border cases of trafficking in human beings.To achieve the overall objective, an integrated approach will be applied, covering capacity building and mentoring, awareness raising and knowledge building, and promoting

title.narrative: Projet d'appui ' la résilience des populations et ' la cohésion intercommunautaire au niveau des territoires transfrontaliers (Burkina-Faso, Bénin, Togo) - PARCIT

description.narrative: Contract related to: Projet d'appui ' la résilience des populations et ' la cohésion intercommunautaire au niveau des territoires transfrontaliers (Burkina-Faso, Bénin, Togo) - PARCIT - Les zones frontalières d¿Afrique subsaharienne sont souvent caractérisées par des mouvements de population, de bétail, de marchandises, de ressources naturelles, mais aussi par des trafics illégaux. Ces zones, lorsqu'elles sont associées à l'insécurité, aux conflits, aux impacts des changements climatiques, à la pauvreté, ou à l'isolement par rapport à l'État central, peuvent progressivement se muer en foyers d'instabilité, entraînant d'importants déplacements forcés. Ceci est notamment le cas du Sahel, en raison des développements politiques et de l'expansion récente de l'extrémisme violent dans les États du littoral du golfe de Guinée, ainsi que de l¿Afrique centrale, qui a entraîné des déplacements forcés internes et transfrontaliers. Il convient également de souligner les liens de cet extrémisme avec les mouvements de transhumance transfrontalière.Cette action vise à prévenir et atténuer l¿impact des conflits locaux en améliorant la résilience et la cohésion sociale des communautés transfrontalières. Pour ce faire, une approche intégrée sera appliquée, permettant de renforcer la gouvernance locale autour des ressources (y compris les aires protégées), en promouvant le dialogue et la médiation d¿une part, et d¿autre part en facilitant l¿accès aux services sociaux et marchands, notamment en renforçant les filières porteuses. Il y aura deux fenêtres subrégionales :Fenêtre Afrique de l¿Ouest :L¿action vise à prévenir et à atténuer l'impact des conflits locaux dans les zones frontalières du Bénin, du Burkina Faso et du Togo. Elle interviendra sur deux principaux domaines. Le premier domaine consiste à soutenir les dynamiques transfrontalières de vigilance communautaire autour des ressources naturelles, de la transhumance, de l¿insécurité et de la cohésion sociale. Il s¿agira de renforcer les cadres institutionnels de coopération transfrontalière et d¿échanges entre les acteurs locaux, d¿accompagner la mise en place d¿outils territoriaux transfrontaliers intégrés et de soutenir le développement d¿initiatives transfrontalières dans ces différents domaines. Il permettra également d¿accroitre les compétences et les moyens d¿actions des organisations de la société civile en matière de citoyenneté et d¿implication dans les actions de développement et favorisera les échanges entre les acteurs de la société civile et les autorités locales.Le deuxième domaine est relatif à l¿amélioration de l¿accès aux services sociaux de base, aux services marchands d¿intérêt transfrontalier, la productivité durable et la valorisation des filières agro-pastorales et halieutiques. Il s¿agit ici de la réalisation d¿infrastructures et de services sociaux de base dans les zones de déficit majeur, y compris dans les communes d¿accueil des personnes déplacées. Les infrastructures sont celles pouvant renforcer les dynamiques commerciales et économiques transfrontalières et des aménagements agropastoraux en soutien à la valorisation des filières. Cet axe devra être mise en ¿uvre en complémentarité avec les initiatives en cours, par exemple dans le cadre du programme PRADEP-AOS. Un dernier volet dans cet axe développera des mécanismes d¿appui et d¿accompagnement à la valorisation des chaines de valeur intégrées pour la création d¿emplois et de revenus au profit des femmes et des jeunes.Fenêtre Afrique Centrale :Cette action vise à s¿attaquer aux causes profondes de l¿instabilité et des conflits en Afrique centrale, dont particulièrement les flux de transhumance, en améliorant la résilience des communautés transfrontalières, en ren

description.narrative:
The African Virtual Investment Platform (AVIP) aims to address critical barriers to investment in Africa by providing comprehensive, timely, and reliable data on the continent's investment landscape. AVIP is a cornerstone of the Africa-OECD Partnership, endorsed by the OECD Ministerial Council in June 2023, and aligned with strategic frameworks such as Agenda 2063 and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

The Overall Objective is to accelerate the mobilisation of public and private investment for Africa¿s productive transformation, job creation and sustainable development.

The Specific Objective (Outcome) is is to develop comprehensive and reliable data and analysis on Africa¿s investment landscape and improve investment data collection and policy-making on the African continent.

AVIP¿s implementation will contribute to three main outputs:

·Comparable data, indicators and granular analysis on investment trends and policies in Africa are developed: AVIP will provide regularly updated indicators and analysis of Africa¿s investment landscape, covering foreign and domestic investment trends, infrastructure ecosystems, and sustainability impacts. A user-friendly online portal will serve as a central repository for this data, enabling tailored visualisations and country-specific profiles.

·The capacity of national, regional, and continental African statistical and other institutions to collect investment data and engage in investment impact and policy analysis is developed. : Through targeted training and technical support, AVIP will strengthen the capabilities of African statistical agencies and investment promotion entities to collect, harmonise, and analyse investment data. This capacity-building effort ensures long-term ownership and sustainability of the platform.

·Global, regional and national policy dialogue and cooperation on investment policies and good practices in view of implementing AU investment priorities, including the AfCFTA Investment Protocol, is enhanced. : AVIP will facilitate structured dialogues between public and private stakeholders, focusing on investment climate reforms and regional integration. These efforts aim to align national policies with the AfCFTA Investment Protocol and other global standards, such as the World Trade Organization (WTO) Investment Facilitation for Development, as well as contributing to the implementation of Sustainable Investment Facilitation Agreement negotiated by the European Union (EU), fostering an enabling environment for sustainable investments.

title.narrative: Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment for African Union Member States

description.narrative: Contract related to: Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment for African Union Member States - The Action has the goal to provide comprehensive support for trade and digitalisation towards a sustainable setup of an African single digital market within a robust cybersecurity environment. The objectives of the Action span across three macro-areas: eCommerce and ePayments; eGovernance; and cybersecurity to complement the support provided under other EU Actions including the Policy and Regulation Initiative for Digital Africa (PRIDA), the Data Governance in Africa initiative, Africa Europe Regulators Partnership and overall digital infrastructure investments.The Action will be segmented into five distinct components: regional clusters of countries in Western, Eastern, Central and Southern Africa, as well as a continental component that may support coordination and implementation of said clusters.Within the area of eCommerce and ePayments, the Action will support the different steps of digitally-enabled Business-to-Business (B2B) and Business-to-Consumer (B2C) trade transactions. From ordering to delivering goods and services, it will focus on expanding and rendering more inclusive, secure and trusted existing eCommerce platforms in collaboration wih national postal services. At the same time, the Action will support the payment systems enabligng such transactions through the interconnectivity of existing payment systems, offering tailor-made solutions for low transactions traders, and facilitating fintech integration, all in line with EU standards in view of their future interoperability with EU systems. Through its eGovernance work stream, the Action aims to address related legal and technical gaps at national, regional and continental level by supporting an enabling environment, the development and implementation of identified reusable eGovernance building blocks and services that will accelerate the development of an African single digital market.To complement this, the Action will focus on tackling the essential aspects of cybersecurity, by enhancing cyber resilience of target regions and countries. It will support the development of strategies, laws and regulations, promoting cyber hygiene, as well as enhancing capacity for the protection of critical infrastructure. Such an approach will not only ensure a unified political strategy against cross-border cyber threats, but also facilitate cooperation at technical level in preventing, deterring and responding to cyber attacks.The Overall Objective (Impact) of this Action is To accelerate digital trade and e-governance at continental, regional and bilateral levels within a robust cybersecurity environment in the framework of an African single digital market.The Specific Objectives (Outcomes) of this action are to: 1.    Enable and increase the inclusive and secure use of eCommerce platforms for cross-border trade.2.    En

title.narrative: PanAfGeo+ ''Invest'' - Support to geological sciencesand technology

description.narrative: Contract related to: PanAfGeo+ ''Invest'' - Support to geological sciencesand technology - Africa faces numerous economic, societal and environmental challenges linked to the green transition and the digital transformation, which can be addressed through geosciences partnerships, technologies and skills.The action will aim at improving the governance framework of African geoscience continental organisations and African Geological Surveys, as well as develop African Expert Networks in geoscience linking with the academic and private sector to provide support to African geological surveys and relevant national institutions delivering specific knowledge and science-policy outreach. The action will also aim at delivering high-quality training sessions and at providing specific technical assistance to Geological Surveys in geoscience topics. In addition, the action will promote economic partnerships through developing and maintaining B2B platform to generate project proposals on Critical Raw Materials and develop a match-making system to foster sustainable investments.Activities will be carried out at continental level while a focus will be given to activities at national level through specific country-windows, notably for countries that have signed or are in a process to sign EU-Africa partnerships on sustainable raw material value chains. The action will potentially aim at contributing to the subsequent specific roadmaps that the countries will elaborate to implement these partnerships. Based on the successful geoscientific programmes PanAfGeo1 and 2[1], and the EU-Africa business platform and networks developed in AfricaMaVal[2], the Action will aim at contributing to sustainable management of geological resources, addressing climate change adaptation and mitigation, in Africa and promote EU-African partnerships in geosciences in particular raw materials. The action will have three components:1.Strengthen Africa ¿ EU institutional partnerships on Geosciences at continental, regional and national levels;2.Make more effective African Geological Surveys and the Organisation of African Geological Surveys in terms of geoscientific information and of national, regional and continental support to policy making and planning processes;3.Promote EU-Africa economic partnerships on raw materials value chains including gender and human rights sensitive approach.[1] Home ¿ PanAfGeo - PanAfGeo (eurogeosurveys.org)[2] AfricaMaVal ¿ EU-Africa Partnerships on sustainable Raw Materials Value Chain

description.narrative: Contract related to: Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 - The action will contribute to advancing the realisation of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in Africa through reducing the harmful practices that violate the human rights of girls and young women and increase the availability, affordability and accessibility of quality assured, life-saving sexual and reproductive health (SRH) knowledge and services.The action is proposed in the framework of the Global Gateway Health Package presented at the EU-AU Summit in 2022 and is elaborated in the context of the Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights Team Europe Initiative (SRHR TEI). The Action will contribute to the EU human development target, SDG 3 and SDG 5, and it is principally aimed at sexual and reproductive health and health systems. Its secondary objective is gender and women¿s and girls¿ equality. Through its focus on equality, the realisation of SRH rights, and on reducing harmful practices, the Action contributes to the delivery of Gender Action Plan III (GAP III) and to the EU Global Health Strategy. Addressing harmful practices requires a combination of legal, governance, social, economic and cultural shifts. From a programme delivery perspective, reaching communities is a key challenge. The engagement of all stakeholders, especially civil society, community and faith leaders and families, is fundamental to achieving sustainable change. The Action will continue the longstanding EU support to eliminating child marriage and FGM, including through the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (stream I and II), working in collaboration with the African Union Commission, governments and civil society organizations (CSOs) to protect women and girls at risk, and to support survivors. Increasingly, programmes invest in and through groups led by adolescent and young women themselves.[1]Inadequate availability, affordability of quality assured SRH commodities negatively affects a range of SRHR outcomes. The action will contribute to better access to quality assured SRH commodities to strengthen regulatory capacity, improve sustainable procurement and more predictable supply chain management functioning including by improving economies of scale through efficient well-functioning regional procurement mechanisms. The action will be rooted in on-going EC action in this area (AD2023) building on progress and expanding on opportunities that arise from earlier efforts while avoiding duplication. Data and evidence are insufficiently generated, disseminated, and used to advance advocacy and promote accountability. Improved prioritisation and SRHR-related systems strengthening requires better use of relevant, strategic data to identify and target evolving challenges and needs. The Action will promote better collection and management and more productive use of strategic information, improving priority setting and capacitating CSOs to hold governments and local authorities to account for progress against SRHR commitments. EU and Africa objectives and priorities are addressed through this action. description.narrative: This contract supports the promotion of neglected and underutilized species (NUS) under the DeSIRA+ framework, with the aim of strengthening agroecological innovation, agrobiodiversity, and the resilience of food systems in Africa, particularly in Burkina Faso and Niger. It focuses on improving the sustainable use and valorisation of local crop diversity, especially species that are often overlooked despite their nutritional, environmental, and economic potential. By encouraging the integration of these crops into farming systems and local value chains, the action contributes to more diversified agricultural production, improved livelihoods, and greater resilience to climate and market shocks. It also promotes collaboration among research institutions, development partners, producers¿ organisations, and other stakeholders to generate knowledge, test innovations, and scale up good practices. More broadly, the contract contributes to the objectives of DeSIRA+ by linking agricultural research and innovation with practical solutions for sustainable development, better nutrition, ecosystem preservation, and inclusive rural transformation.

title.narrative: PICVERT - Programme Intégré pour la Conservation, la Valorisation économique et la Résilience Transfrontalière du paysage du Niokolo-Badiar-Dulombi-Boe

description.narrative: Contract related to: PICVERT - Programme Intégré pour la Conservation, la Valorisation économique et la Résilience Transfrontalière du paysage du Niokolo-Badiar-Dulombi-Boe - The overall objective of the NaturAfrica initiative is to tackle biodiversity loss through restoring and protecting a network of protected areas and high value ecosystems and promoting the sustainable management of surrounding landscapes whilst creating decent incomes and jobs in green sectors for local populations. Through the financing of the conservation and restoration of natural habitats and ecosystems, and the sustainable management and development of key landscapes, the EU aims also to enhance ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, soil fertility, water cycle regulation, disaster risk reduction, etc. as well as benefits for the local populations.The NaturAfrica initiative intends to work in Key Landscapes for Conservation and Development (KLCD) for (i) increasing the conservation of areas with high biodiversity value and high carbon content, and developing green economy activities by and for the neighbouring local communities and (ii) improving the inclusive governance of these landscapes to improve territorial planning, reduce conflicts and mobilise carbon finance. The transboundary nature of biological resources, their ecosystems and habitats species and communities calls for interventions at regional level through transboundary landscapes. Key transboundary landscapes were identified in six priority regions, following a wide consultation of stakeholders, including national institutions, civil society and the private sector. These regions are representatives of main African habitats with specific challenges each, and include: Congo Basin Forest ecosystems (Gabon, Burundi, Cameroon, Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Central African Republic (CAR), Uganda, South Sudan, Rwanda)   Transhumance landscapes in Central Africa (Chad, CAR, Nigeria, Cameroon)  West Africa Forests (Burkina Faso, Guinea Conakry, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Cote d¿Ivoire Ivory Coast, Nigeria)  Sudano-Sahelian savannahs of West Africa (Burkina Faso, Benin, Niger, Togo, Ghana, Senegal, Guinea)   Eastern Rift savannahs and watersheds (Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Tanzania)  Trans-frontier conservation areas of Southern Africa (Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Malawi, Mozambique, Angola, South Africa).    Relevant green economy activities include renewable energy and sustainable value chains (agriculture, livestock, fisheries, timber/non-timber forest products, tourism, ethical and sustainable fashion and circular industries). The NaturAfrica initiative complements numerous national initiatives that are foreseen in the national programmes within the same transboundary landscapes or expanding the approach to other important national landscapes and altogether, with the contribution of EU Member States (MS), is part of the large NaturAfrica flagship.This is the first phase of a 2-phased programme with a mid-term evaluation leading to a second phase in 2025. Phase 1 will initiate interventions in key landscapes, building synergies between actors and interventions, and pave the way for consolidation in phase 2.  <p

title.narrative: EU-EAC DEEP: Digital Economy, E-Commerce, E-Payments, and Public E-Services Programme

description.narrative: Contract related to: EU-EAC DEEP: Digital Economy, E-Commerce, E-Payments, and Public E-Services Programme - The Action has the goal to provide comprehensive support for trade and digitalisation towards a sustainable setup of an African single digital market within a robust cybersecurity environment. The objectives of the Action span across three macro-areas: eCommerce and ePayments; eGovernance; and cybersecurity to complement the support provided under other EU Actions including the Policy and Regulation Initiative for Digital Africa (PRIDA), the Data Governance in Africa initiative, Africa Europe Regulators Partnership and overall digital infrastructure investments.The Action will be segmented into five distinct components: regional clusters of countries in Western, Eastern, Central and Southern Africa, as well as a continental component that may support coordination and implementation of said clusters.Within the area of eCommerce and ePayments, the Action will support the different steps of digitally-enabled Business-to-Business (B2B) and Business-to-Consumer (B2C) trade transactions. From ordering to delivering goods and services, it will focus on expanding and rendering more inclusive, secure and trusted existing eCommerce platforms in collaboration wih national postal services. At the same time, the Action will support the payment systems enabligng such transactions through the interconnectivity of existing payment systems, offering tailor-made solutions for low transactions traders, and facilitating fintech integration, all in line with EU standards in view of their future interoperability with EU systems. Through its eGovernance work stream, the Action aims to address related legal and technical gaps at national, regional and continental level by supporting an enabling environment, the development and implementation of identified reusable eGovernance building blocks and services that will accelerate the development of an African single digital market.To complement this, the Action will focus on tackling the essential aspects of cybersecurity, by enhancing cyber resilience of target regions and countries. It will support the development of strategies, laws and regulations, promoting cyber hygiene, as well as enhancing capacity for the protection of critical infrastructure. Such an approach will not only ensure a unified political strategy against cross-border cyber threats, but also facilitate cooperation at technical level in preventing, deterring and responding to cyber attacks.The Overall Objective (Impact) of this Action is To accelerate digital trade and e-governance at continental, regional and bilateral levels within a robust cybersecurity environment in the framework of an African single digital market.The Specific Objectives (Outcomes) of this action are to: 1.    Enable and increase the inclusive and secure use of eCommerce platforms for cross-border trade.2.    En

title.narrative: PROGIRESS OS1 - Recherche et Information pour la Gestion des Eaux Transfrontalières (RIGET)

description.narrative: Contract related to: PROGIRESS OS1 - Recherche et Information pour la Gestion des Eaux Transfrontalières (RIGET) - L¿action vise à renforcer la résilience aux changements climatiques des systèmes des eaux de surface (Bassin du Fleuve Sénégal ou BFS) et des eaux souterraines (Bassin Aquifère Sénégalo-Mauritanien ou BASM) à travers l¿amélioration de la gestion durable des ressources en eau et des écosystèmes dans les deux bassins. Elle répond à l¿attention grandissante des populations par rapport aux problématiques de dégradation environnementale (salinisation des terres, érosion des sols, perte de couvert végétal, plantes invasives) et de réduction de la qualité et de la disponibilité de la ressource en eau, problématiques qui contribuent à renforcer le processus de désertification, affectent la production agricole et énergétique et nuisent au développement socio-économique durable des zones ciblées.L¿action s¿inscrit dans le cadre de l¿Initiative Equipe Europe pour la gestion des eaux transfrontalières en Afrique portée par les institutions européennes et huit Etats membres afin de soutenir le développement et l¿intégration régionale à travers le continent. Elle renforce le rôle de leader de l¿Equipe Europe sur la gestion des eaux transfrontalières et de leurs bassins versants en Afrique et en particulier dans la région ciblée.L¿action s¿inscrit dans la stratégie de la Commission européenne « Global Gateway », en investissant sur des activités d¿adaptation et de résilience face au changement climatique, en promouvant la consolidation de la paix et de la bonne gouvernance et en soutenant la connaissance et le montage de projets pour permettre la réalisation d¿investissements transfrontaliers d¿envergure au service du bien commun.Les résultats indiqués et les activités qui sont prévues constituent des priorités déjà identifiées par les organismes de bassin responsables de la gestion des ressources en eau dans les deux bassins, à savoir l¿Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS) et l¿Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Gambie (OMVG). Au niveau des pays des bassins ciblés par l¿action (Gambie, Guinée, Guinée Bissau, Mali, Mauritanie et Sénégal), l¿action est également alignée avec les politiques sectorielles nationales et complémentaires des projets et programmes actuellement mis en ¿uvre. Sur le plan régional, l¿action est en particulier complémentaire de l¿Initiative Blue Peace Bonds (FEDD+) au bénéfice de l¿OMVG et du projet NaturAfrica mené dans le Parc national du Niokolo-Koba, affluent du fleuve Gambie.L¿action contribue à l¿atteinte des ODD 6 (eau potable et assainissement), 5 (égalité entre les sexes), 8 (travail décent et croissance économique), 10 (réduire les inégalités), 12 (consommation et production responsable), 13 (lutte contre les changements climatiques) et 15 (vie terrestre). L¿objectif général de cette action est l¿amélioration de la résilience aux changements climatiques des systèmes des eaux de surface dans le bassin du fleuve Sénégal (BFS) et des eaux souterraines dans le bassin aquifère Sénégalo-Mauritanien (BASM). Les objectifs spécifiques de cette action sont : 1.La gestion durable des ressources en eau de surface et souterraines est renforcée2.L¿état des ressources naturelles et de la biodiversité est amélioré3.La coopération dans le domaine de la gestion de l¿eau est renforcée

title.narrative: Supporting the strategic development, operational implementation, and financial sustainability of the Traceability and Verification System (TRVST) for vaccines and other health products in the African continent to strengthen countries Primary Health

description.narrative: Expansion of the Traceability and Verification System (TRVST), a digital traceability mechanism managed by UNICEF and inspired by the European Medicines Verification System. The EU already initiated a partnership with UNICEF under AAP 2021 in support of TRVST and the current contract is coming to an end in December of 2024. This consecutive support would allow for a roll-out of TRVST to additional African countries and to expand the system to other essential medicines and health products beyond vaccines. This project brings digitalization to combat the issue of falsified and substandard health products.

title.narrative: Farmers¿ Organizations for Institutional strengthening, Market access, Policy engagement, Advocacy, Community and Transformation (FO4IMPACT)

description.narrative: Contract related to: Farmers¿ Organizations for Institutional strengthening, Market access, Policy engagement, Advocacy, Community and Transformation (FO4IMPACT) - This Action aims at enhancing innovation through multi-stakeholder partnerships involving research to accelerate agro-ecological transitions of food systems in Sub-Saharan Africa. Investments are indeed needed to better understand and use ecological processes, to develop agro-ecological technologies, to stimulate and bring innovations to scale, to mobilize and strengthen the capacities of national research, farmers¿ organizations, NGOs and private sector, and to improve enabling policies for agro-ecology and sustainable food systems. The Action will be articulated around three components that will support: (1) the Consultative Group of International Agriculture Research (CGIAR) in addressing Africa¿s pressing challenges to make food systems more productive and resilient.           (2) key partnerships, led by non-research actors but supported by research, to co-create and scale up agro-ecological innovations in Africa for more productive and more resilient food systems.          (3) the implementation of the SADC regional strategy on sustainable food systems while building on the dynamics of the other two components and previous experience in the region.

title.narrative: Health System Strengthening for Universal Health Coverage (UHC) Programme ¿ Phase V (2025-2028)

description.narrative: Contract related to: Health System Strengthening for Universal Health Coverage (UHC) Programme ¿ Phase V (2025-2028) - This action aligns with the Multi-Annual Financing Framework 2021-2027 and will continue crucial EU support for the UHC-Partnership with the World Health Organization (WHO) starting in 2025. The action is in line with the 2022 EU Global Health Strategy (GHS), utilising the Global Gateway and the Team Europe approach, funded by the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI-Global Europe). Launched in 2011, the programme is currently active in more than 120 countries across Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, Asia, and Europe, with participation from EU Member States such as Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, and Luxembourg, as well as the United Kingdom, Canada, and Japan. The action aims to support the implementation of WHO¿s 14th General Programme of Work (2025-2028) in partner countries, enhancing efforts to build resilient health systems and achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

title.narrative: Increasing awareness and accession to the Water Convention (Phase 3)

description.narrative:
The objective of this project is to support the UNECE Secretariat in charge of the 1992 Convention on the Protection and Use of Transboundary Watercourses and International Lakes (Water Convention). The Water Convention aims to ensure the sustainable use of transboundary water resources by facilitating cooperation across transboundary water basins. The Water Convention is ratified by 56 countries and the EU.

The Water Convention Secretariat is in charge of fostering the application of Convention principles and improve the management of transboundary waters, both surface and groundwater, at the national, basin and regional level in different continents. The contract will provide technical and legal advice, and build capacities among newly acceding countries and other regions, which have requested support to accede to the Water Convention.

title.narrative: EFI support to the EU Flagship Initiative on Sustainable Cocoa, in Côte d¿Ivoire Ghana and Cameroon (SCP 2.0)

description.narrative: Contract related to: EFI support to the EU Flagship Initiative on Sustainable Cocoa, in Côte d¿Ivoire Ghana and Cameroon (SCP 2.0) - The Action aims to empower farmers (women and men), farmers¿ organisations, including women farmers¿ organizations, and cooperatives, as well as to promote inclusive, sustainable and climate resilient agricultural value chains. The Action will enhance linkages between farmer¿s organisations and cooperatives with local and international agribusinesses (traders, processing companies, food industry) and financial institutions. Strong and consolidated farmers¿ organisations are key in order to develop truly inclusive and sustainable agricultural value chains in Africa. Investments are crucial to support cooperatives and agri-MSMEs, allowing to add value to local productions, a smooth sustainable agri-food transition and decent and green job creation. The Action will have two linked components: (1) The first one will support African farmer¿s organisations at continental, regional, and national level. This Component will specifically support technical and economic services provided by farmer¿s organisations, as well as enhance contract farming between farmers¿ organisations and cooperatives with local agri-SMEs and multinationals.(2) The second component will complement the ongoing EU initiatives on Key Value Chains, notably sustainable cocoa and cashew.The Overall Objective of this Action is to promote inclusive, sustainable and climate resilient agricultural value chains through policy support, technical assistance and the empowerment of key actors linking agribusiness to African farmers, to fully increase the participation of farmers in the transformation and modernisation of the agriculture sector at the national/regional level thereby increasing their incomes and reducing poverty in African countries.

description.narrative: Contract related to: IMO Future-Ready Shipping in Africa - In line with the external dimension of the EU Green Deal, the EU Energy & Climate Diplomacy, the transport sector in its railway and maritime sub-sectors is at a critical juncture with the potential to play a significant role in global decarbonisation efforts. The EU external action on transport has become more strategic and geopolitical, and the relation with and support to EU companies has become a key priority. EU values and its regulatory framework contribution towards rail and maritime global sectors sustainability is key to also to find entry points supporting EU industry competitivity. This action will complement EU¿s support to international organisations such as the International Maritime Organization (IMO) activities involving several countries sharing EU values also looking for further support to EU¿s efforts on the regulatory front. In a similar manner, it will promote through entities such as the European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) the EU¿s rail regulatory framework in the African context.  This action aims at completing INTPA¿s toolbox in preparation to scale up the Global Gateway in the next MFF, and includes two main specific objectives: (i) to support partner countries in improving the investment climate and regulatory frameworks to contribute to unlocking investment, (ii) to promote and transpose to partner countries EU values, standards, knowledge, and best practices on sustainable transport, including just and better working conditions for women building the necessary human resources capacity. Three outcomes are expected: (a) specific support to the rail sector in sub-Saharan Africa, (b) on the maritime sector, cooperation with international organisations such as IMO for port governance and green and digital investments preparation (including single window), specifically in sub-Saharan Africa, and (c) support globally on maritime transport-related gender issues.  The African maritime and port governance components, as well as the project on African rail, are key to the continent's efforts in maritime and rail decarbonisation and promoting greener, safer, and more socially responsible transportation. The actions include capacity building aiming to develop advanced training capacity for a new generation of seafarers proficient in decarbonised and digital shipping operations. Additionally, this action will contribute to combating violence and harassment in the maritime industry, with the goal of fostering a culture of zero tolerance and strengthening regulatory frameworks, in line with EU commitments to promote decent, safe, and fair employment, and improve workplace safety and culture at sea. the EU's perspective, supporting these actions is crucial as it aligns with the EU's own goals of reducing emissions, promoting sustainable transportation, and ensuring safe and fair working conditions, and demonstrates the EU's commitment to cooperation and partnership with African countries in achieving these shared objectives, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable and equitable global maritime industry. The proposed maritime and railway components contribute to the NDICI-Global Europe `Global Challenges¿ Priority area on Prosperity, directly addressing climate change mitigation through GHG emission reduction in international maritime shipping, maritime and port governance, the green transition and promoting zero tolerance

description.narrative: Contract related to: Desira+ - MainstreamAIS (Agricultural Innovation System) - This Action aims at enhancing innovation through multi-stakeholder partnerships involving research to accelerate agro-ecological transitions of food systems in Sub-Saharan Africa. Investments are indeed needed to better understand and use ecological processes, to develop agro-ecological technologies, to stimulate and bring innovations to scale, to mobilize and strengthen the capacities of national research, farmers¿ organizations, NGOs and private sector, and to improve enabling policies for agro-ecology and sustainable food systems. The Action will be articulated around three components that will support: (1) the Consultative Group of International Agriculture Research (CGIAR) in addressing Africa¿s pressing challenges to make food systems more productive and resilient.           (2) key partnerships, led by non-research actors but supported by research, to co-create and scale up agro-ecological innovations in Africa for more productive and more resilient food systems.          (3) the implementation of the SADC regional strategy on sustainable food systems while building on the dynamics of the other two components and previous experience in the region.

title.narrative: Corridors Abidjan-Lagos et Abidjan-Ouagadougou : vers des corridors de développement verts et inclusifs

description.narrative:
La présente Action s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme « Mesures de facilitation du commerce et du transport pour les corridors stratégiques en Afrique » de l'UE, qui vise à éliminer les obstacles physiques et non physiques au commerce, qui ont jusqu'à présent entravé le commerce et l'intégration intra-africains, et à accroître l'efficacité des systèmes de transport sur les corridors et de leur gestion. L'Action s'articule autour de trois piliers : 1) la coordination et la gouvernance des corridors, 2) la facilitation du transport et 3) la facilitation des échanges.

L¿Action couvre deux des douze corridors stratégiques : le corridor Abidjan-Ouagadougou (CAO) et le corridor Abidjan-Lagos (CAL) qui relie la Côte d¿Ivoire, le Ghana, le Togo, le Bénin et le Nigeria.

L'Action est d'une durée de 48 mois et d'un montant total de 45 300 000 EUR, dont 45 000 000 financés par l'UE. Elle est mise en oeuvre par un consortium composé de ENABEL (lead), Expertise France et Trade Mark Africa.

L'objectif global est : Contribuer à l¿amélioration de l¿intégration régionale et économique en Afrique

Les objectifs spécifiques sont :

OSA Les autorités contractantes et de gestion des corridors planifient, réalisent et gèrent les infrastructures de manière durable et en soutien à la croissance inclusive

OSB Les systèmes du transport terrestre des corridors AO et AL réduisent les coûts, les délais et les externalités négatives à travers le renforcement de leur régulation, performance et innovation opérationnelle

OSC La coordination des échanges et l¿amélioration de l¿infrastructure contribuent à l¿accroissement du commerce inclusif et durable

title.narrative: Fighting antimicrobial resistance and strengthening the One Health workforce in Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: Fighting antimicrobial resistance and strengthening the One Health workforce in Africa - This regional action is proposed in the framework of the health pillar of the Global Gateway Africa-Europe Investment Package presented at the 2022 EU-AU Summit, where the AU and EU adopted ¿A Joint Vision 2030¿ declaration with strong commintments on health security and the One Health approach. The regional TEI with Africa on sustainable health security using a One Health approach (as defined by the One Health High Level Expert Pannel (OHHLEP)[1]) has a strong EU member states (MS) support:five EU MS are involved in the TEI (EUR 309 million indicative financial contributions by Team Europe (TE)). This TEI aims to develop further the EU¿s strategic partnership with the Africa CDC, public health agency of the AU, and to align with the AU call for a New Public Health Order in Africa. Priority areas of support have been identified jointly by TE members and Africa CDC. The intention is also to substantiate the partnership with other African organizations for Health security using a One Health approach.The overall objective of this action is to contribute to sustainably strengthen health security in Africa through two main interventions:·A first component will focus on improving the surveillance, prevention and control of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) using an integrated, systems strengthening One Health approach at national, regional and continental levels. This component will thereby particularly focus on providing support to the AMR Control programme of the Africa CDC and to its effective roll-out at regional and national levels in alignment with Global standards.·A second component will focus on improving the skills and capacities of relevant professional groups from various sectors in applying the One Health approach,As this will be the second package of action financed by the European Commission under the framework of the TEI with Africa on sustainable Health Security using a One Health approach (TEIA HSOH), it consciously builds on the RIP AAP23 Action for ¿Strengthening One Health surveillance, early detection and prevention of emerging zoonotic diseases in Africa¿ and further substantiates EU¿s strategic partnership with Africa CDC in particular the existing collaboration with its European counterpart the European Center for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). Furthermore, it leverages expertise available among European and national institutes and agencies relevant to the One Health approach and TEI Member States¿ development agencies (see section 2.2 on stakeholders).[1] https://www.who.int/news/item/01-12-2021-tripartite-and-unep-support-ohhlep-s-definition-of-one-health

title.narrative: EU- NGO Human Rights Forum: focus on Equality and Non-Discrimination

description.narrative: Contract related to: EU- NGO Human Rights Forum: focus on Equality and Non-Discrimination - This action supports the implementation of the Action Plan on Human Rights and Democracy 2020-2027 and in particular the priority area 5 ¿Working better together¿ of the MIP for the Thematic Programme on Human Rights and Democracy. Its main objective is to provide support measures as identified in Article 24(1) of the NDICI Regulation. In particular, it intends to prepare, monitor, evaluate and audit the activities financed by the Human Rights and Democracy thematic programme in order to strengthen the effectiveness of the funding. It will also add value, complementarity and consistency with geographical programmes while enhancing the human rights and democracy thematic programme¿s synergy with EU¿s policy priorities. Furthermore, this Action will enhance the work of civil society actors working on human rights and democracy issues by providing the necessary visibility, opportunity for consultation, access to political dialogue, support to their monitoring activities which will overall enhance their contribution to sustainable development. The mobilisation of civil society actors around these matters will enhance human rights and democracy advocacy efforts at national level. This will in turn increase visibility of EU support and promotion of EU fundamental values in third-country partners. The end beneficiaries of the action are civil society organisations active in the field of human rights and democracy including women¿s rights organisations, human rights defenders and more generally communities of third partner countries. Additional networking activities will ensure their long-term involvement around these issues.

title.narrative: Technical assistance for the OACPS financial management reinforcement

description.narrative:
The objective of this assignment is to support the OACPS Secretariat in enhancing its efficiency of reporting to the European Commission and in strengthening its budgeting, procurement, financial and accounting capabilities by offering targeted guidance in daily operations and comprehensive training for newly recruited staff.

Specifically, the role of the technical assistance should focus on accompanying the Secretariat in enhancing its capacity in drafting its operating budget taking into account OACPS MS contributions and different level of priorities in spending, as well as in managing its budget in a sound, sustainable and effective way. To this regard, the TA will work closely with the department of Administration, Finance and Human Resources, and will provide targeted guidance in daily operations and comprehensive training for newly recruited staff. Finally, the TA will support the Secretariat in reinforcing its financial and accounting reporting capacity.

title.narrative: 2025-2027 INTPA/ENEST/MENA contribution for licenced and Processed Data provided by EIB as per Supplementary Agreement

description.narrative: Contract related to: 2025-2027 INTPA/ENEST/MENA contribution for licenced and Processed Data provided by EIB as per Supplementary Agreement - NDICI - Global Europe (GE) Regulation[1] established EFSD+ and related budgetary guarantees as a means to support investments and increase access to financing in partner countries. Technical Assistance (TA) is an important part of EFSD+ that will enable implementation of budgetary guarantees in the global context. In accordance with that, Commission adopted three Decisions regarding Regional Multi-Annual Indicative Programmes (MIPs) 2021-2027 for Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), Asia and the Pacific (AP), and the Americas and the Caribbean (AC),[2] confirming funding for EFSD+ TA activities. The overall objective of the Action is to foster sustainable and inclusive economic, environmental and social development, and poverty reduction in partner countries, through investments in the following sectors: MSMEs; agriculture, biodiversity, forests; sustainable cities including sanitation and water sector; human development and sustainable finance.The specific objective of the Action is to facilitate deployment of EFSD+ budgetary guarantees that are used to de-risk bankable projects with a developmental impact and crowd-in private sector financing. The innovative character of the guarantees makes the TA indispensable to develop a pipeline of transactions, as well as to facilitate the roll-out of the financial products, while ensuring the expected development impact. It will be particularly important to enable the operationalisation of the guarantees in fragile, Least Developed Countries (LDCs) context, ensuring that distribution of EFSD+ investments is balanced. The Action is fully in line with the EU and partner countries¿ priorities and supports, directly or indirectly, an overwhelming majority of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and with cross-cutting issues such as gender equality, human rights, climate adaptation and environmental protection. [1] Regulation (EU) 2021/947 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 June 2021 establishing the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument ¿ Global Europe, amending and repealing Decision No 466/2014/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Regulation (EU) 2017/1601 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Council Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 480/2009 (Text with EEA relevance)[2] COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION adopting a Multiannual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa for the period 2021-2027 (C(2021) 9373), COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION adopting a Multiannual Indicative Programme for Asia Pacific Region for the period 2021-2027 ( C(2021) 9251), COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION adopting a Multiannual Indicative Programme for the Americas and the Caribbean for the period 2021-2027, (C(2021) 9356),

title.narrative: IYBA WIDU - Maximiser le potentiel de la jeunesse et de l'entrepreneuriat en partenariat avec la diaspora de l'Afrique de l¿Ouest

description.narrative: Contract related to: IYBA WIDU - Maximiser le potentiel de la jeunesse et de l'entrepreneuriat en partenariat avec la diaspora de l'Afrique de l¿Ouest - The goal of this Action is to improve the inclusion of youth in resilient and climate-smart green economic transitions that address the root causes of irregular migration in West African countries. It complements the ¿Managing Migration Better in Western Africa¿ Action which aims at strengthening migration management. A comprehensive approach including skills development, improved access to finance for Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) notably through diaspora investment and support to value chains development is expected to influence individual decision-making processes and potentially reduce migration aspirations by providing better local prospects. It is also expected to help and facilitate sustainable reintegration. More specifically, this Action ¿Unleashing the Potential of Youth in West Africa¿ will contribute to green skills¿ alignment with the private sector needs (1.1), promote diaspora¿s investments (2.1), as well as enhance access to finance and technical support for green business growth (2.2). Job creation will also be supported through the development of targeted green, circular and low-carbon value chains (2.3).This action contributes to the implementation of the Youth Action Plan. To the extent possible, this action will build upon and benefit from Global Gateway investments in the targeted countries, contributing to strengthening the local economy, job creation and markets aligned with the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Investing in Young Businesses in Africa[1], the Regional Team Europe Initiative Opportunity-driven Skills and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Africa as well as the two migration-related regional TEIs[2]. Conversely, it will contribute to building the skills required and achieving the targeted transformational impact of the Global Gateway strategy, and its commitments to address gender equality, by maximizing its impact on the relevant ecosystems with a 360 approach. The transition to green growth is mainstreamed throughout the action. By aligning with the Nationally Determined Contributions and the National Adaptation Plans available for the region, this action aims to create a lasting impact on the vulnerable population of Western African nations. The Action will be implemented in direct management through grants and service contracts as well as in indirect management.In addition, this action contributes to strengthening migration management, migration policy, and migration governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. Therefore, the funds allocated to this action, will address some sub-components of the priority area 6 on Migration and forced displacement (Migration, Forced displacement and Flexible funding mechanism).[1] Core members of the TEI IYBA include: the European Commission, 11 EU Member States - BE, DE, ES, FI, FR, IT, NL, PT, MT, SE, SV, the European Investment Bank (EIB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Association of European Development Finance Institutions (EDFI).[2] The TEI on the Atlantic and Western Mediterranean route and the TEI on the Central Mediterranean route.

title.narrative: ECDC and EFSA - Fighting antimicrobial resistance and strengthening the One Health workforce in Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: ECDC and EFSA - Fighting antimicrobial resistance and strengthening the One Health workforce in Africa - This regional action is proposed in the framework of the health pillar of the Global Gateway Africa-Europe Investment Package presented at the 2022 EU-AU Summit, where the AU and EU adopted ¿A Joint Vision 2030¿ declaration with strong commintments on health security and the One Health approach. The regional TEI with Africa on sustainable health security using a One Health approach (as defined by the One Health High Level Expert Pannel (OHHLEP)[1]) has a strong EU member states (MS) support:five EU MS are involved in the TEI (EUR 309 million indicative financial contributions by Team Europe (TE)). This TEI aims to develop further the EU¿s strategic partnership with the Africa CDC, public health agency of the AU, and to align with the AU call for a New Public Health Order in Africa. Priority areas of support have been identified jointly by TE members and Africa CDC. The intention is also to substantiate the partnership with other African organizations for Health security using a One Health approach.The overall objective of this action is to contribute to sustainably strengthen health security in Africa through two main interventions:·A first component will focus on improving the surveillance, prevention and control of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) using an integrated, systems strengthening One Health approach at national, regional and continental levels. This component will thereby particularly focus on providing support to the AMR Control programme of the Africa CDC and to its effective roll-out at regional and national levels in alignment with Global standards.·A second component will focus on improving the skills and capacities of relevant professional groups from various sectors in applying the One Health approach,As this will be the second package of action financed by the European Commission under the framework of the TEI with Africa on sustainable Health Security using a One Health approach (TEIA HSOH), it consciously builds on the RIP AAP23 Action for ¿Strengthening One Health surveillance, early detection and prevention of emerging zoonotic diseases in Africa¿ and further substantiates EU¿s strategic partnership with Africa CDC in particular the existing collaboration with its European counterpart the European Center for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). Furthermore, it leverages expertise available among European and national institutes and agencies relevant to the One Health approach and TEI Member States¿ development agencies (see section 2.2 on stakeholders).[1] https://www.who.int/news/item/01-12-2021-tripartite-and-unep-support-ohhlep-s-definition-of-one-health

title.narrative: Mise en ¿uvre de solutions durables aux déplacements forcés dans les villes secondaires du Burkina Faso et du Mali à travers l¿approche territoriale intégrée.

description.narrative:
Le projet vise à établir un cadre d¿intervention efficace pour la mise à l¿échelle de solutions durables aux déplacements forcés à travers l¿approche territoriale intégrée dans les villes secondaires du Sahel Central, en se focalisant sur le Burkina Faso et le Mali. Il y a trois composantes :

1 Renforcement des capacités locales ;

2¿ Accès aux services essentiels et intégration urbaine ;

3¿ Insertion socio-économique.

Les Résultats attendus sont :

-Capacités renforcées des acteurs locaux en planification urbaine et gestion des déplacements forcés ;

-Meilleur accès aux infrastructures et services sociaux pour les PDIs et communautés hôtes ;

-Augmentation des opportunités économiques pour les populations vulnérables ; Appropriation locale et durabilité des actions mises en place.

title.narrative: Investing in Young Businesses in Africa – IYBA Invest

description.narrative:
IYBA INVEST, implemented by FMO and I&P, will consist of 3 main components:

  1. Component 1: Strengthening IPDEV Partner Funds & Portfolio Companies (EUR 16 700 000) ¿
  2. Financial Risk Capital (EUR 10 000 000 from the EU, EUR 3 000 000 from FMO MASSIF): A first-loss capital mechanism to de-risk investments and attract additional investors, including Development Finance Institutions and private investors.
  3. Technical Assistance (¿1.2M from the EU): Capacity-building support for IPDEV¿s 8 existing and 5-7 new partner funds, strengthening their investment teams and management practices. ¿ MSME Capacity Building (¿0.5M from the EU): Direct support for portfolio companies to enhance operational efficiency and business development.
  4. Management Cost (EUR 2 000 000 from the EU)

This component will enable IPDEV 1) to support the 8 existing partner funds in raising capital for second and third investment cycles and 2) to launch 5 to 7 new funds in new frontier markets. The objective is to provide 20 to 40% of the capital and convince local private sector and institutions to invest in the fund. Additionally, up to 200 MSMEs are expected to benefit from this component through equity and debt investments provided by the locally managed partner funds.

  1. Component 2: Pipeline Development & Acceleration of MSMEs (¿9.9M)
  2. Seed Funding (¿5M from the EU): A mix of repayable grants, low-interest loans, and convertible equity to help early-stage MSMEs develop their business models.
  3. Technical Assistance (¿3.9M from the EU): Customized business development services delivered by investment experts, consultants, and the Club Africain des Entrepreneurs.
  4. Management Cost (EUR 1 000 000 from the EU)

This component will support 90 high-potential MSMEs, preparing them for later-stage equity investments and sustainable growth.

  1. Component 3: Ecosystem Building & Advocacy (¿400K from the EU) Recognizing the importance of a supportive entrepreneurial environment, IYBA INVEST funds:
  2. Knowledge Sharing & Policy Advocacy: Research, case studies, and best practice dissemination to improve access to finance for MSMEs.
  3. Workshops & Stakeholder Engagement: Collaboration with local entrepreneurship support organizations (ESOs), financial institutions, and policymakers.
  4. Capacity Development for Ecosystem Players: Strengthening networks that connect MSMEs with investors, mentors, and technical advisors.

title.narrative: EU Support to Aviation Sector in Africa (SASA)

description.narrative:
The Overall Objective of this action is: to improve sustainable connectivity by air within Africa, and subsequently between Africa and the EU.

The Specific(s) Objective(s) of this action are to:

1.Promote a safe, sustainable and integrated aviation market through the development of a Single Aviation Air Transport Market (SAATM) and continued support to other forms of regional cooperation.

2.Improve and reinforce the regulatory and institutional environment to comply with international aviation rules, standards and best practices, with a focus on safety, the integration of sustainable technologies, environmental measures and climate mitigation and resilience.

3.Improve capacity to ensure safe and sustainable aviation, to support a disaster resilient air transport infrastructure that is fit for the future, to use new technology solutions while managing its associated risks and to ensure sufficient qualified aviation professionals.

4.Strengthen exchanges between EU and African aviation authorities and communities to the benefit of African aviation by promoting exchanges on regulatory issues, industrial exchanges, sharing of expert knowledge, best practices, training and demonstration activities towards a ¿continent to continent¿ partnership on aviation

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Technical Assistance to ECOWAS in Transport Governance in the West Africa under NDICI

description.narrative:
The action intends to support road transport governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. It targets transport policy and management, through consensus building on continental priorities and advocacy for the adoption of standards and regulations on one side (continental), facilitation of dialogue for exchange of good practices and concertation of efforts on the other side (regional). Both levels aim at removing hindrances to free trade and mobility. The expected impact is a reduction of costs for trade and to an ease in mobility of persons, thus fostering growth of an integrated African economy and job opportunities. The action will be implemented through geographic components, institutionally anchored at the level of the African Union Commission (AUC), the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) and the Regional Economic Communities (RECs), which are the mandated entities for the definition and implementation of continental/regional legislative frameworks.

It is proposed to structure the action on the following geographic components:

¿   Continental level (AUC, AUDA-NEPAD and the WB lead multi-donor Africa Transport Programme (SSATP))

¿      Regional component Tripartite region (EAC, COMESA, SADC)

¿      Regional component West Africa (ECOWAS) and Central Africa (CEEAC and CEMAC)

The common frame of this action provides a structured approach based on the principle of subsidiarity that will ensure overall coherence and complementarity among the different components of the action, while taking into account the different level of advancement in

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Contrat GE VERNOVA Systeme - Component A -

description.narrative: Contract related to: Contrat GE VERNOVA Systeme - Component A - - L¿objectif général du programme est de réduire les émissions de gaz à effet de serre en augmentant la part des énergies renouvelables dans le mix énergétique grâce à la mise en place et au développement du marché régional de l¿électricité.¿L'action consiste à appuyer l¿opérationnalisation du réseau interconnecté, l¿accroissement de la part des énergies renouvelables dans le mix énergétique en vue de réduire les émissions de gaz à effets de serre, et la mise en place du marché régional de l¿électricité en l¿Afrique de l¿Ouest. Ce dernier a été lancé en 2018 avec une première phase au cours de laquelle les échanges de l¿énergie électrique entre les Etats participant au marché se font essentiellement par contrats bilatéraux. Le lancement de la seconde phase, consistant à la mise en place d¿un accès ouvert au réseau électrique régional, a été retardé d¿environ deux ans notamment à cause de la pandémie du Covid-19 qui n¿a pas permis aux Etats de promulguer les règles et principes nécessaires à l¿accès à ce réseau. Malgré ces retards, le développement de ce marché en Afrique de Ouest est bien plus avancé par rapport à d¿autres régions de l¿Afrique sub-saharienne. A cet effet, l¿action appuiera les organisations régionales impliquées dans le développement du marché régional sur les plans techniques et réglementaires afin d¿améliorer et d¿intensifier la coopération énergétique régionale. Il s¿agit notamment de la Communauté Economique des Etats de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO/ECOWAS) en charge de la politique énergétique régionale et de l¿adoption des directives s¿y rapportant, le Système d¿Échanges d¿Énergie Électrique Ouest Africain (EEEOA/WAPP) en charge de la promotion et du développement des infrastructures de production et de transport d'électricité, et de la coordination des échanges d'électricité entre les États membres, l¿ Autorité Régionale de Régulation du secteur de l¿Électricité (ARREC/ERERA), en charge de la régulation du marché régional, et le Centre pour les Energies Renouvelables et l'Efficacité Energétique de la CEDEAO (CEREEC/ECREEE) en charge de la promotion et de la règlementation des énergies renouvelables. L¿action sera coordonnée avec un programme d¿appui aux planification, préparation et execution des infrastructures et investissements à vocation régionale dans le domaine de la génération d¿électricité renouvelable et des interconnexions permettant le transport d¿électricité des lieux de production de taille d¿origine renouvelable. Elle mettra en ¿uvre de l¿assistance technique, et des appuis institutionnels et de renforcement des capacités des institutions clés. L¿action sera mise en ¿uvre par les délégations de l¿UE au Bénin (cheffe de file), au Nigéria, au Ghana, et au Cap Vert en fonction de l¿optimisation de la gestion des interventions de mise en oeuvre. L¿action est alignée sur les objectifs du programme régional RIP (priorité 3: Green and climate transition) et s¿inscrit pleinement dans les objectifs de l¿initiative Global Gateways ainsi que dans l¿Africa-EU Green Energy Initiative. Elle contribuera à la réalisation des objectifs du programme de développement durable à l¿horizon 2030 des Nations Unies (en particulier en ce qui concerne l¿énergie durable et l¿éradication de la pauvreté) et contribuera désormais à la réalisation du ODD 13 (luttre contre les changements climatiques) et ODD 7 (Accès à l¿energie) ainsi ODD 9 (Industrie, innovation et infrastructures) et ODD 17 (Partenariats).

title.narrative: Biodiversity Conservation in the Greater Gola Landscape (BiCoGol)

description.narrative: Contract related to: Biodiversity Conservation in the Greater Gola Landscape (BiCoGol) - The overall objective of the NaturAfrica initiative is to tackle biodiversity loss through restoring and protecting a network of protected areas and high value ecosystems and promoting the sustainable management of surrounding landscapes whilst creating decent incomes and jobs in green sectors for local populations. Through the financing of the conservation and restoration of natural habitats and ecosystems, and the sustainable management and development of key landscapes, the EU aims also to enhance ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, soil fertility, water cycle regulation, disaster risk reduction, etc. as well as benefits for the local populations.The NaturAfrica initiative intends to work in Key Landscapes for Conservation and Development (KLCD) for (i) increasing the conservation of areas with high biodiversity value and high carbon content, and developing green economy activities by and for the neighbouring local communities and (ii) improving the inclusive governance of these landscapes to improve territorial planning, reduce conflicts and mobilise carbon finance. The transboundary nature of biological resources, their ecosystems and habitats species and communities calls for interventions at regional level through transboundary landscapes. Key transboundary landscapes were identified in six priority regions, following a wide consultation of stakeholders, including national institutions, civil society and the private sector. These regions are representatives of main African habitats with specific challenges each, and include: Congo Basin Forest ecosystems (Gabon, Burundi, Cameroon, Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Central African Republic (CAR), Uganda, South Sudan, Rwanda)   Transhumance landscapes in Central Africa (Chad, CAR, Nigeria, Cameroon)  West Africa Forests (Burkina Faso, Guinea Conakry, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Cote d¿Ivoire Ivory Coast, Nigeria)  Sudano-Sahelian savannahs of West Africa (Burkina Faso, Benin, Niger, Togo, Ghana, Senegal, Guinea)   Eastern Rift savannahs and watersheds (Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Tanzania)  Trans-frontier conservation areas of Southern Africa (Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Malawi, Mozambique, Angola, South Africa).    Relevant green economy activities include renewable energy and sustainable value chains (agriculture, livestock, fisheries, timber/non-timber forest products, tourism, ethical and sustainable fashion and circular industries). The NaturAfrica initiative complements numerous national initiatives that are foreseen in the national programmes within the same transboundary landscapes or expanding the approach to other important national landscapes and altogether, with the contribution of EU Member States (MS), is part of the large NaturAfrica flagship.This is the first phase of a 2-phased programme with a mid-term evaluation leading to a second phase in 2025. Phase 1 will initiate interventions in key landscapes, building synergies between actors and interventions, and pave the way for consolidation in phase 2.  <p

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to the Governance Structure of the Global Gateway with African Stakeholders

description.narrative:
The action will primarily support the governance capacities of key African continental institutions, especially the African Union Commission (AUC), so that they can better facilitate regional infrastructure investments through coordination, policy harmonization, and alignment of priorities between the EU and AU

This Contribution Agreement (CA) is linked to the 1.35Bo Financing Agreement in this way:

The Financing Agreement of this Action NDICI AFRICA/2021/043-421 (OPSYS number: ACT-61126) ¿ Investments in Regional Infrastructures¿ had an initial agreement of 750Mo signed between EU and AUC in 2021, followed by an SFA (Simplified Financing Agreement) of 600Mo top up signed by EC in 12/2024 and countersigned by AUC on Octobre 2025, bringing the total to 1.35Bo.

The SFA allows INTPA to commit funds for specific investment projects within three years from the date of signature of the SFA. Under the SFA, EUR 2M were allocated to the AUC to enhance its role in ensuring the needed coordination of African stakeholders and between African stakeholders and the EU in support to major continental / regional infrastructure in the area of transport, energy and digital transformation.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Cooperation in International Waters in Africa - Contribution to Trust WB Fund

description.narrative: Contract related to: Cooperation in International Waters in Africa - Contribution to Trust WB Fund - The action intends to respond to some of the many challenges which the Lake Chad Basin has been grappling with ranging from institutional reforms, climate and environmental issues, population growth, human and economic development to conflicts and instability. The action is part of the Team Europe Initiative for the management of transboundary water in Africa (TEI-TWM), especially Specific Objective 3 on improving transboundary integrated water resource management and Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems-Nexus approaches for climate change adaptation and biodiversity conservation as well as Specific Objective 2 on enabling cooperation and peer learning among transboundary basin bodies. Furthermore, the action will enhance transboundary water management to support development and regional integration within the Lake Chad Basin. The action is part of the European Commission's "Global Gateway" strategy, investing in adaptation and resilience activities in the face of climate change, promoting peace consolidation and good governance, and supporting knowledge and project development to enable large-scale cross-border investments for the common good and interest.The action will also provide a framework for coordinated action between EU Member States and EU institutions to work with their African partners at continental, regional and national levels.The implementation modalities will be through indirect management with EU Member state entrusted entities and grant to World Bank CIWA.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Assistance Technique pour la coordination des deux actions « Mieux gérer les migrations en Afrique de l'Ouest » et ¿Libérer le potentiel de la jeunesse en Afrique de l'Ouest¿ de la mesure individuelle en Afrique de l¿Ouest

description.narrative:
Le contrat d'assistance technique vise à appuyer l¿Unité géographique « Afrique de l¿Ouest » - de la DG INTPA à Bruxelles dans la coordination des deux actions complémentaires[1]: « Mieux gérer les migrations en Afrique de l'Ouest » et ¿Libérer le potentiel de la jeunesse en Afrique de l'Ouest¿.

Ces deux actions visent à améliorer la gestion des migrations et à stimuler le développement socio-économique vert dans les pays partenaires d'Afrique de l'Ouest.

Plus spécifiquement, la première action contribuera à améliorer la durabilité des systèmes de gestion des migrations dans les pays concernés, en plaçant les droits des migrants, en particulier de retour, au centre des préoccupations. La deuxième action visera à améliorer l'inclusion des jeunes, tentés par la migration ou migrants de retour, par la promotion de l¿emploi, l¿accès à la finance autour de filières de l¿économie verte.  

Les systèmes de référencement des migrants de retour soutenus par la première action devraient alimenter, en partie, le public ciblé par la deuxième action. Cette synergie est essentielle pour la réussite de ces actions.

L¿Assistance Technique aura pour tâches, entre autres :

-d¿assurer le suivi des résultats attendus, (collecte, analyse et restitution des informations), en veillant particulièrement à la complémentarité des 2 actions.

-d¿assurer la capitalisation et la diffusion des leçons apprises, et proposer, si besoin des études complémentaires pour le pilotage des actions ;

-de préparer, sur un plan logistique et de contenu, les comités de pilotage stratégiques couvrant les 2 actions ;

-d¿assurer la communication et la visibilité des actions


[1] Commission Implementing Decision C(2024)8895 of 11.12.2024 on the financing of the individual measure in favour of West Africa for 2025
