title.narrative: Activity under preparation Study and Research in Africa Component 2 + 3

description.narrative: Contract related to: Study and Research in Africa Component 2 + 3 - Study and Research in Africa aims to increase the attractiveness of African higher education offer for all types of mobile learners within Africa and to Africa. It seeks to strengthen regional integration, knowledge networks, cooperation, branding of EU-funded programmes in African Higher Education and in particular support the effective creation of the African Higher Education and Research Space (AHERS). The programme will also support the capacity building of universities/ and their affiliated research centres (RCs)[1] to interact with the wider eco-system (i.e., public and private organizations and institutions, development finance institutions, civil society organizations, etc.) in Global Gateway (GG) investment priority areas such as digital, climate, energy, transport, health, and applied research so that they play a stronger role in the skills development and innovation of value chains and build up a more relevant training offer. It will build scale, connect initiatives, and increase the relevance of projects funded through EU, as well as MS programmes and will offer an enabling facility to build up multilayer partnerships at the country level, increasing the chances of countries to access EFSD+. In the medium term, the Action will support the attractiveness of African Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) by creating a platform to disseminate information, advancing the wider ecosystem of HEIs in Africa and by supporting HEIs access to EU funds.Contributing towards the external dimension of the European Education Area¿s European Universities Strategy, the action will be structured around three components covering Opportunities, Partnerships and Targeted Support, all contributing to a transformational impact of Team Europe efforts in Africa in the field of higher education.The action is part of the Youth Mobility for Africa GG flagship initiative, which brings together several EU programmes in higher education and youth, such as Erasmus+, the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme and the Africa-EU Youth Academy under one umbrella. Supporting continental integration, providing learning opportunities both within Africa, and between Africa and Europe and reinforcing cooperation to leverage investment in knowledge and innovation to support strategic autonomy and sustainable value chains, build scale and enhance African higher education¿s relevance and responsiveness to labour market needs in partner countries, while also creating green growth, are core elements of the GG Africa-Europe Investment Package and are the aims of the Youth Mobility for Africa GG Flagship Initiative.Concretely, the Action will focus on three specific objectives/components:1.Opportunities: Support African HEIs to be more visible and accessible, strengthen their profile, branding and disseminate targeted information, attract mobile learners, researchers and staff and sharing of data and information.HEIs will be supported in positioning themselves in fields in which they excel, and which can also highlight the linkages with EU investments at country or regional level. This positioning will help mobile learners, researchers and staff make informed decisions about their choice of studies, work and location and build up the internationalisation and marketing of countries offer. The lack of access to information and data is a significant barrier for mobile learners, researchers, HEIs in Africa and therefore SDG4 and SDG9, creating more inequalities in the continent and hampering mobility across the region. title.narrative: Regional Energy Governance and Information System for West Africa (REGIS WA)

description.narrative:
To contribute to the overall objective and specific objective 1, the project will support ECOWAS through the implementation of two components:

  1. Component 1 - Support for the implementation and monitoring/follow-up of the regional energy policy, for the transposition in the Member States of the regional directives and the regional energy action plan, and for liaison with the African Union (AU).


  1. Component 2 - Support for the development of ECOWAS¿s energy statistical system. Improvement of capacities and support to Member States for the collection and production of statistical energy data, monitoring of the collection and production of statistical data, provision of equipment, software and trainings at the level of ECOWAS and its Member States, strengthening collaboration with African Energy Commission (AFREC[1]) on energy statistics, and integrating a gender-sensitive approach where possible.


[1] AFREC operates under the African Union, whose main headquarters are in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, but AFREC itself is based in Algiers

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to the African Governance, Peace & Security Architectures

description.narrative: Contract related to: Support to the African Governance, Peace & Security Architectures - This Action seeks to contribute to the above joint principles as well as the African Union¿s (AU) Agenda 2063 and the ¿Silencing the Guns¿ flagship initiative (2020-2030). The latter¿s objective is to end all wars, civil conflicts, gender-based violence and violent conflicts, and prevent genocide by supporting: i) the APSA as the main framework for promoting peace, security and stability in Africa, and ii) the AGA in responding to the AU vision to promote and protect human and people¿s rights, consolidate democratic institutions, good governance and the rule of law on the continent. In addition, the Action further contributes to SDG 5: Gender Equality; SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions; and SDG 17: Partnership for the Goals. Specifically, this Action will support the African Governance Architecture (AGA) and African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA) to help prevent conflict and enhance participatory democratic governance across the African continent. This will be done by engaging with the AU Commission (AUC) and its continental organs, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and AU Member States (AUMS) at political, policy and operational levels. It represents a more focused support to the AU Governance, Peace and Security (GPS) Architectures, while continuing the EU¿s political commitment to the continent in the spirit of shared African-European priorities.Indeed, this Action proposes to gather formerly separate support programmes to APSA (peace and security) and AGA (governance)[1] under one conceptual roof by building on lesson learnt and wider consultations with the AU at various levels. With a planned budget of EUR 40 million over four years managed by the EUD to the AU, it will address key thematic issues of mutual interest and reinforce the GPS nexus. The Action responds to ongoing major AU reforms, notably i) the effective transformation of the Political Affairs, Peace, and Security Department (AU-PAPS) towards more integrated approaches to conflicts and their political root causes by addressing the Governance, Peace and Security (GPS) nexus; ii) the operationalisation of the AU Peace Fund; and iii) the rationalisation of the AU treaty-based human rights organs. Engagement with Pan-African civil society networks (CSOs), think tanks and academia is mainstreamed to build on positive results of previous programmes. To ensure the sustainability of GPS efforts, the need to engage with youth and women is widely recognised as instrumental to maximising the demographic dividend.

description.narrative: Contract related to: IYBA business Afrique de l'Ouest - The goal of this Action is to improve the inclusion of youth in resilient and climate-smart green economic transitions that address the root causes of irregular migration in West African countries. It complements the ¿Managing Migration Better in Western Africa¿ Action which aims at strengthening migration management. A comprehensive approach including skills development, improved access to finance for Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) notably through diaspora investment and support to value chains development is expected to influence individual decision-making processes and potentially reduce migration aspirations by providing better local prospects. It is also expected to help and facilitate sustainable reintegration. More specifically, this Action ¿Unleashing the Potential of Youth in West Africa¿ will contribute to green skills¿ alignment with the private sector needs (1.1), promote diaspora¿s investments (2.1), as well as enhance access to finance and technical support for green business growth (2.2). Job creation will also be supported through the development of targeted green, circular and low-carbon value chains (2.3).This action contributes to the implementation of the Youth Action Plan. To the extent possible, this action will build upon and benefit from Global Gateway investments in the targeted countries, contributing to strengthening the local economy, job creation and markets aligned with the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Investing in Young Businesses in Africa[1], the Regional Team Europe Initiative Opportunity-driven Skills and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Africa as well as the two migration-related regional TEIs[2]. Conversely, it will contribute to building the skills required and achieving the targeted transformational impact of the Global Gateway strategy, and its commitments to address gender equality, by maximizing its impact on the relevant ecosystems with a 360 approach. The transition to green growth is mainstreamed throughout the action. By aligning with the Nationally Determined Contributions and the National Adaptation Plans available for the region, this action aims to create a lasting impact on the vulnerable population of Western African nations. The Action will be implemented in direct management through grants and service contracts as well as in indirect management.In addition, this action contributes to strengthening migration management, migration policy, and migration governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. Therefore, the funds allocated to this action, will address some sub-components of the priority area 6 on Migration and forced displacement (Migration, Forced displacement and Flexible funding mechanism).[1] Core members of the TEI IYBA include: the European Commission, 11 EU Member States - BE, DE, ES, FI, FR, IT, NL, PT, MT, SE, SV, the European Investment Bank (EIB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Association of European Development Finance Institutions (EDFI).[2] The TEI on the Atlantic and Western Mediterranean route and the TEI on the Central Mediterranean route.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation PRO-JUST: strengthening the criminal Justice chain in PALOP-TL countries

description.narrative: The Action aims at contribution to peace and justice trough the promotion of stronger institutions and the rule of law. Emphasis will be placed on the reduction of corruption, money laundering, and organized crime with a focus on dru trafficking, through prevention, investigation, and criminalization to improve accountability and compliance with good governance principles. The Action builds upon the results obtained with the programme PACED and will include new components (digitalization) and involve other actors (media and Civil society) and adopt a new strategy priming for the materialization of the knowledge gathered in the past decade. The intervention will focus on i) drafting legislation, strategies and plans on corruption, money laundering and organized cirme; ii) improving skills of key state and non state actors involved in the fight against corruption, ml and organized crime; iii) operationalize strategic means (including digital) for the criminal justice actors and strengthen their mandate.

To ensure the sustainability of GPS efforts, the need to engage with youth and women is widely recognised as instrumental to maximising the demographic dividend.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation AFD - GG Sustainable Infrastructure Projects Preparation Facility

description.narrative:
AFD Global Gateway Investment Preparation Facility is an essential instrument to facilitate the construction of a pipeline of projects to scale up the Global Gateway, even beyond the current MFF. The need to prepare quality, bankable projects is one of the key pre-requisites for increasing investments in infrastructure in emerging and developing countries. In Sub-Saharan Africa, slow deployment of strategic and sustainable infrastructures is not only due to the scarcity of financial resources, but also to the low availability of projects that are based on international standards and best practices. Emerging markets tend to rush into procurement without proper understanding of project costs and impacts. To address this challenge, adequate project preparation is key as it ensures alignment of public sector needs and private investors¿ engagement.

The facility would cover the financing of: pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, preliminary and detailed design studies, preparation studies; assessments of climate risk, vulnerability, ecosystem services, nature-based solutions; identification of innovative finance, including green finance, e.g. payments for ecosystem services; elaboration of tendering documentation including for Operation & Maintenance, that is crucial to attract and secure potential international private operators; transaction advisory, which aims at attracting private stakeholders in relevant projects when feasible; TA supporting governments, regulators, utilities and sectors¿ ecosystems in the framework of project preparation and implementation.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation CDP - Technical Assistance for the implementation of budgetary guarantee - RISE

description.narrative: Contract related to: CDP - Technical Assistance for the implementation of budgetary guarantee - RISE - NDICI - Global Europe (GE) Regulation[1] established EFSD+ and related budgetary guarantees as a means to support investments and increase access to financing in partner countries. Technical Assistance (TA) is an important part of EFSD+ that will enable implementation of budgetary guarantees in the global context. In accordance with that, Commission adopted three Decisions regarding Regional Multi-Annual Indicative Programmes (MIPs) 2021-2027 for Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), Asia and the Pacific (AP), and the Americas and the Caribbean (AC),[2] confirming funding for EFSD+ TA activities. The overall objective of the Action is to foster sustainable and inclusive economic, environmental and social development, and poverty reduction in partner countries, through investments in the following sectors: MSMEs; agriculture, biodiversity, forests; sustainable cities including sanitation and water sector; human development and sustainable finance.The specific objective of the Action is to facilitate deployment of EFSD+ budgetary guarantees that are used to de-risk bankable projects with a developmental impact and crowd-in private sector financing. The innovative character of the guarantees makes the TA indispensable to develop a pipeline of transactions, as well as to facilitate the roll-out of the financial products, while ensuring the expected development impact. It will be particularly important to enable the operationalisation of the guarantees in fragile, Least Developed Countries (LDCs) context, ensuring that distribution of EFSD+ investments is balanced. The Action is fully in line with the EU and partner countries¿ priorities and supports, directly or indirectly, an overwhelming majority of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and with cross-cutting issues such as gender equality, human rights, climate adaptation and environmental protection. title.narrative: Activity under preparation ODEBAC - EFCA - Appui au controle et surveillance des peches industrielles en Afrique Centrale

description.narrative: Contract related to: ODEBAC - EFCA - Appui au controle et surveillance des peches industrielles en Afrique Centrale - Cette action constitue la première initiative régionale d¿envergure en Afrique centrale, abordant la préservation et la valorisation des espaces et ressources marins/côtiers. Les nécessités dans ce domaine sont donc multiples. La structuration des filières liées à l¿économie bleue (EB) est encore très faible et les échanges régionaux sont limités. Les systèmes nationaux de conservation de la biodiversité marine sont très hétérogènes : tandis que le Gabon développe l¿initiative Gabon Bleu, le Congo et Sao Tomé n¿ont engagé que récemment le processus de création de leurs premières aires marines protégées (AMP). Il conviendra de renforcer ces créations par des mesures concrètes de gestion de ces AMP. Les enjeux côtiers (accroissement des populations, développement de l¿habitat et de zones industrielles/portuaires, absence de gestion des déchets notamment plastiques, etc.) s¿intensifient, affectant la sécurité des investissements côtiers, menacés par les risques naturels, dont l¿érosion. En fonction des besoins identifiés, trois objectifs spécifiques à la fois complémentaires et interdépendants sont proposés: (i) gouvernance internationale, régionale et nationale de l¿océan ; (ii) développement de l¿EB et amélioration de la durabilité des pêches, incluant un fond de promotion de l¿innovation en matière d¿EB ; (iii) préservation du capital naturel et de la biodiversité marins et côtiers. Le renforcement de la gouvernance régionale visera les capacités de facilitation inter Etats (éventuellement au niveau de la CEEAC) pour le suivi de la mise en ¿uvre des engagements des Etats, notamment auprès des accords multilatéraux sur l¿environnement (AME). Ce volet inclura également le renforcement des capacités régionales de recherche (« Science to Policy »), et le développement du capital humain, au travers de formations spécialisées. La question de l¿aménagement résilient des territoires côtiers sera abordée au travers d¿une planification spatiale stratégique régionale de la zone côtière et de la mer côtière (identification des secteurs côtiers à risques). Ce volet inclura également une opération pilote de dépollution basée sur la mobilisation sociale et la mise en place de partenariats public-privés. La promotion de l¿EB inclura un appui régional au développement des stratégies nationales et à des plans d¿investissement EB. La promotion de l¿EB sera supportée par un fonds régional d¿appel à projets, ciblant les initiatives innovantes de la société civile, des collectivités, et du secteur privé, en particulier portées par les femmes/filles et les jeunes, dans toute leur diversité (y compris d¿autres personnes en situation de vulnérabilité), ou visant à accompagner leur professionnalisation. L¿amélioration de la durabilité des pêches reposera sur des actions de coordination de la lutte contre la pêche illicite, non déclarée et non réglementée (INN), la promotion d¿une gestion coordonnée des stocks halieutiques partagés, et la consolidation des filières. La conservation/restauration de la biodiversité s¿appuiera sur la mise à niveau des dispositifs de conservation marine à l¿échelle régionale, ciblant en particulier les aires marines protégées (AMP). La ratification et la mise en ¿uvre du Traité `Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction¿ (BBNJ ¿ adopté formellement le 19 juin 2023) seront également appuyées. La professionnalisation (recyclage) d¿agents des administrations des différents pays en matière de conservation marine et d¿écotourisme bleu est également intégrée dans cette composante. L¿action aborde de manière transversale et intégrée les dimensions biodiversité et climat.L¿action repose sur plusieurs principes : (i) subsidiarité et valeur ajoutée régionale des activités envisagé

description.narrative: Contract related to: Borderlands IV - Les zones frontalières d¿Afrique subsaharienne sont fréquemment caractérisées par des mouvements de population, de bétail, de marchandises, et de ressources naturelles. Ces zones, lorsqu'elles sont associées à l'insécurité, aux conflits, aux impacts du changement climatique, à la pauvreté ou à un abandon par rapport à l'État central, peuvent progressivement se muer en foyers d'instabilité. Ceci est notamment le cas des territoires riverains de la frontière entre le Mali et la Mauritanie, où l¿escalade des violences perpétrées par les groupes armés non étatiques au Mali a causé un nouvel afflux d¿arrivants maliens et de retournés mauritaniens. Dans la sous-région des Grands lacs, les tensions dans les zones frontalières sont souvent exacerbées par le développement des groupes armés, les difficultés d¿accès aux services sociaux de base, l¿absence de dialogue politique et le faible progrès économique et développement global de la population. La guerre civile au Soudan et l¿afflux de personnes déplacées au Sud Soudan ont contribué à aggraver les tensions dans la zone frontalière déjà en proie de récurrents conflits inter et intra-ethniques violents, potentiel pôle de déstabilisation pour les deux pays.Cette action vise à prévenir et atténuer l¿impact des conflits locaux en améliorant la résilience et la cohésion sociale des communautés transfrontalières. Pour ce faire, une approche intégrée à la sécurité sera appliquée, en promouvant la coopération transfrontalière en tant que levier de paix. Il y aura trois fenêtres subrégionales: Sahel, Grand Lacs, Abyei (Sudan/South Sudan)

description.narrative: Contract related to: EU-Ghana Pact for Skills II: Support to the Transformation of the TVET System in Ghana - The goal of this Action is to improve the inclusion of youth in resilient and climate-smart green economic transitions that address the root causes of irregular migration in West African countries. It complements the ¿Managing Migration Better in Western Africa¿ Action which aims at strengthening migration management. A comprehensive approach including skills development, improved access to finance for Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) notably through diaspora investment and support to value chains development is expected to influence individual decision-making processes and potentially reduce migration aspirations by providing better local prospects. It is also expected to help and facilitate sustainable reintegration. More specifically, this Action ¿Unleashing the Potential of Youth in West Africa¿ will contribute to green skills¿ alignment with the private sector needs (1.1), promote diaspora¿s investments (2.1), as well as enhance access to finance and technical support for green business growth (2.2). Job creation will also be supported through the development of targeted green, circular and low-carbon value chains (2.3).This action contributes to the implementation of the Youth Action Plan. To the extent possible, this action will build upon and benefit from Global Gateway investments in the targeted countries, contributing to strengthening the local economy, job creation and markets aligned with the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Investing in Young Businesses in Africa[1], the Regional Team Europe Initiative Opportunity-driven Skills and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Africa as well as the two migration-related regional TEIs[2]. Conversely, it will contribute to building the skills required and achieving the targeted transformational impact of the Global Gateway strategy, and its commitments to address gender equality, by maximizing its impact on the relevant ecosystems with a 360 approach. The transition to green growth is mainstreamed throughout the action. By aligning with the Nationally Determined Contributions and the National Adaptation Plans available for the region, this action aims to create a lasting impact on the vulnerable population of Western African nations. The Action will be implemented in direct management through grants and service contracts as well as in indirect management.In addition, this action contributes to strengthening migration management, migration policy, and migration governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. Therefore, the funds allocated to this action, will address some sub-components of the priority area 6 on Migration and forced displacement (Migration, Forced displacement and Flexible funding mechanism).[1] Core members of the TEI IYBA include: the European Commission, 11 EU Member States - BE, DE, ES, FI, FR, IT, NL, PT, MT, SE, SV, the European Investment Bank (EIB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Association of European Development Finance Institutions (EDFI).[2] The TEI on the Atlantic and Western Mediterranean route and the TEI on the Central Mediterranean route.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Social Protection Systems Strengthening - AAP 2025

description.narrative: Contract related to: Social Protection Systems Strengthening - AAP 2025 - The Social Protection Systems Strengthening Action in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is aimed at building inclusive, resilient, and sustainable social protection (SP) systems. This action supports the EU¿s Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for SSA under Priority Area 1: Human Development, focusing on reducing poverty, promoting gender equality, ensuring decent work, and advancing social inclusion. The action aligns with key African Union (AU) frameworks, including Agenda 2063, which underscores social protection as a critical component of economic stability and integration. It also supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1, No Poverty, Target 1.3.SSA¿s social protection systems face numerous structural challenges. With fewer than 20% of people in the region covered by any form of social protection, factors such as high levels of informality, limited fiscal resources, administrative capacity, inadequate benefit levels and fragmented policies contribute to substantial coverage gaps. These limitations, combined with pressures from recurring crises¿including the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change impacts, migration, economic instability and fragility contexts¿necessitate social protection systems that are adaptable, responsive, and accessible to vulnerable populations. Inadequate SP coverage leaves marginalized groups without necessary support systems, deepening poverty and widening social inequalities.A regional approach to SP across SSA offers substantial added value, fostering alignment of policy standards, enabling cross-border crisis-responsive measures, promoting portability of rights while facilitating exchange of experiences across countries. A regional approach can reduce disparities that lead to migration pressures and economic inequality while enhancing countries¿ abilities to respond cohesively to regional crises. The coordinated framework facilitates the exchange of best practices and collaborative learning among SSA countries. Collaboration at the regional level is also integral to achieving the ambitions of Agenda 2063, which emphasizes social protection as fundamental for economic integration, social cohesion, and sustainable development.This action has a clear results chain aimed at achieving the overall impact through specific objectives and outputs.The overall objective is to support and strengthen national social protection systems in SSA by leveraging a region-to-region approach. The ultimate aim is to enhance resilience, reduce poverty, and promote equitable economic growth aligned with the sustainable development agenda.The specific objectives are:Support Social Protection System Strengthening: This objective focuses on building SSA countries¿ capacity to design and implement robust, inclusive SP systems. Capacity building and regional knowledge-sharing initiatives will improve social protection governance, sustainable financing, and integrated policy frameworks for inclusive and shock-responsive social protection systems in participating countries.<span style="color: rgb(13, 13

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Borderlands V - West Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: Borderlands V - West Africa - Border regions across Sub-Saharan Africa are characterised by complex, overlapping dynamics of fragility, where weak governance, insecurity, displacement and migratory movements, and limited economic opportunities intersect with environmental degradation and demographic pressures. These cross-border settings often experience the spillover of conflict, violent extremism, and illicit trade, while remaining vital corridors for mobility, trade, and cooperation. Addressing these challenges requires integrated, conflict-sensitive approaches that combine security, governance, and socio-economic resilience.The Action takes an integrated approach connecting peace, security, governance, and sustainable development to address fragility stemming from governance deficits, resource pressures, demographic trends, and climate change across the targeted regions. It also tackles displacement and migratory challenges, contributing to the EU¿s migration agenda through stability, inclusion, and sustainable solutions in priority areas.The overall objective of this Action is to prevent and mitigate instability and the impact of local conflicts in border areas. This subject was identified in Priority Area 2 (Democratic Governance, Peace and Security, Culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The Action is in line with SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, as well as No poverty (SDG 1); Zero hunger (SDG 2); Reduce inequality (SDG 10), Gender equality (SDG 5), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8) and Climate action (SDG 13).The action will target four different geographical windows: (i) border areas between Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, and Guinea (West Africa window) which face structural weaknesses worsened by climate change and natural resources degradation trafficking, and violent extremism. In this region, the Action will aim to enhance stability and resilience in border areas through inclusive economic growth, sustainable resource management, and coordinated action against cross-border trafficking; (ii) border areas between Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) - Uganda (Great Lakes window), where armed groups, natural resource exploitation, and weak law enforcement shape regional dynamics. In this area, the Action will enhance stability and resilience by addressing the drivers of violent extremism and fostering inclusive socio-economic development; (iii) border areas between Kenya, Somalia, Ethiopia and South Sudan (Horn of Africa window), where climate change jeopardises the main economic activities thus worsening inter-communal and cross-border conflict. In this region, the Action will aim to enhance peace, resilience, and sustainable growth in cross-border communities (including those affected by displacement) through strengthened conflict management, sustainable natural resource use, and inclusive, climate-smart economic development; (iv) border areas between Malawi and Mozambique (Southern Africa window) impacted by radicalisation within vulnerable communities and the spill over of terrorism and organised crime. Here, the Action will enhance institutional cooperation and community resilience to prevent conflict and radicalisation, fostering inclusive and secure border environments.The Action will be carried out in complementarity and coordination with both EU and non-EU funded actions at national and regional level, including relevant Regional Economic Communities and other regional stakeholders. This would include relevant TEIs, nexus actions, green deal sector related actions, as well as actions addressing terrorism spillover.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Africa - EU Space Parnership Programme - AESPP Boost

description.narrative: Contract related to: Africa - EU Space Parnership Programme - AESPP Boost - The Action will contribute to make more effective use of space technologies, based on the EU Space programme such as Copernicus and Galileo, through the development of services and applications focusing on most pressing challenges related to the green transition sectors.The Action will build and capitalise on ongoing EU supported space related programmes such as GMES&Africa, ClimSA and ASECNA-JPO.Focus will be given on operationalise Earth Observation (EO) and Satellite Navigation (SatNav) based services. Specific attention will be paid to complementarities and added-value of joining the use of these two space technologies in selected sectors of intervention.The sectors of intervention will be selected according to Africa priorities in the green transition and building on ongoing programmes and the longstanding partnership with Africa, strengthening synergies of combining EO and SatNav technologies. The Action may therefore focus on Land and Water Management; Marine and Coastal area; Agriculture and Food security; and Climate change. However, new topic(s) may be added to the intervention (i.e. urban planning). During the formulation phase, he sectors will be confirmed. In addition, a potential focus for sustainable development for SIDS will be explored.Support will be given to the African organisations that are developing the space-based services but also to public institutions that utilise those products and services to improve decision-making processes and to digital private sector as to develop the African space ecosystem. The programme will foster synergies with TEI and other regional and national programmes. Further to that, the Action will explore how to better support national priorities in the green transition areas by strengthening the link between the regional and national dimensions.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Africa Multi-Country Telecom Network Rollout (Vodacom)

description.narrative: Contract related to: Africa Multi-Country Telecom Network Rollout (Vodacom) - Through strategic infrastructure investments, this Action seeks to foster Mozambique¿s digital transformation through widening affordable connectivity. It positions the EU as a strategic partner in Mozambique¿s digital sector, leveraging European expertise in sustainable connectivity, trusted data systems and digital governance. EU engagement brings strong added value by mobilising private investment (with clear opportunities for EU trusted vendors), promoting European standards and ensuring an inclusive and sustainable approach to digitalisation in the country. Anchored within Team Europe's broader cooperative framework, this initiative will become a fundamental part of the Digital Economy Package (DEP), symbolizing a milestone in EU-Mozambique bilateral relations. It underscores a political commitment to boost European investments, aligning with Team Europe's support for digital transformation through initiatives like Italy¿s Piano Mattei, and implemented through a blending project with a pillar assessed entity, to be identify during the design phase. The EU's contribution is crucial in overcoming a defined market failure: the limited commercial viability of network rollout due to low revenue streams and affordability constraints in underserved areas. By providing financial support, the project bridges viability gaps, enables connectivity for excluded communities, and contributes to unlocking access to essential services and mobile banking.

description.narrative: Contract related to: Southern Africa/Angola/Lobito Corridor Logistics - The Opportunity-driven Skills and VET in Africa Action intends to complement VET and skills development programmes financed at country level by helping these orient towards concrete employment opportunities created by (EU) investments, trade, (regional) value chain development, grants and other market dynamics in partner countries. The Action is a key element under the EU-Africa Global Gateway Investment Package announced at the 2022 EU-Africa-Summit, supporting sectors that are part of the package. At regional level, the action consists of five building blocksA Technical Assistance (TA) facility providing support based on requests from EU Delegations, EU Member States or private sector organisations to identify employment opportunities and required skills needs around flagship initiatives and translate findings in targeted recommendations for VET system support responsive to identified employment opportunities.Regional exchange on Public-Private-Partnerships to promote opportunity-driven VET and skills development in SSA, and to create a space to allow for practical exchange between public and private stakeholders on active partnerships. This includes a linkage to relevant Erasmus+ financed actions on capacity building for PPP in VET to strengthen EU-Africa engagement on skills.A Competitive Funding mechanism to finance regional and multi-country VET initiatives in support of (regional) value chains that complement country MIPs, as well as actions that more generally support this paradigm shift of reverse engineering VET in function of employment opportunities market dynamics create.A flexible funding mechanism, which allows for country-driven funding for opportunity-driven skills development and training linked to GG investments with concrete employment opportunities.A continental Africa-Europe coordination mechanism for knowledge sharing, to deliver agile skills intelligence, innovation, dialogue, and advisory support alongside the African Continental Free Trade Area (ACfTA) and the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), informing and valorising Global Gateway priority sectors and priority value chains.The Action is aligned with the priority areas of the regional MIP for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021 ¿ 2027 (Priority area 1: Human Development, Result 2.2. and Priority area 5: Sustainable Growth and Decent Jobs, Result 3.2.) and SDGs 8 Decent work and economic growth, 4 Quality education, 5 Gender equality, 10 Reduced inequalities and 17 Partnerships.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Top Up. Improving Cameroon`s migration management capacity and cooperation

description.narrative:
This projet aims to strengthen migration governance in Cameroon through the development of a comprehensive national migration policy, while enhancing institutional capacities for the safe, dignified, and effective return, readmission, and sustainable reintegration (RRR) of migrants and ensuring long-term socioeconomic integration.

Objectifs:

1. Specific Objective: Support to National Authorities to Develop Cooperation with the EU and Build National Capacities for the Management of Return, Readmission, and Reintegration.

2.   Specific Objective: Support Community-Based Activities Addressing Root Causes of Irregular Migration and Facilitating Reintegration.

3.    Specific Objective: Support the Formulation of the First National Migration Policy.

By aligning national efforts with global and African Union frameworks, this project supports the development of a comprehensive migration policy and addresses critical return, readmission, and reintegration challenges, enhancing Cameroon¿s capacity to manage migration flows effectively and sustainably.

description.narrative: Contract related to: Technical Assistance to EU-Africa Trade and Investment Agreements (EPA Facility) and Customs Cooperation - SummaryThis Action is central to the Global Gateway (GG) Africa-Europe Investment Package (GG AEIP) roll-out and contributes to the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) in support to African economic integration towards the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), a flagship objective of the African Union¿s Agenda 2063 and a major priority for the European Union (EU). The EU has built a strategic approach in support of intra-African and EU-Africa investment and trade by anchoring its support on key priority areas (i.e. trade in goods, services, trade facilitation, competition, digital trade) of free trade and investment agreements at continental, regional and national levels (AfCFTA, RECs, EU Bilateral and Regional - EPAs), as well as key value chains, and trade corridors.To complement this support, this Action will focus on four additional key enablers of EU-Africa and intra-Africa sustainable trade and investment that will be concretely implemented through four different projects, some of which are a continuation of existing support, namely:1. Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) protection and enforcement are key for investment and innovation facilitation and protection. Support will contribute to the harmonisation, creation, registration, management, utilisation and administration, protection, and enforcement of IPRs in Africa. To this end, the Action will focus on continental, regional and national: (i) African IP legal and policy frameworks (i.e. AfCFTA IP Protocol, the Continental Strategy for Geographical Indications (GIs) of the African Union, Regional and national IP regulations, etc.); (ii) African IP administration capacities; (iii) African and EU productive sector support, with a particular focus on SMEs (i.e. the Africa IP SME Helpdesk); and (iv) Support to the elaboration and implementation of the post 2023 Continental Strategy for GIs of the African Union.2. EU-Africa Trade and Investment Agreements, with the main objective to boost sustainable EU ¿ Africa trade and investment flows and strengthen the trade and investment capacities of African partners through the design of a flexible on-demand facility that can offer ad-hoc support to countries with whom the EU has concluded trade and investment agreements (EPAs, SIFAs, etc.). This facility will also provide complementary technical support needed for alignment with EU regulations and directives having an impact on EU-Africa trade and investment, such as the relevant policies adopted in the framework of the European Green Deal and the EU Circular Economy Action Plan or the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D).3. Customs Cooperation, a main enabler at the basis of all trade. The Action proposes a follow up to the existing successful programmes `Harmonizing the classification of goods based on WCO standards to enhance African trade¿ (EU-WCO Harmonised System (HS) Programme, 2018-2024) and `Implementation and application of Rules of Origin (RoO)¿ (EU-WCO RoO Programme, 2021-2025). The scope of the new programme is to enhance African trade by further developing and implementing key customs pillars of the AfCFTA and of other regional agreements through dedicated technical capacity support to (i) Harmonised System (HS), (ii) Rules of Origin (RoO), and (iii) Valuation. 4. Investment Facilitation, a crucial soft enabler to accompany Global Gateway hard investments, ensuring that they are conducive to sustainable and inclusive development. description.narrative: Contract related to: Fit For Market - Africa 2030 - The Action aims to enable agribusinesses, MSMEs, farmer groups, and farmers to maintain and improve access to domestic, regional and EU market, benefitting from the AfCFTA commitments, EPAs and other preferential trade arrangements with the EU (main focus on fruit and vegetables, but open to other agri-food value chains). The Action will increase the resilience, fairness (inclusiveness), competitiveness and sustainability of a selected number of agricultural value chains, through the development and adoption of safe and sustainable practices, skills and technologies, as well as boosting equal access to finance and investments, which in turn are expected to contribute to decent job creation and the sustainable and inclusive transformation of the agri-food sector in the target countries. Skilled and resilient agri-food operators from both private and public sectors are key in order to promote inclusive, sustainable, low carbon and (climate) resilient agricultural value chains. In this context, the action will focus on two mutually reinforcing components: 1) Continental facility; 2) Country facility.Component 1 (continental facility ¿ Sustainable horticulture in SSA) Important challenges and bottlenecks are impairing the competitiveness of the horticultural sector in Africa. The enabling environment struggles to effectively support the private sector by providing adequate and cost-effective services such as extension, regulation, certification, logistics and in general enabling a predictable and stable business environment.This component seeks to strengthen national horticultural production and distribution systems across SSA countries. This means supporting agri-food MSMEs (including farmer groups and cooperatives), local services providers in the horticultural sector and the national competent authorities, to strengthen their capabilities and support a strong African horticultural sector. By improving access to domestic, regional and international markets for fruit and vegetable value chains, as well as access to finance and investment, this component will create an operational and enabling platform that contributes to the overall transformation of food systems in SSA within a sustainable framework. Component 1 will also seek the development of partnerships with African educational institutions to develop massive open vocational capacity building. Component 2 (Selected country-agrifood value chain facility)The European Union continues to be a highly appealing market for African agricultural goods, while intra-continental exchanges are also gaining importance. Agri-food exports from SSA economies to the EU are of pivotal importance in terms of generating income and employment, and key contributors towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Nonetheless, meeting evolving EU Regulations and Standards remains a major and challenging determinant for market access, as well as competitiveness. title.narrative: Activity under preparation SAFE SEAS AFRICA (Western Indian Ocean) - Grant to IOC (extension)

description.narrative: Contract related to: SAFE SEAS AFRICA (Western Indian Ocean) - Grant to IOC (extension) - Over the last decade, illicit maritime activities have had a destabilizing effect in the countries along the Gulf of Guinea (GoG) and the Western Indian Ocean (WIO), weakening local communities¿ resilience, states¿ institutions and economies and regions¿ stability. While maritime threats are varied, coastal countries in the WIO and GoG face similar challenges, among which piracy, armed robbery and illicit trafficking at sea, and illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing. The groups behind some of these illicit activities have been exploiting jurisdictions and law enforcement gaps and weaknesses, as well as lack of coordination among actors involved in the fight against these threats, both at strategic and at operational level. This contributes to increase the insecurity of the waters in the two regions and jeopardise sustainable development as well as rights of local communities. This Action has the overall objective of contributing to enhancing maritime security and safety in Africa. The Action will address the causes of insecurity at sea and contribute to the overall coordination among actors involved in the fight against maritime criminality. This subject was identified in the Priority Area 2 (Democratic governance, peace and security, and culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The Action is in line with SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions and DAC Markers on maritime security and trafficking, legal and judicial development, advanced technical and managerial training, and governance.In both regions, the Specific Objectives of the Action are: increasing the capacities and capabilities of national maritime law enforcement agencies to prevent, respond and investigate maritime crimes; building up the capacities of judicial bodies to prevent, repress, respond and adjudicate maritime crimes, enhancing legal finish; strengthening the capacities of the maritime security architectures in the two regions (the Yaoundé Architecture in the GoG and the Regional Maritime Security Architecture in the WIO); and, developing coordination and cooperation at intra-national/inter-agency and inter-regional level. The different outputs and activities of the Action are organised by geographical area.To achieve the overall objective, an integrated approach will be applied, covering capacity building and mentoring, and promoting communication and coordination among national, international and regional partners. The Action will be carried out in complementarity with both EU and non-EU funded actions at national and regional level, including relevant Regional Economic Communities and other regional stakeholders.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation West Africa/Guinea-Bissau/TVET&Agribusiness-Agronegócio Promoção das Cadeias de Valor-Extension

description.narrative: The action will focus on the cashew nut value chain, which presents significant untapped potential for creating added value, expanding market-share, drive local economic growth and benefitting local economy ¿ including the potential for job creation - given that less than 10% of cashew nuts production is processed domestically. Limited skills and expertise, entrepreneurial capacity, together with lack of competitive (and insufficient) local processing facilities and inadequate infrastructure, fragmented market linkages, hinder productivity, quality, market access and competitiveness in the global market. The action will notably contribute to close critical skills gaps and reduce mismatches along this value chain, focusing on both short and long-term employability and entrepreneurship. It will actively engage with private sector players in the cashew nut industry to ensure that training provision matches and is fully aligned with skills and competencies demanded by the domestic, regional and international labour market. It will target young people, women, and rural populations, to support value-added processing, technical skills, quality control, market development and compliance practices, (exported-oriented logistics( logistics and supply chain management competencies for the export of high-quality and competitive cashew products. It will also target MSMEs, cooperatives and trade associations to strengthen their capacities on business development and financial management and market positioning.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Renforcement du système d'Etat civil

description.narrative: Contract related to: Renforcement du système d'Etat civil - The aim of the proposed intervention ¿ the Flexible Mechanism, hereinafter ¿the Mechanism¿ ¿ is to maximise EU leverage in migration discussions vis-à-vis Sub-Saharan African counterparts, based on a flexible and incentives-based approach while also respecting policy coherence for development, as well as foreign policy objectives of the Union. Through the financing of migration-related cooperation projects, the EU aims to expand its external engagement with African partners on migration and forced displacement. In line with the most recent developments in both internal and external EU migration policy, including the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, the Mechanism will support the development and reinforcement of strong, balanced, comprehensive and mutually beneficial partnerships and programs with relevant countries of origin, transit and destination of migrants and forcibly displaced people. The action will also contribute to the Team Europe Initiative for a Comprehensive migration approach in the Maghreb, Sahel and West African countries in the Atlantic / Western Mediterranean route and to the Team Europe Initiative on Central Mediterranean migration route.Interventions will be weighed against the specific migration and/or forced displacement situation of each partner country or region, the nature of the overall dialogue with the EU, and the partner country¿s level of engagement with the EU on migration. This assessment will be done in coordination with EU Member States. In this regard, several factors, inter alia, can be taken into consideration, notably whether : (i) the country is engaging or showing willingness to engage in fighting against migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, as well as stemming irregular migration; (ii) the country is stepping up its efforts to host migrants and/or displaced people, and people in need of international protection, in a dignified way, in line with international and EU standards; (iii) the country/region is reinforcing capacities on migration management and governance, including on management of forced displacement flows, in the context of its partnership with the EU ; (iv) the country is showing a substantial and sustained cooperation with the EU and its MS on return, readmission and sustainable reintegration; (v) and/or the country/region is willing to cooperate with the EU and its MS to support well-managed legal migration or the implementation of the Global Compact on Refugees (or durable solutions for refugees).The action implementation modalities will depend on the concrete intervention agreed for each country. The action foresees that a mix of direct and indirect management will be used.

description.narrative: Contract related to: Protection des migrants débarqués - FICR - Phase 2 - The aim of the proposed intervention ¿ the Flexible Mechanism, hereinafter ¿the Mechanism¿ ¿ is to maximise EU leverage in migration discussions vis-à-vis Sub-Saharan African counterparts, based on a flexible and incentives-based approach while also respecting policy coherence for development, as well as foreign policy objectives of the Union. Through the financing of migration-related cooperation projects, the EU aims to expand its external engagement with African partners on migration and forced displacement. In line with the most recent developments in both internal and external EU migration policy, including the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, the Mechanism will support the development and reinforcement of strong, balanced, comprehensive and mutually beneficial partnerships and programs with relevant countries of origin, transit and destination of migrants and forcibly displaced people. The action will also contribute to the Team Europe Initiative for a Comprehensive migration approach in the Maghreb, Sahel and West African countries in the Atlantic / Western Mediterranean route and to the Team Europe Initiative on Central Mediterranean migration route.Interventions will be weighed against the specific migration and/or forced displacement situation of each partner country or region, the nature of the overall dialogue with the EU, and the partner country¿s level of engagement with the EU on migration. This assessment will be done in coordination with EU Member States. In this regard, several factors, inter alia, can be taken into consideration, notably whether : (i) the country is engaging or showing willingness to engage in fighting against migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, as well as stemming irregular migration; (ii) the country is stepping up its efforts to host migrants and/or displaced people, and people in need of international protection, in a dignified way, in line with international and EU standards; (iii) the country/region is reinforcing capacities on migration management and governance, including on management of forced displacement flows, in the context of its partnership with the EU ; (iv) the country is showing a substantial and sustained cooperation with the EU and its MS on return, readmission and sustainable reintegration; (v) and/or the country/region is willing to cooperate with the EU and its MS to support well-managed legal migration or the implementation of the Global Compact on Refugees (or durable solutions for refugees).The action implementation modalities will depend on the concrete intervention agreed for each country. The action foresees that a mix of direct and indirect management will be used.

description.narrative:
Le projet contribuera à assurer le maintien de la stabilité du pays, en particulier dans les zones connaissant d'importants mouvements de populations mixtes. Cette action permettra la mise en place d'une quatrième unité GARSI à Sélibaby, dans la zone des trois frontières Mauritanie-Mali-Sénégal.

Dans le prolongement de la création et du déploiement des trois premières unités du Groupe d'action rapide, de surveillance et d'intervention (GARSI) actives sur le territoire national, l'action soutiendra la création ¿ par la formation et l'équipement ¿ d'une quatrième unité GARSI. Celle-ci sera basée à Sélibaby (région du Guidimakha), dans la zone des trois frontières entre la Mauritanie, le Mali et le Sénégal, une zone identifiée comme prioritaire compte tenu des flux migratoires mixtes (incluant de nombreux déplacements forcés depuis le Mali), des menaces émanant de groupes armés maliens ainsi que des trafics illicites et de la contrebande transfrontaliers.

Ces mesures complètent des interventions similaires en cours de préparation côté sénégalais. La nouvelle unité GARSI prendra la forme d'une compagnie d'environ 180 gendarmes vouée au contrôle du territoire, à la surveillance et à la sécurisation des zones frontalières, ainsi qu'à la lutte contre la traite des êtres humains, le terrorisme et tous les trafics illicites, en coordination avec les autres forces de sécurité nationales. La compagnie comprendra une composante fluviale renforcée, conçue comme une capacité clé du dispositif opérationnel dans la zone d'intervention.

L¿action contribuera également à la pérennisation des trois unités GARSI précédemment soutenues et toujours opérationnelles, au soutien à la coordination des quatre unités GARSI et au renforcement de la coopération transfrontalière avec les unités sénégalaises opérant de l¿autre côté du fleuve Sénégal. Pour mémoire les GARSI côté Sénégal sont également mis en ¿uvre par la FIAP grâce aux financements de l¿Union européenne.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation TVET Sierra Leone - Unleashing the Potential of Youth in West Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: TVET Sierra Leone - Unleashing the Potential of Youth in West Africa - The goal of this Action is to improve the inclusion of youth in resilient and climate-smart green economic transitions that address the root causes of irregular migration in West African countries. It complements the ¿Managing Migration Better in Western Africa¿ Action which aims at strengthening migration management. A comprehensive approach including skills development, improved access to finance for Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) notably through diaspora investment and support to value chains development is expected to influence individual decision-making processes and potentially reduce migration aspirations by providing better local prospects. It is also expected to help and facilitate sustainable reintegration. More specifically, this Action ¿Unleashing the Potential of Youth in West Africa¿ will contribute to green skills¿ alignment with the private sector needs (1.1), promote diaspora¿s investments (2.1), as well as enhance access to finance and technical support for green business growth (2.2). Job creation will also be supported through the development of targeted green, circular and low-carbon value chains (2.3).This action contributes to the implementation of the Youth Action Plan. To the extent possible, this action will build upon and benefit from Global Gateway investments in the targeted countries, contributing to strengthening the local economy, job creation and markets aligned with the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Investing in Young Businesses in Africa[1], the Regional Team Europe Initiative Opportunity-driven Skills and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Africa as well as the two migration-related regional TEIs[2]. Conversely, it will contribute to building the skills required and achieving the targeted transformational impact of the Global Gateway strategy, and its commitments to address gender equality, by maximizing its impact on the relevant ecosystems with a 360 approach. The transition to green growth is mainstreamed throughout the action. By aligning with the Nationally Determined Contributions and the National Adaptation Plans available for the region, this action aims to create a lasting impact on the vulnerable population of Western African nations. The Action will be implemented in direct management through grants and service contracts as well as in indirect management.In addition, this action contributes to strengthening migration management, migration policy, and migration governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. Therefore, the funds allocated to this action, will address some sub-components of the priority area 6 on Migration and forced displacement (Migration, Forced displacement and Flexible funding mechanism).[1] Core members of the TEI IYBA include: the European Commission, 11 EU Member States - BE, DE, ES, FI, FR, IT, NL, PT, MT, SE, SV, the European Investment Bank (EIB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Association of European Development Finance Institutions (EDFI).[2] The TEI on the Atlantic and Western Mediterranean route and the TEI on the Central Mediterranean route.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation West Africa/Sierra Leone/Education Skills Skills Development infrastructure for value chain upgrading

description.narrative:
This grant would support Sierra Leone¿s national development priorities and the EU Global Gateway strategy, focusing on enhancing connectivity through strategic infrastructure investments in West African trading corridors. A key initiative under this framework is the rehabilitation of key feeder roads through the EU funded Opportunity Salone project, launched in 2021, implemented by the ILO and its partners in Sierra Leone. Improved infrastructure is a precondition for ACFTA.

Activities

Taking a 360-degree approach the additional funding will contribute to ensuring that (i) investments in roads and (ii) selected agricultural value chains are sustainable, benefit local communities and are embedded in a conducive institutional framework. The ILO proposes to expand the current project by strengthening skills institutions, methodologies and systems. Activities will include:

  1. Creating a regular mechanism for identifying critical skills gaps both for road infrastructure support as well as specific skills that can help enhancing the ecosystem fort entrepreneurship and for agricultural sector development. Making sure both public and private sector needs are captured and developing a framework of how this information can inform and guide the TVET, entrepreneurship and private training system and offer, as for providers to update and develop relevant curricula.
  2. Developing one or two national/regional centres for vocational excellence for labour-based works in road construction and maintenance and for agrifood products, in close collaboration with the private sector. These centres will focus on delivering quality and market-relevant skills training and will serve as hubs for opportunity driven skills development, including on skills relevant for on employment intensive investments and road maintenance.
  3. Ensuring that workers in labour-based construction work acquire skills and receive government approved certification at the end of their contract, plus soft, entrepreneurial and agro-processing relevant skills, to enhance their employability and career prospects. This will be achieved through a network of TVET centres and business development service providers supporting graduates.
  4. Reviewing and improving regulatory frameworks to include skills certification by relevant government partners (Ministry of Technical and Higher Education).
  5. Reviewing and improving governance and financing arrangements for inclusive skills development, so that skills development provision can flexibly react to investment opportunities.

description.narrative: Contract related to: East Africa/Rwanda/E-Mobility - The Opportunity-driven Skills and VET in Africa Action intends to complement VET and skills development programmes financed at country level by helping these orient towards concrete employment opportunities created by (EU) investments, trade, (regional) value chain development, grants and other market dynamics in partner countries. The Action is a key element under the EU-Africa Global Gateway Investment Package announced at the 2022 EU-Africa-Summit, supporting sectors that are part of the package. At regional level, the action consists of five building blocksA Technical Assistance (TA) facility providing support based on requests from EU Delegations, EU Member States or private sector organisations to identify employment opportunities and required skills needs around flagship initiatives and translate findings in targeted recommendations for VET system support responsive to identified employment opportunities.Regional exchange on Public-Private-Partnerships to promote opportunity-driven VET and skills development in SSA, and to create a space to allow for practical exchange between public and private stakeholders on active partnerships. This includes a linkage to relevant Erasmus+ financed actions on capacity building for PPP in VET to strengthen EU-Africa engagement on skills.A Competitive Funding mechanism to finance regional and multi-country VET initiatives in support of (regional) value chains that complement country MIPs, as well as actions that more generally support this paradigm shift of reverse engineering VET in function of employment opportunities market dynamics create.A flexible funding mechanism, which allows for country-driven funding for opportunity-driven skills development and training linked to GG investments with concrete employment opportunities.A continental Africa-Europe coordination mechanism for knowledge sharing, to deliver agile skills intelligence, innovation, dialogue, and advisory support alongside the African Continental Free Trade Area (ACfTA) and the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), informing and valorising Global Gateway priority sectors and priority value chains.The Action is aligned with the priority areas of the regional MIP for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021 ¿ 2027 (Priority area 1: Human Development, Result 2.2. and Priority area 5: Sustainable Growth and Decent Jobs, Result 3.2.) and SDGs 8 Decent work and economic growth, 4 Quality education, 5 Gender equality, 10 Reduced inequalities and 17 Partnerships.

description.narrative:
L'Action SAH'LAM vise à prévenir et atténuer l'impact des conflits locaux dans la zone frontalière Mauritanie-Mali-Sénégal, en renforçant la cohésion sociale et l¿accès aux services sociaux de base et aux services marchands.

La stratégie d'intervention repose sur trois piliers complémentaires. Le premier renforce la cohésion sociale et la gouvernance territoriale par la mise à jour des plans d'action territoriaux, le renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux, l'accompagnement des organisations de la société civile et la formalisation d'accords sociaux favorisant une gestion inclusive des ressources naturelles. Le deuxième soutient le développement économique durable grâce au renforcement des filières agricoles et pastorales, à la valorisation des productions locales, au développement de l'entrepreneuriat, à l'accès au financement, ainsi qu'à la réalisation ou la réhabilitation d'infrastructures multiservices, d'ouvrages communautaires et d'équipements économiques d'intérêt transfrontalier. Le troisième pilier développe les mécanismes de prévention des conflits en consolidant les espaces de concertation existants, en soutenant les dispositifs de dialogue communautaire et institutionnel, en renforçant les capacités de prévention des conflits et en développant des actions de sensibilisation à travers les radios locales et les autres médias de proximité. Cette approche repose sur la conviction que le renforcement simultané de la gouvernance territoriale, de l'accès aux services essentiels, des opportunités économiques et du dialogue entre les acteurs permettra de restaurer progressivement la confiance, de réduire les tensions et de renforcer durablement la résilience des territoires frontaliers.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Supporting Clean Cooking Solutions in Central and East Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: Supporting Clean Cooking Solutions in Central and East Africa - The clean cooking sector is gaining traction in some countries of East and Central Africa, but it remains fragmented and underfunded. The dominating use of low-efficiency biomass cooking solutions comes with major negative environmental, socio-economic, health and gender impacts. Significant additional financing and policy efforts in the region are required to reach universal access to clean cooking by 2030.The Action intends to contribute to increasing and accelerating the access to affordable, clean and sustainable cooking solutions (high-tier cooking solutions) in East and Central Africa. The Action will foster clean cooking business development with coaching, financial partnership brokering (finance catalyst) and innovative financial solutions for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) including manufacturers, distributors and importers of clean cooking solutions. More particularly, it will offer results-based-finance and thematic grants to support and accelerate market development and innovation. It will also expand the portfolio of finance institutions to clean cooking through training, sector-specific tools and de-risking mechanisms, like guarantees and credit lines where blending will be possible. It will strengthen the regulatory and market framework by supporting regional dialogue and coordination of policies and plans through platforms, networks of task forces, and by promoting regional performance standards and reduced tariffs barriers, contributing to stronger clean cooking strategies and facilitated international trade of clean cooking solutions. The Action is fully aligned with regional and national policies and strategies. It will build on on-going activities, more particularly, Europe (EU) and EU Member States¿ funded programmes in the region. It is intended to improve, adapt and replicate successful approaches, to selected countries for a possible future extension at full regional scale. This Action will contribute to the regional priority area 3 of the MIP ¿Green Transition¿ and to its specific objective 2 ¿Support the development of an efficient, sustainable and resilient African energy sector¿. The action will also actively contribute to the pledge of the Clean Cooking Declaration of Paris (2024) to make clean cooking a priority and enhance the efforts toward achieving universal access for all.The action will contribute to affordable and clean energy access for cooking (SDG7), climate mitigation (SDG13), forest conservation (SDG15), gender equality, including in entrepreneurship (SDG5), health, more particularly of women and girls (SDG3), and sustainable cities (SDG11).

title.narrative: Activity under preparation CRM- EDFI-MC Blending Facility

description.narrative: Contract related to: CRM- EDFI-MC Blending Facility - Until 2020, the Latin America (LAIF) and Caribbean (CIF) Facilities have been operating under different budgetary regimes, LAIF under the Development Cooperation Instrument (DCI) and the CIF under the European Development Fund (EDF). This new Facility, LACIF, follows the strategic logic under the new NDICI to merge different financial instruments under the same umbrella. DCI and EDF converge in the new NDICI and this provides the opportunity to combine the two previous facilities in one, taking advantage of shared structures and stakeholders, minimizing administrative transaction costs and adding flexibility to the process of resource allocation, while catering to the unique opportunities and challenges of the two regions. Moreover, action at regional level is particularly relevant to tackle crucial aspects of infrastructure involving networks (transport, energy, water and digital) and regarding cross-border issues (health security, supply chains, migration, etc.). LACIF will continue to boost access to funds from financial institutions, which are supporting key investments for sustainable inclusive infrastructure development with a focus on climate change, as well as rights and gender responsive private sector development in the region contributing substantially to poverty alleviation throughout the continent.European financial institutions were key partners of LAIF and CIF, an important factor for the success of the Facilities was the participation of the regional Latin American and Caribbean financial institutions, more prominently the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), the Latin American Development Bank (CAF), the Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI) and the Caribbean Development Bank (CDB), acting as co-lead implementers for many operations. This resulted in a stronger and more strategic partnership between European and Latin American financial institutions.

description.narrative: The Project consists of the deployment of 15.188 ground telecom access points, backhauled via satellite, to deliver basic telecommunication services (voice and data) to underserved rural areas across 20 sub-Saharan Africa countries. Each village will be equipped with a connectivity kit comprising a satellite reception terminal (antenna and modem), solar-powered energy equipment (solar panels and battery), and a Wi-Fi router. The service will deliver affordable data services be accessible to users with low-end smartphones within a 150-meter radius of each hotspot.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation AU-EU Health Support Facility

description.narrative: Contract related to: AU-EU Health Support Facility - The overall objective is to strengthen the African health security architecture, pharmaceutical systems and public health capacity, contributing to stronger, more resilient health systems and improved health outcomes. This objective pursues SDG 3.8 and promotes ultimately universal health coverage (UHC).The Action has two specific objectives:1.Specific Objective 1 (50 M): aims to reinforce health sector resilience and African strategic autonomy by focusing on underserved segments of the pharmaceutical value chain. This action is the fourth EU funded regional programme formulated in the framework of the regional MAV+ initiative. It encompasses a regional level and country level interventions through two workstreams.·Country level: through a Global Gateway 360° approach, it will focus on building stronger public and private ecosystems, with special attention to supporting innovative financial solutions (indicative countries: Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Ethiopia, Guinea Bissau and Guinea Conakry).·Regional level: will focus on 1) supporting regulatory strengthening and harmonisation, in line the African Medicines Agency mandate, 2) support establishment of regional pooled procurement mechanisms 3) support the fight against illicit drugs and 4) strengthen R&D/laboratories (indicative countries: Ethiopia, Guinea Bissau, Guinea Conakry, Burundi, DRC and Angola).2.Specific Objective 2 (5M): create a structure to support the EU-AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative. Following lessons learnt from the MAV+ Team Europe Support Structure (TESS), the support structure will have as main goal to ensure a coherent and coordinated approach of all interventions done under each of 5 hubs under the EU-AU Health Partnership TEI, namely MAV+, SRHR, Health Security using a One Health approach (HSOH), Public Health Institutes (PHI) and Digital Health (DH) and support the teams behind these hubs to ensure an effective implementation.This Action contributes to the Global Gateway Health Package presented at the 6th EU-AU Summit in 2022 and the EU-AU Health Partnership Team Europe Inititiave[1], which includes the Manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+) hub. [1] The EU AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative (TEI) includes five TEI Hubs: theHub on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+), the Hub on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, the Hub on Health Security using a One Health approach, the Hub on Digital Health and the Hub on Support to Public Health Insititutes in SSA
