title.narrative: Activity under preparation Action pour la Coopération en matière de Transparence, d¿Intégration Fiscale et de lutte contre les Flux Financiers Illicites en Afrique de l¿Ouest et Centrale (ACTIF +)

description.narrative: Contract related to: Action pour la Coopération en matière de Transparence, d¿Intégration Fiscale et de lutte contre les Flux Financiers Illicites en Afrique de l¿Ouest et Centrale (ACTIF +) - Upholding democratic governance goes far beyond single electoral events and requires informed citizen engagement through credible, transparent and inclusive decision-making processes that enhance the effectiveness, responsiveness and legitimacy of public policies. This action will reaffirm the EU¿s position as a reliable partner in supporting African ownership in the implementation of the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP) ; provide comprehensive electoral support at national, regional and continental levels; and enhance accountability mechanisms integrating a human rights-based approach (HRBA) perspective, including oversight by independent media, open governance reforms, and the fight against tax evasion, fraud, and illicit financial flows to reinforce credible inclusive democratic institutions, sustain resilient and accountable democracies, and increase tax transparency and domestic resource mobilisation. In a context of an evolving autocratic wave[1] and increasing political instability affecting in particular Sub-Saharan Africa, the action aligns with EU and AU strategies and interests, including that of promoting a rules-based order, enhancing the respect for human rights and gender equality and ultimately fulfilling African citizens¿ aspirations for a democracy that delivers positive outcomes.[2] The proposed action adopts a multi-level, multi-stakeholder approach, recognising that sustainable solutions require coordination across continental, regional, and national levels. It aims to strengthen African institutions, enhance electoral integrity, promote independent media and accountable governance, ultimately contributing to a more stable and prosperous continent.Transitional Justice (TJ) is considered at the highest political level by the African Union (AU) as a tool for conflict prevention and resolution, essential for addressing the root causes of conflict and building the foundation for lasting peace and sustainable development. Operationalising ¿African solutions to African problems¿, AU Member States (MS) have demanded increased support from the AU to implement the AUTJP and its roadmap. Hence, building on a predecessor project[3] under AAP 2022, greater emphasis will be placed on capacitating AU MS and regional bodies such as ECOWAS, SADC, IGAD and ECCAS.To enhance electoral processes, SO2 (Electoral Support) will extend beyond traditional technical and logistical support to election management bodies and State institutions, incorporating support for civil society, voter education, and independent media to ensure fair democratic coverage. The EU will promote a coherent approach by supporting the implementation of EU Election Observation Missions¿ (EU EOMs) recommendations and harmonising pan-African electoral capacities. To counter shrinking civic space, the action will strengthen regional CSO networks for election observation and foster structured collaboration between the AU, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and corresponding CSO platforms.The action will also promote accountability by strengthening independent media, advancing open governance reforms, and reinforcing the fight against tax fraud, evasion, and illicit financial flows. Support to media will focus on strengthening the resilience and financial sustainability of independent media and investigative journalism. description.narrative: Contract related to: Networking of Commun Operational Partnership (NET-COP) ¿ Phase III - This action will contribute to the two Migration Team Europe Initiatives (TEIs) in Western Africa (Atlantic/Western Mediterranean Central Mediterranean routes), in particular the return & reintegration and the anti-trafficking/anti-smuggling components, which are integral parts of both TEIs and help ensuring safe, regular and orderly migration. This initiative focuses on Western Africa countries (whether countries of origin or transit for irregular migration) covered by the Team Europe Initiatives on the Atlantic/Western Mediterranean[1] and Central Mediterranean routes[2]. For reintegration, the action puts a specific emphasis on Chad, Côte d¿Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and The Gambia. Within this group, Côte d¿Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Nigeria, and Senegal have already developed, to a certain extent, national capacities, structures and referral systems for reintegration and it is expected that referral systems for reintegration in these five countries would be operational at a mid-term horizon enabling these countries to manage the sustainable reintegration of all returnees.[1] The Team Europe Initiative on Atlantic/Western Mediterranean route covers the following Western African countries: Burkina Faso, Côte d¿Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal and The Gambia.[2] The Team Europe Initiative on Central Mediterranean migration route covers the following Western African countries: Burkina Faso, Chad, Côte d¿Ivoire, Guinea, Niger, Nigeria.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation West Africa/Ghana/TVET&Pharma -Support to pharmaceutical sector with focus on vaccines development in Ghana - Extension

description.narrative: Contract related to: West Africa/Ghana/TVET&Pharma -Support to pharmaceutical sector with focus on vaccines development in Ghana - Extension - The Opportunity-driven Skills and VET in Africa Action intends to complement VET and skills development programmes financed at country level by helping these orient towards concrete employment opportunities created by (EU) investments, trade, (regional) value chain development, grants and other market dynamics in partner countries. The Action is a key element under the EU-Africa Global Gateway Investment Package announced at the 2022 EU-Africa-Summit, supporting sectors that are part of the package. At regional level, the action consists of five building blocksA Technical Assistance (TA) facility providing support based on requests from EU Delegations, EU Member States or private sector organisations to identify employment opportunities and required skills needs around flagship initiatives and translate findings in targeted recommendations for VET system support responsive to identified employment opportunities.Regional exchange on Public-Private-Partnerships to promote opportunity-driven VET and skills development in SSA, and to create a space to allow for practical exchange between public and private stakeholders on active partnerships. This includes a linkage to relevant Erasmus+ financed actions on capacity building for PPP in VET to strengthen EU-Africa engagement on skills.A Competitive Funding mechanism to finance regional and multi-country VET initiatives in support of (regional) value chains that complement country MIPs, as well as actions that more generally support this paradigm shift of reverse engineering VET in function of employment opportunities market dynamics create.A flexible funding mechanism, which allows for country-driven funding for opportunity-driven skills development and training linked to GG investments with concrete employment opportunities.A continental Africa-Europe coordination mechanism for knowledge sharing, to deliver agile skills intelligence, innovation, dialogue, and advisory support alongside the African Continental Free Trade Area (ACfTA) and the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), informing and valorising Global Gateway priority sectors and priority value chains.The Action is aligned with the priority areas of the regional MIP for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021 ¿ 2027 (Priority area 1: Human Development, Result 2.2. and Priority area 5: Sustainable Growth and Decent Jobs, Result 3.2.) and SDGs 8 Decent work and economic growth, 4 Quality education, 5 Gender equality, 10 Reduced inequalities and 17 Partnerships.

title.narrative: Économie verte inclusive et approches sensibles aux conflits pour la conservation des paysages PoMoCo et WAP en Afrique de l'Ouest »

description.narrative: Contract related to: Économie verte inclusive et approches sensibles aux conflits pour la conservation des paysages PoMoCo et WAP en Afrique de l'Ouest » - The overall objective of the NaturAfrica initiative is to tackle biodiversity loss through restoring and protecting a network of protected areas and high value ecosystems and promoting the sustainable management of surrounding landscapes whilst creating decent incomes and jobs in green sectors for local populations. Through the financing of the conservation and restoration of natural habitats and ecosystems, and the sustainable management and development of key landscapes, the EU aims also to enhance ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, soil fertility, water cycle regulation, disaster risk reduction, etc. as well as benefits for the local populations.The NaturAfrica initiative intends to work in Key Landscapes for Conservation and Development (KLCD) for (i) increasing the conservation of areas with high biodiversity value and high carbon content, and developing green economy activities by and for the neighbouring local communities and (ii) improving the inclusive governance of these landscapes to improve territorial planning, reduce conflicts and mobilise carbon finance. The transboundary nature of biological resources, their ecosystems and habitats species and communities calls for interventions at regional level through transboundary landscapes. Key transboundary landscapes were identified in six priority regions, following a wide consultation of stakeholders, including national institutions, civil society and the private sector. These regions are representatives of main African habitats with specific challenges each, and include: Congo Basin Forest ecosystems (Gabon, Burundi, Cameroon, Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Central African Republic (CAR), Uganda, South Sudan, Rwanda)   Transhumance landscapes in Central Africa (Chad, CAR, Nigeria, Cameroon)  West Africa Forests (Burkina Faso, Guinea Conakry, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Cote d¿Ivoire Ivory Coast, Nigeria)  Sudano-Sahelian savannahs of West Africa (Burkina Faso, Benin, Niger, Togo, Ghana, Senegal, Guinea)   Eastern Rift savannahs and watersheds (Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Tanzania)  Trans-frontier conservation areas of Southern Africa (Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Malawi, Mozambique, Angola, South Africa).    Relevant green economy activities include renewable energy and sustainable value chains (agriculture, livestock, fisheries, timber/non-timber forest products, tourism, ethical and sustainable fashion and circular industries). The NaturAfrica initiative complements numerous national initiatives that are foreseen in the national programmes within the same transboundary landscapes or expanding the approach to other important national landscapes and altogether, with the contribution of EU Member States (MS), is part of the large NaturAfrica flagship.This is the first phase of a 2-phased programme with a mid-term evaluation leading to a second phase in 2025. Phase 1 will initiate interventions in key landscapes, building synergies between actors and interventions, and pave the way for consolidation in phase 2.  <p

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Third party monitoring Portefeuille migration

description.narrative: Contract related to: Third party monitoring Portefeuille migration - The aim of the proposed intervention ¿ the Flexible Mechanism, hereinafter ¿the Mechanism¿ ¿ is to maximise EU leverage in migration discussions vis-à-vis Sub-Saharan African counterparts, based on a flexible and incentives-based approach while also respecting policy coherence for development, as well as foreign policy objectives of the Union. Through the financing of migration-related cooperation projects, the EU aims to expand its external engagement with African partners on migration and forced displacement. In line with the most recent developments in both internal and external EU migration policy, including the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, the Mechanism will support the development and reinforcement of strong, balanced, comprehensive and mutually beneficial partnerships and programs with relevant countries of origin, transit and destination of migrants and forcibly displaced people. The action will also contribute to the Team Europe Initiative for a Comprehensive migration approach in the Maghreb, Sahel and West African countries in the Atlantic / Western Mediterranean route and to the Team Europe Initiative on Central Mediterranean migration route.Interventions will be weighed against the specific migration and/or forced displacement situation of each partner country or region, the nature of the overall dialogue with the EU, and the partner country¿s level of engagement with the EU on migration. This assessment will be done in coordination with EU Member States. In this regard, several factors, inter alia, can be taken into consideration, notably whether : (i) the country is engaging or showing willingness to engage in fighting against migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, as well as stemming irregular migration; (ii) the country is stepping up its efforts to host migrants and/or displaced people, and people in need of international protection, in a dignified way, in line with international and EU standards; (iii) the country/region is reinforcing capacities on migration management and governance, including on management of forced displacement flows, in the context of its partnership with the EU ; (iv) the country is showing a substantial and sustained cooperation with the EU and its MS on return, readmission and sustainable reintegration; (v) and/or the country/region is willing to cooperate with the EU and its MS to support well-managed legal migration or the implementation of the Global Compact on Refugees (or durable solutions for refugees).The action implementation modalities will depend on the concrete intervention agreed for each country. The action foresees that a mix of direct and indirect management will be used.

description.narrative: Contract related to: Expenditure verification MR AVP 2026 (382-883, 408-970, 456-522) - Within the framework of promoting a rules-based multilateralism and partnerships to achieve the SDGs, the Overall Objective of this action is to mobilise support expenditure for the implementation of the 3 "specific objectives" of NDICI-Global Europe-Global Challenges-Partnerships (cf. Global Challenges MIP): 1. Enhanced global and multilateral partnerships; 2. Stronger economic governance and inclusive societies; and 3. Strengthened local authorities at global level.The Specific Objectives of this action are to: 1. Support activities and practitioners involved in ensuring and/or multiplying the impact of operational interventions funded through the NDICI instrument (notably, the Partnerships component of Global Challenges). 2. Reinforce monitoring, evaluation and auditing activities of actions and programmes funded through NDICI (notably, the Partnerships component of Global Challenges).  3. Provide support in the design of actions, programmes and strategies which require a more in-depth analysis, including on cross-cutting issues. 4. Promote policy dialogue, communication/visibility, public diplomacy activities, capacity-building, technical preparation, and any support needed to facilitate joint programming and Team Europe and Global Gateway coordination at country level.Therefore, this action can include multi-sector support and serve both headquarters and Union delegations.In terms of timeline, this action is intended to support the work of HQs and EUDs through the end of the current MFF 2021-2027 and the very beginning of the new MFF 2028-2034, with a total planned amount of EUR 1,700,000 ¿ divided into EUR 800,000 from 2025¿s Partnerships budgetary appropriations; EUR 500,000 from 2026¿s Partnerships budgetary appropriations; and EUR 400,000 from 2027¿s Partnerships budgetary appropriations.

description.narrative: Contract related to: Afripi II - SummaryThis Action is central to the Global Gateway (GG) Africa-Europe Investment Package (GG AEIP) roll-out and contributes to the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) in support to African economic integration towards the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), a flagship objective of the African Union¿s Agenda 2063 and a major priority for the European Union (EU). The EU has built a strategic approach in support of intra-African and EU-Africa investment and trade by anchoring its support on key priority areas (i.e. trade in goods, services, trade facilitation, competition, digital trade) of free trade and investment agreements at continental, regional and national levels (AfCFTA, RECs, EU Bilateral and Regional - EPAs), as well as key value chains, and trade corridors.To complement this support, this Action will focus on four additional key enablers of EU-Africa and intra-Africa sustainable trade and investment that will be concretely implemented through four different projects, some of which are a continuation of existing support, namely:1. Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) protection and enforcement are key for investment and innovation facilitation and protection. Support will contribute to the harmonisation, creation, registration, management, utilisation and administration, protection, and enforcement of IPRs in Africa. To this end, the Action will focus on continental, regional and national: (i) African IP legal and policy frameworks (i.e. AfCFTA IP Protocol, the Continental Strategy for Geographical Indications (GIs) of the African Union, Regional and national IP regulations, etc.); (ii) African IP administration capacities; (iii) African and EU productive sector support, with a particular focus on SMEs (i.e. the Africa IP SME Helpdesk); and (iv) Support to the elaboration and implementation of the post 2023 Continental Strategy for GIs of the African Union.2. EU-Africa Trade and Investment Agreements, with the main objective to boost sustainable EU ¿ Africa trade and investment flows and strengthen the trade and investment capacities of African partners through the design of a flexible on-demand facility that can offer ad-hoc support to countries with whom the EU has concluded trade and investment agreements (EPAs, SIFAs, etc.). This facility will also provide complementary technical support needed for alignment with EU regulations and directives having an impact on EU-Africa trade and investment, such as the relevant policies adopted in the framework of the European Green Deal and the EU Circular Economy Action Plan or the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D).3. Customs Cooperation, a main enabler at the basis of all trade. The Action proposes a follow up to the existing successful programmes `Harmonizing the classification of goods based on WCO standards to enhance African trade¿ (EU-WCO Harmonised System (HS) Programme, 2018-2024) and `Implementation and application of Rules of Origin (RoO)¿ (EU-WCO RoO Programme, 2021-2025). The scope of the new programme is to enhance African trade by further developing and implementing key customs pillars of the AfCFTA and of other regional agreements through dedicated technical capacity support to (i) Harmonised System (HS), (ii) Rules of Origin (RoO), and (iii) Valuation. 4. Investment Facilitation, a crucial soft enabler to accompany Global Gateway hard investments, ensuring that they are conducive to sustainable and inclusive development. title.narrative: Activity under preparation Targeted alpha-immune therapy for Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: Targeted alpha-immune therapy for Africa - The overall objective is to strengthen the African health security architecture, pharmaceutical systems and public health capacity, contributing to stronger, more resilient health systems and improved health outcomes. This objective pursues SDG 3.8 and promotes ultimately universal health coverage (UHC).The Action has two specific objectives:1.Specific Objective 1 (50 M): aims to reinforce health sector resilience and African strategic autonomy by focusing on underserved segments of the pharmaceutical value chain. This action is the fourth EU funded regional programme formulated in the framework of the regional MAV+ initiative. It encompasses a regional level and country level interventions through two workstreams.·Country level: through a Global Gateway 360° approach, it will focus on building stronger public and private ecosystems, with special attention to supporting innovative financial solutions (indicative countries: Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Ethiopia, Guinea Bissau and Guinea Conakry).·Regional level: will focus on 1) supporting regulatory strengthening and harmonisation, in line the African Medicines Agency mandate, 2) support establishment of regional pooled procurement mechanisms 3) support the fight against illicit drugs and 4) strengthen R&D/laboratories (indicative countries: Ethiopia, Guinea Bissau, Guinea Conakry, Burundi, DRC and Angola).2.Specific Objective 2 (5M): create a structure to support the EU-AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative. Following lessons learnt from the MAV+ Team Europe Support Structure (TESS), the support structure will have as main goal to ensure a coherent and coordinated approach of all interventions done under each of 5 hubs under the EU-AU Health Partnership TEI, namely MAV+, SRHR, Health Security using a One Health approach (HSOH), Public Health Institutes (PHI) and Digital Health (DH) and support the teams behind these hubs to ensure an effective implementation.This Action contributes to the Global Gateway Health Package presented at the 6th EU-AU Summit in 2022 and the EU-AU Health Partnership Team Europe Inititiave[1], which includes the Manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+) hub. [1] The EU AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative (TEI) includes five TEI Hubs: theHub on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+), the Hub on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, the Hub on Health Security using a One Health approach, the Hub on Digital Health and the Hub on Support to Public Health Insititutes in SSA

title.narrative: Activity under preparation DREAM Kenya ¿ Democratic Resilience and Electoral Accountability to Meet Popular Demands in Kenya¿s 2027 electoral cycle

description.narrative: Contract related to: DREAM Kenya ¿ Democratic Resilience and Electoral Accountability to Meet Popular Demands in Kenya¿s 2027 electoral cycle - Upholding democratic governance goes far beyond single electoral events and requires informed citizen engagement through credible, transparent and inclusive decision-making processes that enhance the effectiveness, responsiveness and legitimacy of public policies. This action will reaffirm the EU¿s position as a reliable partner in supporting African ownership in the implementation of the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP) ; provide comprehensive electoral support at national, regional and continental levels; and enhance accountability mechanisms integrating a human rights-based approach (HRBA) perspective, including oversight by independent media, open governance reforms, and the fight against tax evasion, fraud, and illicit financial flows to reinforce credible inclusive democratic institutions, sustain resilient and accountable democracies, and increase tax transparency and domestic resource mobilisation. In a context of an evolving autocratic wave[1] and increasing political instability affecting in particular Sub-Saharan Africa, the action aligns with EU and AU strategies and interests, including that of promoting a rules-based order, enhancing the respect for human rights and gender equality and ultimately fulfilling African citizens¿ aspirations for a democracy that delivers positive outcomes.[2] The proposed action adopts a multi-level, multi-stakeholder approach, recognising that sustainable solutions require coordination across continental, regional, and national levels. It aims to strengthen African institutions, enhance electoral integrity, promote independent media and accountable governance, ultimately contributing to a more stable and prosperous continent.Transitional Justice (TJ) is considered at the highest political level by the African Union (AU) as a tool for conflict prevention and resolution, essential for addressing the root causes of conflict and building the foundation for lasting peace and sustainable development. Operationalising ¿African solutions to African problems¿, AU Member States (MS) have demanded increased support from the AU to implement the AUTJP and its roadmap. Hence, building on a predecessor project[3] under AAP 2022, greater emphasis will be placed on capacitating AU MS and regional bodies such as ECOWAS, SADC, IGAD and ECCAS.To enhance electoral processes, SO2 (Electoral Support) will extend beyond traditional technical and logistical support to election management bodies and State institutions, incorporating support for civil society, voter education, and independent media to ensure fair democratic coverage. The EU will promote a coherent approach by supporting the implementation of EU Election Observation Missions¿ (EU EOMs) recommendations and harmonising pan-African electoral capacities. To counter shrinking civic space, the action will strengthen regional CSO networks for election observation and foster structured collaboration between the AU, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and corresponding CSO platforms.The action will also promote accountability by strengthening independent media, advancing open governance reforms, and reinforcing the fight against tax fraud, evasion, and illicit financial flows. Support to media will focus on strengthening the resilience and financial sustainability of independent media and investigative journalism. EU engagement for the Open Government Partnership (OGP) will complement that of the ¿

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Réponse humanitaire POC

description.narrative: Contract related to: Réponse humanitaire POC - The aim of the proposed intervention ¿ the Flexible Mechanism, hereinafter ¿the Mechanism¿ ¿ is to maximise EU leverage in migration discussions vis-à-vis Sub-Saharan African counterparts, based on a flexible and incentives-based approach while also respecting policy coherence for development, as well as foreign policy objectives of the Union. Through the financing of migration-related cooperation projects, the EU aims to expand its external engagement with African partners on migration and forced displacement. In line with the most recent developments in both internal and external EU migration policy, including the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, the Mechanism will support the development and reinforcement of strong, balanced, comprehensive and mutually beneficial partnerships and programs with relevant countries of origin, transit and destination of migrants and forcibly displaced people. The action will also contribute to the Team Europe Initiative for a Comprehensive migration approach in the Maghreb, Sahel and West African countries in the Atlantic / Western Mediterranean route and to the Team Europe Initiative on Central Mediterranean migration route.Interventions will be weighed against the specific migration and/or forced displacement situation of each partner country or region, the nature of the overall dialogue with the EU, and the partner country¿s level of engagement with the EU on migration. This assessment will be done in coordination with EU Member States. In this regard, several factors, inter alia, can be taken into consideration, notably whether : (i) the country is engaging or showing willingness to engage in fighting against migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, as well as stemming irregular migration; (ii) the country is stepping up its efforts to host migrants and/or displaced people, and people in need of international protection, in a dignified way, in line with international and EU standards; (iii) the country/region is reinforcing capacities on migration management and governance, including on management of forced displacement flows, in the context of its partnership with the EU ; (iv) the country is showing a substantial and sustained cooperation with the EU and its MS on return, readmission and sustainable reintegration; (v) and/or the country/region is willing to cooperate with the EU and its MS to support well-managed legal migration or the implementation of the Global Compact on Refugees (or durable solutions for refugees).The action implementation modalities will depend on the concrete intervention agreed for each country. The action foresees that a mix of direct and indirect management will be used.

title.narrative: PRO-JUST: strengthening the criminal Justice chain in PALOP-TL countries

description.narrative: Contract related to: PRO-JUST: strengthening the criminal Justice chain in PALOP-TL countries - The Action will strengthen institutions in the African Portuguese speaking countries[1] and Timor-Leste (PALOP-TL) contributing to peace and justice. It will focus on fighting corruption, money laundering, and organized crime; and on improving accountability and good governance. By so doing, it will contribute to achieve the objectives of the continental TEI to support Africa in combatting Illicit Financial Flows (IFFs) and Transitional Organised Crime (TOC). The Action builds on the results of the previous programme Supporting the Consolidation of the Rule of Law in PALOP countries and Timor-Leste (PACED) which ended in June 2022. Further than consolidating networks, agreements, materials, and digital platform developed by the previous programme, it will include new components (e.g. digitalisation) and involve new stakeholders (e.g. customs and media). The lead entity in charge of this action is the EU Delegation to Mozambique.The entity in charge of the contract management is the EU Delegation to Mozambique. [1] Angola, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, São Tomé and Príncipe.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation EU Investments for Nutrition (EU - I4N)

description.narrative: Contract related to: EU Investments for Nutrition (EU - I4N) - In the framework of Team Europe nutrition commitments, the EU Investment for Nutrition (EU-I4N) Action aims to improve nutritional outcomes by supporting the development of a pipeline of bankable nutrition-positive investment opportunities in agri-food value chains, with a particular focus on Sub-Saharan Africa, under a Global Gateway approach.The Action will seek to improve the availability, affordability, and competitiveness of nutritious foods through three mutually reinforcing pillars:Originate: investment pipeline development.Strengthen: operational technical assistance.Enable: support to the enabling legal, regulatory and policy environment.The Action will use EU funding catalytically to identify and structure investment opportunities, support selected projects and firms in becoming investment-ready and implementation-ready, and strengthen the enabling environment for responsible nutrition-sensitive investment. It will thereby help crowd in larger volumes of public and private capital while contributing to healthier diets, stronger local value addition and more resilient food systems.EU private sector actors will be involved, where relevant, as investors, technical partners, technology providers, processors, off-takers and business networks. Priority value chains may include formulated complementary foods and other specific nutritional foods, fortified foods, dairy, fresh fruits and vegetables, legumes and pulses, fish and aquaculture, eggs, aviculture, roots and tubers, biofortified crops and other nutrient-dense food segments, as well as selected enabling non-food segments directly linked to their performance and nutrition impact, such as storage, cold chain, packaging, transport, distribution, wholesale market functions, quality systems and traceability services.The action will not directly fund investments. Rather, it will facilitate matchmaking with third-party sources of finance, including EFSD+ guarantees, EU blending operations, EDFIs, DFIs, PDBs, impact funds and other private financial actors, including via the INTPA Investment Hub where relevant. Potential geographical areas of intervention include West Africa (Nigeria, Cote d¿Ivoire, Benin, Senegal) and East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Rwanda), given favourable business environment, positive dynamics for investment in nutrition-sensitive value chains and strong synergies with other EU programmes (i.e. ATCMA, MbA).

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support Measures- SADC Capacity Building

description.narrative: Support to SADC will enhance project management skills, including gender mainstreaming and human rights based approach HRBA in the project cycle, establish robust systems for project implementation, and ensure quality of outputs. It will tackle capacity constraints by supporting human resources and improving financial management systems to overcome budgetary limitations. Importantly, it will promote broader ownership of regional programmes through active engagement with Member States and Non-State Actors. Embracing new technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics, will enhance staff agility and ensure that skills remain relevant in the digital age. Upgrading legacy ICT systems is crucial for achieving efficient administration and communication, while improving the SADC Library's structure will facilitate better access to institutional knowledge and strategic information. Additionally, creating a dynamic online Monitoring and Evaluation System will ensure continuous progress tracking and provide stakeholders with timely insights for decision-making. Emphasizing internal research capacities and fostering collaboration with regional think tanks will bolster evidence-based policymaking, advancing SADC's regional integration agenda.

In this regard, several factors, inter alia, can be taken into consideration, notably whether : (i) the country is engaging or showing willingness to engage in fighting against migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, as well as stemming irregular migration; (ii) the country is stepping up its efforts to host migrants and/or displaced people, and people in need of international protection, in a dignified way, in line with international and EU standards; (iii) the country/region is reinforcing capacities on migration management and governance, including on management of forced displacement flows, in the context of its partnership with the EU ; (iv) the country is showing a substantial and sustained cooperation with the EU and its MS on return, readmission and sustainable reintegration; (v) and/or the country/region is willing to cooperate with the EU and its MS to support well-managed legal migration or the implementation of the Global Compact on Refugees (or durable solutions for refugees).The action implementation modalities will depend on the concrete intervention agreed for each country. The action foresees that a mix of direct and indirect management will be used.

title.narrative: Activity under preparation Independent Media as a Pillar of Democracy in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative: Contract related to: Independent Media as a Pillar of Democracy in Sub-Saharan Africa - Upholding democratic governance goes far beyond single electoral events and requires informed citizen engagement through credible, transparent and inclusive decision-making processes that enhance the effectiveness, responsiveness and legitimacy of public policies. This action will reaffirm the EU¿s position as a reliable partner in supporting African ownership in the implementation of the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP) ; provide comprehensive electoral support at national, regional and continental levels; and enhance accountability mechanisms integrating a human rights-based approach (HRBA) perspective, including oversight by independent media, open governance reforms, and the fight against tax evasion, fraud, and illicit financial flows to reinforce credible inclusive democratic institutions, sustain resilient and accountable democracies, and increase tax transparency and domestic resource mobilisation. In a context of an evolving autocratic wave[1] and increasing political instability affecting in particular Sub-Saharan Africa, the action aligns with EU and AU strategies and interests, including that of promoting a rules-based order, enhancing the respect for human rights and gender equality and ultimately fulfilling African citizens¿ aspirations for a democracy that delivers positive outcomes.[2] The proposed action adopts a multi-level, multi-stakeholder approach, recognising that sustainable solutions require coordination across continental, regional, and national levels. It aims to strengthen African institutions, enhance electoral integrity, promote independent media and accountable governance, ultimately contributing to a more stable and prosperous continent.Transitional Justice (TJ) is considered at the highest political level by the African Union (AU) as a tool for conflict prevention and resolution, essential for addressing the root causes of conflict and building the foundation for lasting peace and sustainable development. Operationalising ¿African solutions to African problems¿, AU Member States (MS) have demanded increased support from the AU to implement the AUTJP and its roadmap. Hence, building on a predecessor project[3] under AAP 2022, greater emphasis will be placed on capacitating AU MS and regional bodies such as ECOWAS, SADC, IGAD and ECCAS.To enhance electoral processes, SO2 (Electoral Support) will extend beyond traditional technical and logistical support to election management bodies and State institutions, incorporating support for civil society, voter education, and independent media to ensure fair democratic coverage. The EU will promote a coherent approach by supporting the implementation of EU Election Observation Missions¿ (EU EOMs) recommendations and harmonising pan-African electoral capacities. To counter shrinking civic space, the action will strengthen regional CSO networks for election observation and foster structured collaboration between the AU, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and corresponding CSO platforms.The action will also promote accountability by strengthening independent media, advancing open governance reforms, and reinforcing the fight against tax fraud, evasion, and illicit financial flows. Support to media will focus on strengthening the resilience and financial sustainability of independent media and investigative journalism. title.narrative: Activity under preparation Lutte contre la migration irrégulière et le trafic illicite de migrants, via le renforcement des capacités de la police et de la gendarmerie

description.narrative: Contract related to: Lutte contre la migration irrégulière et le trafic illicite de migrants, via le renforcement des capacités de la police et de la gendarmerie - The aim of the proposed intervention ¿ the Flexible Mechanism, hereinafter ¿the Mechanism¿ ¿ is to maximise EU leverage in migration discussions vis-à-vis Sub-Saharan African counterparts, based on a flexible and incentives-based approach while also respecting policy coherence for development, as well as foreign policy objectives of the Union. Through the financing of migration-related cooperation projects, the EU aims to expand its external engagement with African partners on migration and forced displacement. In line with the most recent developments in both internal and external EU migration policy, including the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, the Mechanism will support the development and reinforcement of strong, balanced, comprehensive and mutually beneficial partnerships and programs with relevant countries of origin, transit and destination of migrants and forcibly displaced people. title.narrative: Activity under preparation MAV+ Phase 2 for Nigeria

description.narrative:
The overall objective is to strengthen Nigeria's health security architecture, pharmaceutical systems and public health capacity, contributing to stronger, more resilient health systems and improved health outcomes. This objective pursues SDG 3.8 and promotes ultimately universal health coverage (UHC).

The Nigeria component will contribute to the Specific Objective 1 of the overall Action:

Specific Objective 1 (5M): aims to reinforce health sector resilience and African strategic autonomy by focusing on under-served segments of the pharmaceutical value chain.

Country level: through a Global Gateway 360° approach, it will focus on building stronger public and private ecosystems, with special attention to supporting innovative financial solutions in Nigeria.

The EU AU Health Partnership Team Europe Initiative (TEI) includes five TEI Hubs: the Hub on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies (MAV+), the Hub on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, the Hub on Health Security using a One Health approach, the Hub on Digital Health and the Hub on Support to Public Health Institutes in SSA
